/** Test if all characters in the string are in the Basic Latin (aka ASCII)
   * character set - that they have UTF-16 values equal to or below 0x7f.
   * This check can find which identifiers with Unicode characters need to be
   * escaped in order to allow resulting files to be processed by non-Unicode
   * aware UNIX tools and editors.
   * *
   * See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_characters_in_Unicode
   * for more on Basic Latin.
   *
   * @param s The string to be checked for ASCII-goodness.
   *
   * @return True if all characters in the string are in Basic Latin set.
   */
Method code:
2449 |   static boolean isLatin(String s) {
2450 |     int len = s.length();
2451 |     for (int index = 0; index < len; index++) {
2452 |       char c = s.charAt(index);
2453 |       if (c > LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN) {
2454 |         return false;
2455 |       }
2456 |     }
2457 |     return true;
2458 |   }

===== M0018 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Denormalize.maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Denormalize.java
Original range: 65-127
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse VARs and EXPR_RESULT node into FOR loop initializers where
   * possible.
   */
Method code:
65 |   private void maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node n, Node parent) {
66 |     // Only SCRIPT, BLOCK, and LABELs can have FORs that can be collapsed into.
67 |     // LABELs are not supported here.
68 |     if (parent == null || !NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {
69 |       return;
70 |     }
71 | 
72 |     // Is the current node something that can be in a for loop initializer?
73 |     if (!n.isExprResult() && !n.isVar()) {
74 |       return;
75 |     }
76 | 
77 |     // Is the next statement a valid FOR?
78 |     Node nextSibling = n.getNext();
79 |     if (nextSibling == null) {
80 |       return;
81 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isForIn(nextSibling)) {
82 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
83 |       Node forVar = forNode.getFirstChild();
84 |       if (forVar.isName()
85 |           && n.isVar() && n.hasOneChild()) {
86 |         Node name = n.getFirstChild();
87 |         if (!name.hasChildren()
88 |             && forVar.getString().equals(name.getString())) {
89 |           // OK, the names match, and the var declaration does not have an
90 |           // initializer. Move it into the loop.
91 |           parent.removeChild(n);
92 |           forNode.replaceChild(forVar, n);
93 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
94 |         }
95 |       }
96 |     } else if (nextSibling.isFor()
97 |         && nextSibling.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
98 | 
99 |       // Does the current node contain an in operator?  If so, embedding
100 |       // the expression in a for loop can cause some JavaScript parsers (such
101 |       // as the PlayStation 3's browser based on Access's NetFront
102 |       // browser) to fail to parse the code.
103 |       // See bug 1778863 for details.
104 |       if (NodeUtil.containsType(n, Token.IN)) {
105 |         return;
106 |       }
107 | 
108 |       // Move the current node into the FOR loop initializer.
109 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
110 |       Node oldInitializer = forNode.getFirstChild();
111 |       parent.removeChild(n);
112 | 
113 |       Node newInitializer;
114 |       if (n.isVar()) {
115 |         newInitializer = n;
116 |       } else {
117 |         // Extract the expression from EXPR_RESULT node.
118 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
119 |         newInitializer = n.getFirstChild();
120 |         n.removeChild(newInitializer);
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       forNode.replaceChild(oldInitializer, newInitializer);
124 | 
125 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
126 |     }
127 |   }

Original range: 910-931
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines if the subtree might throw an exception.
   */
Method code:
910 |   public static boolean mayThrowException(Node n) {
911 |     switch (n.getType()) {
912 |       case Token.CALL:
913 |       case Token.GETPROP:
914 |       case Token.GETELEM:
915 |       case Token.THROW:
916 |       case Token.NEW:
917 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
918 |       case Token.INC:
919 |       case Token.DEC:
920 |       case Token.INSTANCEOF:
921 |         return true;
922 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
923 |         return false;
924 |     }
925 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
926 |       if (!ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(c) && mayThrowException(c)) {
927 |         return true;
928 |       }
929 |     }
930 |     return false;
931 |   }

===== M0022 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.add(Node,Context)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 103-756
Documentation:

Method code:
103 |   void add(Node n, Context context) {
104 |     if (!cc.continueProcessing()) {
105 |       return;
106 |     }
107 | 
108 |     int type = n.getType();
109 |     String opstr = NodeUtil.opToStr(type);
110 |     int childCount = n.getChildCount();
111 |     Node first = n.getFirstChild();
112 |     Node last = n.getLastChild();
113 | 
114 |     // Handle all binary operators
115 |     if (opstr != null && first != last) {
116 |       Preconditions.checkState(
117 |           childCount == 2,
118 |           "Bad binary operator \"%s\": expected 2 arguments but got %s",
119 |           opstr, childCount);
120 |       int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
121 | 
122 |       // For right-hand-side of operations, only pass context if it's
123 |       // the IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE one.
124 |       Context rhsContext = getContextForNoInOperator(context);
125 | 
126 |       // Handle associativity.
127 |       // e.g. if the parse tree is a * (b * c),
128 |       // we can simply generate a * b * c.
129 |       if (last.getType() == type &&
130 |           NodeUtil.isAssociative(type)) {
131 |         addExpr(first, p, context);
132 |         cc.addOp(opstr, true);
133 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
134 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(last)) {
135 |         // Assignments are the only right-associative binary operators
136 |         addExpr(first, p, context);
137 |         cc.addOp(opstr, true);
138 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
139 |       } else {
140 |         unrollBinaryOperator(n, type, opstr, context, rhsContext, p, p + 1);
141 |       }
142 |       return;
143 |     }
144 | 
145 |     cc.startSourceMapping(n);
146 | 
147 |     switch (type) {
148 |       case Token.TRY: {
149 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.getNext().isBlock() &&
150 |                 !first.getNext().hasMoreThanOneChild());
151 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount >= 2 && childCount <= 3);
152 | 
153 |         add("try");
154 |         add(first, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
155 | 
156 |         // second child contains the catch block, or nothing if there
157 |         // isn't a catch block
158 |         Node catchblock = first.getNext().getFirstChild();
159 |         if (catchblock != null) {
160 |           add(catchblock);
161 |         }
162 | 
163 |         if (childCount == 3) {
164 |           add("finally");
165 |           add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
166 |         }
167 |         break;
168 |       }
169 | 
170 |       case Token.CATCH:
171 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
172 |         add("catch(");
173 |         add(first);
174 |         add(")");
175 |         add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
176 |         break;
177 | 
178 |       case Token.THROW:
179 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
180 |         add("throw");
181 |         add(first);
182 | 
183 |         // Must have a ';' after a throw statement, otherwise safari can't
184 |         // parse this.
185 |         cc.endStatement(true);
186 |         break;
187 | 
188 |       case Token.RETURN:
189 |         add("return");
190 |         if (childCount == 1) {
191 |           add(first);
192 |         } else {
193 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
194 |         }
195 |         cc.endStatement();
196 |         break;
197 | 
198 |       case Token.VAR:
199 |         if (first != null) {
200 |           add("var ");
201 |           addList(first, false, getContextForNoInOperator(context));
202 |         }
203 |         break;
204 | 
205 |       case Token.LABEL_NAME:
206 |         Preconditions.checkState(!n.getString().isEmpty());
207 |         addIdentifier(n.getString());
208 |         break;
209 | 
210 |       case Token.NAME:
211 |         if (first == null || first.isEmpty()) {
212 |           addIdentifier(n.getString());
213 |         } else {
214 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
215 |           addIdentifier(n.getString());
216 |           cc.addOp("=", true);
217 |           if (first.isComma()) {
218 |             addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(Token.ASSIGN), Context.OTHER);
219 |           } else {
220 |             // Add expression, consider nearby code at lowest level of
221 |             // precedence.
222 |             addExpr(first, 0, getContextForNoInOperator(context));
223 |           }
224 |         }
225 |         break;
226 | 
227 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
228 |         add("[");
229 |         addArrayList(first);
230 |         add("]");
231 |         break;
232 | 
233 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
234 |         add("(");
235 |         addList(first);
236 |         add(")");
237 |         break;
238 | 
239 |       case Token.COMMA:
240 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
241 |         unrollBinaryOperator(n, Token.COMMA, ",", context, Context.OTHER, 0, 0);
242 |         break;
243 | 
244 |       case Token.NUMBER:
245 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
246 |         cc.addNumber(n.getDouble());
247 |         break;
248 | 
249 |       case Token.TYPEOF:
250 |       case Token.VOID:
251 |       case Token.NOT:
252 |       case Token.BITNOT:
253 |       case Token.POS: {
254 |         // All of these unary operators are right-associative
255 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
256 |         cc.addOp(NodeUtil.opToStrNoFail(type), false);
257 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), Context.OTHER);
258 |         break;
259 |       }
260 | 
261 |       case Token.NEG: {
262 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
263 | 
264 |         // It's important to our sanity checker that the code
265 |         // we print produces the same AST as the code we parse back.
266 |         // NEG is a weird case because Rhino parses "- -2" as "2".
267 |         if (n.getFirstChild().isNumber()) {
268 |           cc.addNumber(-n.getFirstChild().getDouble());
269 |         } else {
270 |           cc.addOp(NodeUtil.opToStrNoFail(type), false);
271 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), Context.OTHER);
272 |         }
273 | 
274 |         break;
275 |       }
276 | 
277 |       case Token.HOOK: {
278 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
279 |         int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
280 |         addExpr(first, p + 1, context);
281 |         cc.addOp("?", true);
282 |         addExpr(first.getNext(), 1, Context.OTHER);
283 |         cc.addOp(":", true);
284 |         addExpr(last, 1, Context.OTHER);
285 |         break;
286 |       }
287 | 
288 |       case Token.REGEXP:
289 |         if (!first.isString() ||
290 |             !last.isString()) {
291 |           throw new Error("Expected children to be strings");
292 |         }
293 | 
294 |         String regexp = regexpEscape(first.getString(), outputCharsetEncoder);
295 | 
296 |         // I only use one .add because whitespace matters
297 |         if (childCount == 2) {
298 |           add(regexp + last.getString());
299 |         } else {
300 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
301 |           add(regexp);
302 |         }
303 |         break;
304 | 
305 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
306 |         if (n.getClass() != Node.class) {
307 |           throw new Error("Unexpected Node subclass.");
308 |         }
309 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
310 |         boolean funcNeedsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
311 |         if (funcNeedsParens) {
312 |           add("(");
313 |         }
314 | 
315 |         add("function");
316 |         add(first);
317 | 
318 |         add(first.getNext());
319 |         add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
320 |         cc.endFunction(context == Context.STATEMENT);
321 | 
322 |         if (funcNeedsParens) {
323 |           add(")");
324 |         }
325 |         break;
326 | 
327 |       case Token.GETTER_DEF:
328 |       case Token.SETTER_DEF:
329 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getParent().isObjectLit());
330 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
331 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.isFunction());
332 | 
333 |         // Get methods are unnamed
334 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.getFirstChild().getString().isEmpty());
335 |         if (type == Token.GETTER_DEF) {
336 |           // Get methods have no parameters.
337 |           Preconditions.checkState(!first.getChildAtIndex(1).hasChildren());
338 |           add("get ");
339 |         } else {
340 |           // Set methods have one parameter.
341 |           Preconditions.checkState(first.getChildAtIndex(1).hasOneChild());
342 |           add("set ");
343 |         }
344 | 
345 |         // The name is on the GET or SET node.
346 |         String name = n.getString();
347 |         Node fn = first;
348 |         Node parameters = fn.getChildAtIndex(1);
349 |         Node body = fn.getLastChild();
350 | 
351 |         // Add the property name.
352 |         if (!n.isQuotedString() &&
353 |             TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(name) &&
354 |             // do not encode literally any non-literal characters that were
355 |             // Unicode escaped.
356 |             NodeUtil.isLatin(name)) {
357 |           add(name);
358 |         } else {
359 |           // Determine if the string is a simple number.
360 |           double d = getSimpleNumber(name);
361 |           if (!Double.isNaN(d)) {
362 |             cc.addNumber(d);
363 |           } else {
364 |             addJsString(n);
365 |           }
366 |         }
367 | 
368 |         add(parameters);
369 |         add(body, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
370 |         break;
371 | 
372 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
373 |       case Token.BLOCK: {
374 |         if (n.getClass() != Node.class) {
375 |           throw new Error("Unexpected Node subclass.");
376 |         }
377 |         boolean preserveBlock = context == Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK;
378 |         if (preserveBlock) {
379 |           cc.beginBlock();
380 |         }
381 | 
382 |         boolean preferLineBreaks =
383 |             type == Token.SCRIPT ||
384 |             (type == Token.BLOCK &&
385 |                 !preserveBlock &&
386 |                 n.getParent() != null &&
387 |                 n.getParent().isScript());
388 |         for (Node c = first; c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
389 |           add(c, Context.STATEMENT);
390 | 
391 |           // VAR doesn't include ';' since it gets used in expressions
392 |           if (c.isVar()) {
393 |             cc.endStatement();
394 |           }
395 | 
396 |           if (c.isFunction()) {
397 |             cc.maybeLineBreak();
398 |           }
399 | 
400 |           // Prefer to break lines in between top-level statements
401 |           // because top-level statements are more homogeneous.
402 |           if (preferLineBreaks) {
403 |             cc.notePreferredLineBreak();
404 |           }
405 |         }
406 |         if (preserveBlock) {
407 |           cc.endBlock(cc.breakAfterBlockFor(n, context == Context.STATEMENT));
408 |         }
409 |         break;
410 |       }
411 | 
412 |       case Token.FOR:
413 |         if (childCount == 4) {
414 |           add("for(");
415 |           if (first.isVar()) {
416 |             add(first, Context.IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE);
417 |           } else {
418 |             addExpr(first, 0, Context.IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE);
419 |           }
420 |           add(";");
421 |           add(first.getNext());
422 |           add(";");
423 |           add(first.getNext().getNext());
424 |           add(")");
425 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
426 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
427 |         } else {
428 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
429 |           add("for(");
430 |           add(first);
431 |           add("in");
432 |           add(first.getNext());
433 |           add(")");
434 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
435 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
436 |         }
437 |         break;
438 | 
439 |       case Token.DO:
440 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
441 |         add("do");
442 |         addNonEmptyStatement(first, Context.OTHER, false);
443 |         add("while(");
444 |         add(last);
445 |         add(")");
446 |         cc.endStatement();
447 |         break;
448 | 
449 |       case Token.WHILE:
450 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
451 |         add("while(");
452 |         add(first);
453 |         add(")");
454 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
455 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
456 |         break;
457 | 
458 |       case Token.EMPTY:
459 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
460 |         break;
461 | 
462 |       case Token.GETPROP: {
463 |         Preconditions.checkState(
464 |             childCount == 2,
465 |             "Bad GETPROP: expected 2 children, but got %s", childCount);
466 |         Preconditions.checkState(
467 |             last.isString(),
468 |             "Bad GETPROP: RHS should be STRING");
469 |         boolean needsParens = (first.isNumber());
470 |         if (needsParens) {
471 |           add("(");
472 |         }
473 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
474 |         if (needsParens) {
475 |           add(")");
476 |         }
477 |         add(".");
478 |         addIdentifier(last.getString());
479 |         break;
480 |       }
481 | 
482 |       case Token.GETELEM:
483 |         Preconditions.checkState(
484 |             childCount == 2,
485 |             "Bad GETELEM: expected 2 children but got %s", childCount);
486 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
487 |         add("[");
488 |         add(first.getNext());
489 |         add("]");
490 |         break;
491 | 
492 |       case Token.WITH:
493 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
494 |         add("with(");
495 |         add(first);
496 |         add(")");
497 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
498 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
499 |         break;
500 | 
501 |       case Token.INC:
502 |       case Token.DEC: {
503 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
504 |         String o = type == Token.INC ? "++" : "--";
505 |         int postProp = n.getIntProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP);
506 |         // A non-zero post-prop value indicates a post inc/dec, default of zero
507 |         // is a pre-inc/dec.
508 |         if (postProp != 0) {
509 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
510 |           cc.addOp(o, false);
511 |         } else {
512 |           cc.addOp(o, false);
513 |           add(first);
514 |         }
515 |         break;
516 |       }
517 | 
518 |       case Token.CALL:
519 |         // We have two special cases here:
520 |         // 1) If the left hand side of the call is a direct reference to eval,
521 |         // then it must have a DIRECT_EVAL annotation. If it does not, then
522 |         // that means it was originally an indirect call to eval, and that
523 |         // indirectness must be preserved.
524 |         // 2) If the left hand side of the call is a property reference,
525 |         // then the call must not a FREE_CALL annotation. If it does, then
526 |         // that means it was originally an call without an explicit this and
527 |         // that must be preserved.
528 |         if (isIndirectEval(first)
529 |             || n.getBooleanProp(Node.FREE_CALL) && NodeUtil.isGet(first)) {
530 |           add("(0,");
531 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(Token.COMMA), Context.OTHER);
532 |           add(")");
533 |         } else {
534 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
535 |         }
536 |         add("(");
537 |         addList(first.getNext());
538 |         add(")");
539 |         break;
540 | 
541 |       case Token.IF:
542 |         boolean hasElse = childCount == 3;
543 |         boolean ambiguousElseClause =
544 |             context == Context.BEFORE_DANGLING_ELSE && !hasElse;
545 |         if (ambiguousElseClause) {
546 |           cc.beginBlock();
547 |         }
548 | 
549 |         add("if(");
550 |         add(first);
551 |         add(")");
552 | 
553 |         if (hasElse) {
554 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
555 |               first.getNext(), Context.BEFORE_DANGLING_ELSE, false);
556 |           add("else");
557 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
558 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
559 |         } else {
560 |           addNonEmptyStatement(first.getNext(), Context.OTHER, false);
561 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
562 |         }
563 | 
564 |         if (ambiguousElseClause) {
565 |           cc.endBlock();
566 |         }
567 |         break;
568 | 
569 |       case Token.NULL:
570 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
571 |         cc.addConstant("null");
572 |         break;
573 | 
574 |       case Token.THIS:
575 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
576 |         add("this");
577 |         break;
578 | 
579 |       case Token.FALSE:
580 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
581 |         cc.addConstant("false");
582 |         break;
583 | 
584 |       case Token.TRUE:
585 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
586 |         cc.addConstant("true");
587 |         break;
588 | 
589 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
590 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount <= 1);
591 |         add("continue");
592 |         if (childCount == 1) {
593 |           if (!first.isLabelName()) {
594 |             throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
595 |           }
596 |           add(" ");
597 |           add(first);
598 |         }
599 |         cc.endStatement();
600 |         break;
601 | 
602 |       case Token.DEBUGGER:
603 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
604 |         add("debugger");
605 |         cc.endStatement();
606 |         break;
607 | 
608 |       case Token.BREAK:
609 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount <= 1);
610 |         add("break");
611 |         if (childCount == 1) {
612 |           if (!first.isLabelName()) {
613 |             throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
614 |           }
615 |           add(" ");
616 |           add(first);
617 |         }
618 |         cc.endStatement();
619 |         break;
620 | 
621 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
622 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
623 |         add(first, Context.START_OF_EXPR);
624 |         cc.endStatement();
625 |         break;
626 | 
627 |       case Token.NEW:
628 |         add("new ");
629 |         int precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
630 | 
631 |         // If the first child contains a CALL, then claim higher precedence
632 |         // to force parentheses. Otherwise, when parsed, NEW will bind to the
633 |         // first viable parentheses (don't traverse into functions).
634 |         if (NodeUtil.containsType(
635 |             first, Token.CALL, NodeUtil.MATCH_NOT_FUNCTION)) {
636 |           precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType()) + 1;
637 |         }
638 |         addExpr(first, precedence, Context.OTHER);
639 | 
640 |         // '()' is optional when no arguments are present
641 |         Node next = first.getNext();
642 |         if (next != null) {
643 |           add("(");
644 |           addList(next);
645 |           add(")");
646 |         }
647 |         break;
648 | 
649 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
650 |         Preconditions.checkState(
651 |             childCount == 1, "Object lit key must have 1 child");
652 |         addJsString(n);
653 |         break;
654 | 
655 |       case Token.STRING:
656 |         Preconditions.checkState(
657 |             childCount == 0, "A string may not have children");
658 |         addJsString(n);
659 |         break;
660 | 
661 |       case Token.DELPROP:
662 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
663 |         add("delete ");
664 |         add(first);
665 |         break;
666 | 
667 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT: {
668 |         boolean needsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
669 |         if (needsParens) {
670 |           add("(");
671 |         }
672 |         add("{");
673 |         for (Node c = first; c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
674 |           if (c != first) {
675 |             cc.listSeparator();
676 |           }
677 | 
678 |           if (c.isGetterDef() || c.isSetterDef()) {
679 |             add(c);
680 |           } else {
681 |             Preconditions.checkState(c.isStringKey());
682 |             String key = c.getString();
683 |             // Object literal property names don't have to be quoted if they
684 |             // are not JavaScript keywords
685 |             if (!c.isQuotedString() &&
686 |                 !TokenStream.isKeyword(key) &&
687 |                 TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(key) &&
688 |                 // do not encode literally any non-literal characters that
689 |                 // were Unicode escaped.
690 |                 NodeUtil.isLatin(key)) {
691 |               add(key);
692 |             } else {
693 |               // Determine if the string is a simple number.
694 |               double d = getSimpleNumber(key);
695 |               if (!Double.isNaN(d)) {
696 |                 cc.addNumber(d);
697 |               } else {
698 |                 addExpr(c, 1, Context.OTHER);
699 |               }
700 |             }
701 |             add(":");
702 |             addExpr(c.getFirstChild(), 1, Context.OTHER);
703 |           }
704 |         }
705 |         add("}");
706 |         if (needsParens) {
707 |           add(")");
708 |         }
709 |         break;
710 |       }
711 | 
712 |       case Token.SWITCH:
713 |         add("switch(");
714 |         add(first);
715 |         add(")");
716 |         cc.beginBlock();
717 |         addAllSiblings(first.getNext());
718 |         cc.endBlock(context == Context.STATEMENT);
719 |         break;
720 | 
721 |       case Token.CASE:
722 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
723 |         add("case ");
724 |         add(first);
725 |         addCaseBody(last);
726 |         break;
727 | 
728 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
729 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
730 |         add("default");
731 |         addCaseBody(first);
732 |         break;
733 | 
734 |       case Token.LABEL:
735 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
736 |         if (!first.isLabelName()) {
737 |           throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
738 |         }
739 |         add(first);
740 |         add(":");
741 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
742 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), true);
743 |         break;
744 | 
745 |       case Token.CAST:
746 |         add("(");
747 |         add(first);
748 |         add(")");
749 |         break;
750 | 
751 |       default:
752 |         throw new Error("Unknown type " + type + "\n" + n.toStringTree());
753 |     }
754 | 
755 |     cc.endSourceMapping(n);
756 |   }

423 |     @Override
424 |     public Bind describeFunctionBind(Node n, boolean useTypeInfo) {
425 |       if (!n.isCall()) {
426 |         return null;
427 |       }
428 | 
429 |       Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
430 |       String name = callTarget.getQualifiedName();
431 |       if (name != null) {
432 |         if (name.equals("Function.prototype.bind.call")) {
433 |           // goog.bind(fn, self, args...);
434 |           Node fn = callTarget.getNext();
435 |           if (fn == null) {
436 |             return null;
437 |           }
438 |           Node thisValue = safeNext(fn);
439 |           Node parameters = safeNext(thisValue);
440 |           return new Bind(fn, thisValue, parameters);
441 |         }
442 |       }
443 |

445 |           && callTarget.getLastChild().getString().equals("bind")) {
446 |         Node maybeFn = callTarget.getFirstChild();
447 |         JSType maybeFnType = maybeFn.getJSType();
448 |         FunctionType fnType = null;
449 |         if (useTypeInfo && maybeFnType != null) {
450 |           fnType = maybeFnType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined()
451 |               .toMaybeFunctionType();
452 |         }
453 | 
454 |         if (fnType != null || maybeFn.isFunction()) {
455 |           // (function(){}).bind(self, args...);
456 |           Node thisValue = callTarget.getNext();
457 |           Node parameters = safeNext(thisValue);
458 |           return new Bind(maybeFn, thisValue, parameters);
459 |         }
460 |       }
461 |

463 |     }

===== M0032 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.assignNames(SortedSet<Assignment>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 443-513
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines which new names to substitute for the original names.
   */
Method code:
443 |   private void assignNames(SortedSet<Assignment> varsToRename) {
444 |     NameGenerator globalNameGenerator =
445 |         new NameGenerator(reservedNames, prefix, reservedCharacters);
446 | 
447 |     // Local variables never need a prefix.
448 |     NameGenerator localNameGenerator =
449 |         prefix.isEmpty() ? globalNameGenerator : new NameGenerator(
450 |             reservedNames, "", reservedCharacters);
451 | 
452 |     // Generated names and the assignments for non-local vars.
453 |     List<Assignment> pendingAssignments = new ArrayList<Assignment>();
454 |     List<String> generatedNamesForAssignments = new ArrayList<String>();
455 | 
456 |     for (Assignment a : varsToRename) {
457 |       if (a.newName != null) {
458 |         continue;
459 |       }
460 | 
461 |       if (externNames.contains(a.oldName)) {
462 |         continue;
463 |       }
464 | 
465 |       String newName;
466 |       if (a.oldName.startsWith(LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX)) {
467 |         // For local variable, we make the assignment right away.
468 |         newName = localNameGenerator.generateNextName();
469 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, newName);
470 |       } else {
471 |         // For non-local variable, delay finalizing the name assignment
472 |         // until we know how many new names we'll have of length 2, 3, etc.
473 |         newName = globalNameGenerator.generateNextName();
474 |         pendingAssignments.add(a);
475 |         generatedNamesForAssignments.add(newName);
476 |       }
477 |       reservedNames.add(newName);
478 |     }
479 | 
480 |     // Now that we have a list of generated names, and a list of variable
481 |     // Assignment objects, we assign the generated names to the vars as
482 |     // follows:
483 |     // 1) The most frequent vars get the shorter names.
484 |     // 2) If N number of vars are going to be assigned names of the same
485 |     //    length, we assign the N names based on the order at which the vars
486 |     //    first appear in the source. This makes the output somewhat less
487 |     //    random, because symbols declared close together are assigned names
488 |     //    that are quite similar. With this heuristic, the output is more
489 |     //    compressible.
490 |     //    For instance, the output may look like:
491 |     //    var da = "..", ea = "..";
492 |     //    function fa() { .. } function ga() { .. }
493 | 
494 |     int numPendingAssignments = generatedNamesForAssignments.size();
495 |     for (int i = 0; i < numPendingAssignments;) {
496 |       SortedSet<Assignment> varsByOrderOfOccurrence =
497 |           new TreeSet<Assignment>(ORDER_OF_OCCURRENCE_COMPARATOR);
498 | 
499 |       // Add k number of Assignment to the set, where k is the number of
500 |       // generated names of the same length.
501 |       int len = generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i).length();
502 |       for (int j = i; j < numPendingAssignments
503 |           && generatedNamesForAssignments.get(j).length() == len; j++) {
504 |         varsByOrderOfOccurrence.add(pendingAssignments.get(j));
505 |       }
506 | 
507 |       // Now, make the assignments
508 |       for (Assignment a : varsByOrderOfOccurrence) {
509 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i));
510 |         ++i;
511 |       }
512 |     }
513 |   }

/**
     * Bring the initializers out of FOR loops.  These need to be placed
     * before any associated LABEL nodes. This needs to be done from the top
     * level label first so this is called as a pre-order callback (from
     * shouldTraverse).
     *
     * @param n The node to inspect.
     * @param before The node to insert the initializer before.
     * @param beforeParent The parent of the node before which the initializer
     *     will be inserted.
     */
Method code:
567 |     private void extractForInitializer(
568 |         Node n, Node before, Node beforeParent) {
569 | 
570 |       for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
571 |         next = c.getNext();
572 |         Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
573 |         Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
574 |         switch (c.getType()) {
575 |           case Token.LABEL:
576 |             extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
577 |             break;
578 |           case Token.FOR:
579 |             if (NodeUtil.isForIn(c)) {
580 |               Node first = c.getFirstChild();
581 |               if (first.isVar()) {
582 |                 // Transform:
583 |                 //    for (var a = 1 in b) {}
584 |                 // to:
585 |                 //    var a = 1; for (a in b) {};
586 |                 Node newStatement = first;
587 |                 // Clone just the node, to remove any initialization.
588 |                 Node name = newStatement.getFirstChild().cloneNode();
589 |                 first.getParent().replaceChild(first, name);
590 |                 insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
591 |                 reportCodeChange("FOR-IN var declaration");
592 |               }
593 |             } else if (!c.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
594 |               Node init = c.getFirstChild();
595 |               Node empty = IR.empty();
596 |               empty.copyInformationFrom(c);
597 |               c.replaceChild(init, empty);
598 | 
599 |               Node newStatement;
600 |               // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
601 |               // but are handled differently.
602 |               if (init.isVar()) {
603 |                 newStatement = init;
604 |               } else {
605 |                 newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
606 |               }
607 | 
608 |               insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
609 |               reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
610 |             }
611 |             break;
612 |         }
613 |       }
614 |     }

===== M0066 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node,ControlFlowAnalysis)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 692-789
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
692 |   private static Node computeFollowNode(
693 |       Node fromNode, Node node, ControlFlowAnalysis cfa) {
694 |     /*
695 |      * This is the case where:
696 |      *
697 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
698 |      * the script.
699 |      *
700 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
701 |      * the caller of the function.
702 |      *
703 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
704 |      * back to the caller of the function.
705 |      *
706 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
707 |      * asked to traverse.
708 |      *
709 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
710 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
711 |      */
712 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
713 |     if (parent == null || parent.isFunction() ||
714 |         (cfa != null && node == cfa.root)) {
715 |       return null;
716 |     }
717 | 
718 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
719 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
720 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
721 |       case Token.IF:
722 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
723 |       case Token.CASE:
724 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
725 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
726 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
727 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
728 |           if (parent.getNext().isCase()) {
729 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
730 |           } else if (parent.getNext().isDefaultCase()) {
731 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
732 |           } else {
733 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
734 |           }
735 |         } else {
736 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
737 |         }
738 |         break;
739 |       case Token.FOR:
740 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
741 |           return parent;
742 |         } else {
743 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
744 |         }
745 |       case Token.WHILE:
746 |       case Token.DO:
747 |         return parent;
748 |       case Token.TRY:
749 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
750 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
751 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
752 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
753 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
754 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
755 |           }
756 |         // CATCH block.
757 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
758 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
759 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
760 |           } else {
761 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
762 |           }
763 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
764 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
765 |           if (cfa != null) {
766 |             for (Node finallyNode : cfa.finallyMap.get(parent)) {
767 |               cfa.createEdge(fromNode, Branch.ON_EX, finallyNode);
768 |             }
769 |           }
770 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
771 |         }
772 |     }
773 | 
774 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
775 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
776 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
777 | 
778 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
779 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.isFunction()) {
780 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
781 |     }
782 | 
783 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
784 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
785 |     } else {
786 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transferred up the AST.
787 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
788 |     }
789 |   }

131 |       if (finalValue != info.initialValue) {
132 |         info.initialValueParent.replaceChild(
133 |             info.initialValue, finalValue.cloneTree());
134 |         compiler.addToDebugLog("Overriding @define variable " + defineName);
135 |         changed = changed ||
136 |             finalValue.getType() != info.initialValue.getType() ||
137 |             !finalValue.isEquivalentTo(info.initialValue);
138 |       }
139 |     }
140 | 
141 |     if (changed) {
142 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
143 |     }
144 | 
145 |     Set<String> unusedReplacements = dominantReplacements.keySet();
146 |     unusedReplacements.removeAll(allDefines.keySet());
147 |     unusedReplacements.removeAll(KNOWN_DEFINES);
148 |     for (String unknownDefine : unusedReplacements) {
149 |       compiler.report(JSError.make(UNKNOWN_DEFINE_WARNING, unknownDefine));
150 |     }
151 |   }

132 |     // MakeDeclaredNamesUnique in order for catch block exception names to be

138 |     // cases where a function scope variable conflict with a exception name:

144 |     // TODO(johnlenz): Introduce a separate scope for catch nodes.
145 |     removeDuplicateDeclarations(externs, root);

112 |   @Override
113 |   public void exitScope(NodeTraversal traversal) {
114 |     Preconditions.checkNotNull(traversal);
115 | 
116 |     // This is the case when we are exiting the global scope where we had never
117 |     // collected argument access list. Since we do not perform this optimization
118 |     // for the global scope, we will skip this exit point.
119 |     if (currentArgumentsAccess == null) {
120 |       return;
121 |     }
122 | 
123 |     // Attempt to replace the argument access and if the AST has been change,
124 |     // report back to the compiler.
125 |     if (tryReplaceArguments(traversal.getScope())) {
126 |       traversal.getCompiler().reportCodeChange();
127 |     }
128 | 
129 |     // After the attempt to replace the arguments. The currentArgumentsAccess
130 |     // is stale and as we exit the Scope, no longer holds all the access to the
131 |     // current scope anymore. We'll pop the access list from the outer scope
132 |     // and set it as currentArgumentsAcess if the outer scope is not the global
133 |     // scope.
134 |     if (!argumentsAccessStack.isEmpty()) {
135 |       currentArgumentsAccess = argumentsAccessStack.pop();
136 |     } else {
137 |       currentArgumentsAccess = null;
138 |     }
139 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.isSubtypeHelper(JSType,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/JSType.java
Original range: 1229-1273
Documentation:
/**
   * A generic implementation meant to be used as a helper for common subtyping
   * cases.
   */
Method code:
1229 |   static boolean isSubtypeHelper(JSType thisType, JSType thatType) {
1230 |     // unknown
1231 |     if (thatType.isUnknownType()) {
1232 |       return true;
1233 |     }
1234 |     // all type
1235 |     if (thatType.isAllType()) {
1236 |       return true;
1237 |     }
1238 |     // equality
1239 |     if (thisType.isEquivalentTo(thatType)) {
1240 |       return true;
1241 |     }
1242 |     // unions
1243 |     if (thatType.isUnionType()) {
1244 |       UnionType union = thatType.toMaybeUnionType();
1245 |       for (JSType element : union.alternates) {
1246 |         if (thisType.isSubtype(element)) {
1247 |           return true;
1248 |         }
1249 |       }
1250 |       return false;
1251 |     }
1252 | 
1253 |     // templatized types.
1254 |     if (thisType.isTemplatizedType()) {
1255 |       return !areIncompatibleArrays(thisType, thatType) &&
1256 |           thisType.toMaybeTemplatizedType().getReferencedType().isSubtype(
1257 |               thatType);
1258 |     }
1259 |     if (thatType.isTemplatizedType()) {
1260 |       if (!isExemptFromTemplateTypeInvariance(thatType) &&
1261 |           !thisType.getTemplateTypeMap().checkEquivalenceHelper(
1262 |               thatType.getTemplateTypeMap(), EquivalenceMethod.IDENTITY)) {
1263 |         return false;
1264 |       }
1265 |     }
1266 | 
1267 |     // proxy types
1268 |     if (thatType instanceof ProxyObjectType) {
1269 |       return thisType.isSubtype(
1270 |           ((ProxyObjectType) thatType).getReferencedTypeInternal());
1271 |     }
1272 |     return false;
1273 |   }

58 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
59 |   final JsDocToken getJsDocToken() {

61 |     stringBufferTop = 0;
62 |     for (;;) {
63 |       // eat white spaces
64 |       for (;;) {
65 |         charno = -1;
66 |         c = getChar();
67 |         if (c == EOF_CHAR) {

71 |         } else if (!isJSSpace(c)) {
72 |           break;
73 |         }
74 |       }
75 |

77 |         // annotation, e.g. @type or @constructor

82 |               addToString(c);
83 |             } else {
84 |               ungetChar(c);

87 |               return JsDocToken.ANNOTATION;
88 |             }
89 |           } while (true);
90 | 
91 |         case '*':
92 |           if (matchChar('/')) {
93 |             return JsDocToken.EOC;
94 |           } else {
95 |             return JsDocToken.STAR;
96 |           }
97 | 
98 |         case ',':
99 |           return JsDocToken.COMMA;
100 | 
101 |         case '>':
102 |           return JsDocToken.GT;
103 | 
104 |         case '(':
105 |           return JsDocToken.LP;
106 | 
107 |         case ')':
108 |           return JsDocToken.RP;
109 | 
110 |         case '{':
111 |           return JsDocToken.LC;
112 | 
113 |         case '}':
114 |           return JsDocToken.RC;
115 | 
116 |         case '[':
117 |           return JsDocToken.LB;
118 | 
119 |         case ']':
120 |           return JsDocToken.RB;
121 | 
122 |         case '?':
123 |           return JsDocToken.QMARK;
124 | 
125 |         case '!':
126 |           return JsDocToken.BANG;
127 | 
128 |         case ':':
129 |           return JsDocToken.COLON;
130 | 
131 |         case '=':
132 |           return JsDocToken.EQUALS;
133 | 
134 |         case '|':
135 |           matchChar('|');
136 |           return JsDocToken.PIPE;
137 | 
138 |         case '.':
139 |           c = getChar();
140 |           if (c == '<') {
141 |             return JsDocToken.LT;
142 |           } else {
143 |             if (c == '.') {
144 |               c = getChar();
145 |               if (c == '.') {

149 |               }

152 |             ungetBuffer[ungetCursor++] = c;
153 |             c = '.';
154 |           }

157 |         default: {
158 |           // recognize a JsDoc string but discard last . if it is followed by
159 |           // a non-JsDoc comment char, e.g. Array.<

184 |                   this.string = getStringFromBuffer();

/**

Method code:
286 |   protected void joinInputs(DiGraphNode<N, Branch> node) {
287 |     FlowState<L> state = node.getAnnotation();

293 |         if (inNodes.size() == 1) {

298 |           for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> currentNode : inNodes) {
299 |             FlowState<L> currentNodeState = currentNode.getAnnotation();
300 |             values.add(currentNodeState.getOut());
301 |           }
302 |           state.setIn(joinOp.apply(values));
303 |         }
304 |       }

307 |       if (inNodes.size() == 1) {
308 |         DiGraphNode<N, Branch> inNode = inNodes.get(0);
309 |         if (inNode == cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
310 |           state.setOut(createEntryLattice());
311 |         } else {
312 |           FlowState<L> inNodeState = inNode.getAnnotation();
313 |           state.setOut(inNodeState.getIn());
314 |         }
315 |       } else if (inNodes.size() > 1) {
316 |         List<L> values = new ArrayList<L>(inNodes.size());
317 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> currentNode : inNodes) {
318 |           FlowState<L> currentNodeState = currentNode.getAnnotation();
319 |           values.add(currentNodeState.getIn());

===== M0162 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.checkForStateChangeHelper(Node,boolean,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 789-934
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if some node in n's subtree changes application state.
   * If {@code checkForNewObjects} is true, we assume that newly created
   * mutable objects (like object literals) change state. Otherwise, we assume
   * that they have no side effects.
   */
Method code:
789 |   private static boolean checkForStateChangeHelper(
790 |       Node n, boolean checkForNewObjects, AbstractCompiler compiler) {
791 |     // Rather than id which ops may have side effects, id the ones
792 |     // that we know to be safe
793 |     switch (n.getType()) {
794 |       // other side-effect free statements and expressions
795 |       case Token.CAST:
796 |       case Token.AND:
797 |       case Token.BLOCK:
798 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
799 |       case Token.HOOK:
800 |       case Token.IF:
801 |       case Token.IN:
802 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
803 |       case Token.NUMBER:
804 |       case Token.OR:
805 |       case Token.THIS:
806 |       case Token.TRUE:
807 |       case Token.FALSE:
808 |       case Token.NULL:
809 |       case Token.STRING:
810 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
811 |       case Token.SWITCH:
812 |       case Token.TRY:
813 |       case Token.EMPTY:
814 |         break;
815 | 
816 |       // Throws are by definition side effects
817 |       case Token.THROW:
818 |         return true;
819 | 
820 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
821 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
822 |           return true;
823 |         }
824 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
825 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
826 |                   c.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
827 |             return true;
828 |           }
829 |         }
830 |         return false;
831 | 
832 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
833 |       case Token.REGEXP:
834 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
835 |           return true;
836 |         }
837 |         break;
838 | 
839 |       case Token.VAR:    // empty var statement (no declaration)
840 |       case Token.NAME:   // variable by itself
841 |         if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
842 |           return true;
843 |         }
844 |         break;
845 | 
846 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
847 |         // Function expressions don't have side-effects, but function
848 |         // declarations change the namespace. Either way, we don't need to
849 |         // check the children, since they aren't executed at declaration time.
850 |         return checkForNewObjects || !isFunctionExpression(n);
851 | 
852 |       case Token.NEW:
853 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
854 |           return true;
855 |         }
856 | 
857 |         if (!constructorCallHasSideEffects(n)) {
858 |           // loop below will see if the constructor parameters have
859 |           // side-effects
860 |           break;
861 |         }
862 |         return true;
863 | 
864 |       case Token.CALL:
865 |         // calls to functions that have no side effects have the no
866 |         // side effect property set.
867 |         if (!functionCallHasSideEffects(n, compiler)) {
868 |           // loop below will see if the function parameters have
869 |           // side-effects
870 |           break;
871 |         }
872 |         return true;
873 | 
874 |       default:
875 |         if (isSimpleOperator(n)) {
876 |           break;
877 |         }
878 | 
879 |         if (isAssignmentOp(n)) {
880 |           Node assignTarget = n.getFirstChild();
881 |           if (assignTarget.isName()) {
882 |             return true;
883 |           }
884 | 
885 |           // Assignments will have side effects if
886 |           // a) The RHS has side effects, or
887 |           // b) The LHS has side effects, or
888 |           // c) A name on the LHS will exist beyond the life of this statement.
889 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
890 |                   n.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler) ||
891 |               checkForStateChangeHelper(
892 |                   n.getLastChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
893 |             return true;
894 |           }
895 | 
896 |           if (isGet(assignTarget)) {
897 |             // If the object being assigned to is a local object, don't
898 |             // consider this a side-effect as it can't be referenced
899 |             // elsewhere.  Don't do this recursively as the property might
900 |             // be an alias of another object, unlike a literal below.
901 |             Node current = assignTarget.getFirstChild();
902 |             if (evaluatesToLocalValue(current)) {
903 |               return false;
904 |             }
905 | 
906 |             // A literal value as defined by "isLiteralValue" is guaranteed
907 |             // not to be an alias, or any components which are aliases of
908 |             // other objects.
909 |             // If the root object is a literal don't consider this a
910 |             // side-effect.
911 |             while (isGet(current)) {
912 |               current = current.getFirstChild();
913 |             }
914 | 
915 |             return !isLiteralValue(current, true);
916 |           } else {
917 |             // TODO(johnlenz): remove this code and make this an exception. This
918 |             // is here only for legacy reasons, the AST is not valid but
919 |             // preserve existing behavior.
920 |             return !isLiteralValue(assignTarget, true);
921 |           }
922 |         }
923 | 
924 |         return true;
925 |     }
926 | 
927 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
928 |       if (checkForStateChangeHelper(c, checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
929 |         return true;
930 |       }
931 |     }
932 | 
933 |     return false;
934 |   }

289 |   private void validateTypeAnnotations(JSDocInfo info, AstNode node) {
290 |     if (info.hasType()) {
291 |       boolean valid = false;
292 |       switch (node.getType()) {
293 |         // Casts are valid
294 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.LP:
295 |           valid = node instanceof ParenthesizedExpression;
296 |           break;
297 |         // Variable declarations are valid
298 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.VAR:
299 |           valid = true;
300 |           break;
301 |         // Function declarations are valid
302 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.FUNCTION:
303 |           FunctionNode fnNode = (FunctionNode)node;
304 |           valid = fnNode.getFunctionType() == FunctionNode.FUNCTION_STATEMENT;
305 |           break;
306 |         // Object literal properties and catch declarations are valid.
307 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.NAME:
308 |           valid = node.getParent() instanceof ObjectProperty
309 |               || node.getParent() instanceof CatchClause
310 |               || node.getParent() instanceof FunctionNode;
311 |           break;
312 |         // Object literal properties are valid
313 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.GET:
314 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.SET:
315 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.NUMBER:
316 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.STRING:
317 |           valid = node.getParent() instanceof ObjectProperty;
318 |           break;
319 | 
320 |         // Property assignments are valid, if at the root of an expression.
321 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.ASSIGN:
322 |           if (node instanceof Assignment) {
323 |             valid = isExprStmt(node.getParent())
324 |                 && isPropAccess(((Assignment)node).getLeft());
325 |           }
326 |           break;
327 | 
328 |         // Property definitions are valid, if at the root of an expression.
329 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.GETPROP:
330 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.GETELEM:
331 |           valid = isExprStmt(node.getParent());
332 |           break;
333 | 
334 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.CALL:
335 |           valid = info.isDefine();
336 |           break;
337 |       }
338 |       if (!valid) {
339 |         errorReporter.warning(MISPLACED_TYPE_ANNOTATION,
340 |             sourceName,
341 |             node.getLineno(), "", 0);
342 |       }
343 |     }
344 |   }

201 |   @Override
202 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
203 |     switch (n.getType()) {
204 |       case Token.CALL:
205 |         boolean isExpr = parent.isExprResult();
206 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
207 |         if (left.isGetProp()) {
208 |           Node name = left.getFirstChild();
209 |           if (name.isName() &&
210 |               GOOG.equals(name.getString())) {
211 |             // For the sake of simplicity, we report code changes
212 |             // when we see a provides/requires, and don't worry about
213 |             // reporting the change when we actually do the replacement.
214 |             String methodName = name.getNext().getString();
215 |             if ("base".equals(methodName)) {
216 |               processBaseClassCall(t, n);
217 |             } else if (!isExpr) {
218 |               // All other methods must be called in an EXPR.
219 |               break;
220 |             } else if ("define".equals(methodName)) {
221 |               processDefineCall(t, n, parent);
222 |             } else if ("require".equals(methodName)) {
223 |               processRequireCall(t, n, parent);
224 |             } else if ("provide".equals(methodName)) {
225 |               processProvideCall(t, n, parent);
226 |             } else if ("exportSymbol".equals(methodName)) {
227 |               Node arg = left.getNext();
228 |               if (arg.isString()) {
229 |                 int dot = arg.getString().indexOf('.');
230 |                 if (dot == -1) {
231 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString());
232 |                 } else {
233 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString().substring(0, dot));
234 |                 }
235 |               }
236 |             } else if ("addDependency".equals(methodName)) {
237 |               CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
238 |               List<String> typeDecls =
239 |                   convention.identifyTypeDeclarationCall(n);
240 |               if (typeDecls != null) {
241 |                 for (String typeDecl : typeDecls) {
242 |                   compiler.getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(typeDecl);
243 |                 }
244 |               }
245 | 
246 |               // We can't modify parent, so just create a node that will
247 |               // get compiled out.
248 |               parent.replaceChild(n, IR.number(0));
249 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
250 |             } else if ("setCssNameMapping".equals(methodName)) {
251 |               processSetCssNameMapping(t, n, parent);
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 |         }
255 |         break;
256 | 
257 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
258 |       case Token.NAME:
259 |         // If this is an assignment to a provided name, remove the provided
260 |         // object.
261 |         handleCandidateProvideDefinition(t, n, parent);
262 |         break;
263 | 
264 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
265 |         handleTypedefDefinition(t, n);
266 |         break;
267 | 
268 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
269 |         // If this is a declaration of a provided named function, this is an
270 |         // error. Hoisted functions will explode if they're provided.
271 |         if (t.inGlobalScope() &&
272 |             !NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
273 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
274 |           ProvidedName pn = providedNames.get(name);
275 |           if (pn != null) {
276 |             compiler.report(t.makeError(n, FUNCTION_NAMESPACE_ERROR, name));
277 |           }

279 |         break;

===== M0191 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.optimizeSubtree(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.java
Original range: 35-82
Documentation:

Method code:
35 |   @Override
36 |   Node optimizeSubtree(Node subtree) {
37 |     if (!subtree.isScript() && !subtree.isBlock()) {
38 |       return subtree;
39 |     }
40 | 
41 |     boolean codeChanged = false;
42 | 
43 |     // Look for variable declarations or simple assignments
44 |     // and start processing there.
45 |     for (Node child = subtree.getFirstChild();
46 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()) {
47 |       if (!child.isVar() && !NodeUtil.isExprAssign(child)) {
48 |         continue;
49 |       }
50 |       if (!isPropertyAssignmentToName(child.getNext())) {
51 |         // Quick check to see if there's anything to collapse.
52 |         continue;
53 |       }
54 | 
55 |       Preconditions.checkState(child.hasOneChild());
56 |       Node name = getName(child);
57 |       if (!name.isName()) {
58 |         // The assignment target is not a simple name.
59 |         continue;
60 |       }
61 |       Node value = getValue(child);
62 |       if (value == null || !isInterestingValue(value)) {
63 |         // No initializer or not an Object or Array literal.
64 |         continue;
65 |       }
66 | 
67 |       Node propertyCandidate;
68 |       while ((propertyCandidate = child.getNext()) != null) {
69 |         // This does not infinitely loop because collectProperty always
70 |         // removes propertyCandidate from its parent when it returns true.
71 |         if (!collectProperty(propertyCandidate, name.getString(), value)) {
72 |           break;
73 |         }
74 |         codeChanged = true;
75 |       }
76 |     }
77 | 
78 |     if (codeChanged) {
79 |       reportCodeChange();
80 |     }
81 |     return subtree;
82 |   }

===== M0204 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.computeEscaped(Scope,Set<Var>,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 548-578
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute set of escaped variables. When a variable is escaped in a
   * dataflow analysis, it can be reference outside of the code that we are
   * analyzing. A variable is escaped if any of the following is true:
   *
   * <p><ol>
   * <li>It is defined as the exception name in CATCH clause so it became a
   * variable local not to our definition of scope.</li>
   * <li>Exported variables as they can be needed after the script terminates.
   * </li>
   * <li>Names of named functions because in JavaScript, <i>function foo(){}</i>
   * does not kill <i>foo</i> in the dataflow.</li>
   */
Method code:
548 |   static void computeEscaped(final Scope jsScope, final Set<Var> escaped,
549 |       AbstractCompiler compiler) {
550 |     // TODO(user): Very good place to store this information somewhere.
551 |     AbstractPostOrderCallback finder = new AbstractPostOrderCallback() {
552 |       @Override
553 |       public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
554 |         if (jsScope == t.getScope() || !n.isName()
555 |             || parent.isFunction()) {
556 |           return;
557 |         }
558 |         String name = n.getString();
559 |         Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
560 |         if (var != null && var.scope == jsScope) {
561 |           escaped.add(jsScope.getVar(name));
562 |         }
563 |       }
564 |     };
565 | 
566 |     NodeTraversal t = new NodeTraversal(compiler, finder);
567 |     t.traverseAtScope(jsScope);
568 | 
569 |     // 1: Remove the exception name in CATCH which technically isn't local to
570 |     //    begin with.
571 |     for (Iterator<Var> i = jsScope.getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
572 |       Var var = i.next();
573 |       if (var.getParentNode().isCatch() ||
574 |           compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.getName())) {
575 |         escaped.add(var);
576 |       }
577 |     }
578 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.tryOptimizeConditionalAfterAssign(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.java
Original range: 550-591
Documentation:
/**
   * Attempt to replace the condition of if or hook immediately that is a
   * reference to a name that is assigned immediately before.
   */
Method code:
550 |   private void tryOptimizeConditionalAfterAssign(Node n) {
551 |     Node next = n.getNext();
552 | 
553 |     // Look for patterns like the following and replace the if-condition with
554 |     // a constant value so it can later be folded:
555 |     //   var a = /a/;
556 |     //   if (a) {foo(a)}
557 |     // or
558 |     //   a = 0;
559 |     //   a ? foo(a) : c;
560 |     // or
561 |     //   a = 0;
562 |     //   a || foo(a);
563 |     // or
564 |     //   a = 0;
565 |     //   a && foo(a)
566 |     //
567 |     // TODO(johnlenz): This would be better handled by control-flow sensitive
568 |     // constant propagation. As the other case that I want to handle is:
569 |     //   i=0; for(;i<0;i++){}
570 |     // as right now nothing facilitates removing a loop like that.
571 |     // This is here simply to remove the cruft left behind goog.userAgent and
572 |     // similar cases.
573 | 
574 |     if (isSimpleAssignment(n) && isConditionalStatement(next)) {
575 |       Node lhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentName(n);
576 | 
577 |       Node condition = getConditionalStatementCondition(next);
578 |       if (lhsAssign.isName() && condition.isName()
579 |           && lhsAssign.getString().equals(condition.getString())) {
580 |         Node rhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentValue(n);
581 |         TernaryValue value = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(rhsAssign);
582 |         if (value != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
583 |           Node replacementConditionNode =
584 |               NodeUtil.booleanNode(value.toBoolean(true));
585 |           condition.getParent().replaceChild(condition,
586 |               replacementConditionNode);
587 |           reportCodeChange();
588 |         }
589 |       }
590 |     }
591 |   }

84 |   private void scanRoot(Node n) {
85 |     if (n.isFunction()) {
86 |       if (inputId == null) {
87 |         inputId = NodeUtil.getInputId(n);
88 |         // TODO(johnlenz): inputId maybe null if the FUNCTION node is detached

111 |

114 |     } else {

/**
   * Returns true if this is an immutable value.
   */
Method code:
490 |   static boolean isImmutableValue(Node n) {
491 |     switch (n.getType()) {
492 |       case Token.STRING:
493 |       case Token.NUMBER:
494 |       case Token.NULL:
495 |       case Token.TRUE:
496 |       case Token.FALSE:
497 |         return true;
498 |       case Token.CAST:
499 |       case Token.NOT:

508 |         return "undefined".equals(name)

510 |             || "NaN".equals(name);
511 |     }
512 | 
513 |     return false;
514 |   }

791 |       // AstNode, so there's nothing that has the actual line number that it
792 |       // appeared on.  We know the paren has to appear on the same line as the
793 |       // function name (or else a semicolon will be inserted.)  If there's no
794 |       // function name, assume the paren was on the same line as the function.
795 |       // TODO(bowdidge): Mark line number of paren correctly.
796 |       Name fnName = functionNode.getFunctionName();
797 |       if (fnName != null) {

799 |       } else {

801 |       }
802 |       int lparenCharno = functionNode.getLp() +
803 |           functionNode.getAbsolutePosition();
804 | 
805 |       lp.setCharno(position2charno(lparenCharno));
806 |       for (AstNode param : functionNode.getParams()) {
807 |         Node paramNode = transformParameter(param);
808 |         // When in ideMode Rhino can generate a param list with only a single
809 |         // ErrorNode. This is transformed into an EMPTY node. Drop this node in
810 |         // ideMode to keep the AST in a valid state.
811 |         if (paramNode.isName()) {
812 |           lp.addChildToBack(paramNode);

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.lookAheadForTypeAnnotation()

Documentation:
/**
   * Look ahead for a type annotation by advancing the character stream.
   * Does not modify the token stream.
   * This is kind of a hack, and is only necessary because we use the token
   * stream to parse types, but need the underlying character stream to get
   * JsDoc descriptions.
   * @return Whether we found a type annotation.
   */
Method code:
2433 |   private boolean lookAheadForTypeAnnotation() {
2434 |     boolean matchedLc = false;
2435 |     int c;
2436 |     while (true) {
2437 |       c = stream.getChar();
2438 |       if (c == ' ') {
2439 |         continue;
2440 |       } else if (c == '{') {
2441 |         matchedLc = true;
2442 |         break;
2443 |       } else {
2444 |         break;
2445 |       }
2446 |     }
2447 |     stream.ungetChar(c);
2448 |     return matchedLc;
2449 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.runInCompilerThread(Callable<T>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java

Method code:
664 |   @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
665 |   <T> T runInCompilerThread(final Callable<T> callable) {
666 |     final boolean dumpTraceReport = options != null && options.tracer.isOn();
667 |     T result = null;
668 |     final Throwable[] exception = new Throwable[1];
669 |     Callable<T> bootCompilerThread = new Callable<T>() {
670 |       @Override
671 |       public T call() {
672 |         try {
673 |           compilerThread = Thread.currentThread();
674 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
675 |             Tracer.initCurrentThreadTrace();
676 |           }
677 |           return callable.call();
678 |         } catch (Throwable e) {
679 |           exception[0] = e;
680 |         } finally {
681 |           compilerThread = null;
682 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
683 |             Tracer.logAndClearCurrentThreadTrace();
684 |             tracker.outputTracerReport(outStream == null ?
685 |                 System.out : outStream);
686 |           }
687 |         }
688 |         return null;
689 |       }
690 |     };
691 | 
692 |     Preconditions.checkState(
693 |         compilerThread == null || compilerThread == Thread.currentThread(),
694 |         "Please do not share the Compiler across threads");
695 | 
696 |     // If the compiler thread is available, use it.
697 |     if (useThreads && compilerThread == null) {
698 |       try {
699 |         result = compilerExecutor.submit(bootCompilerThread).get();
700 |       } catch (InterruptedException e) {
701 |         throw Throwables.propagate(e);
702 |       } catch (ExecutionException e) {
703 |         throw Throwables.propagate(e);
704 |       }
705 |     } else {
706 |       try {
707 |         result = callable.call();
708 |       } catch (Exception e) {
709 |         exception[0] = e;
710 |       }
711 |     }
712 | 
713 |     // Pass on any exception caught by the runnable object.
714 |     if (exception[0] != null) {
715 |       throw new RuntimeException(exception[0]);
716 |     }
717 | 
718 |     return result;
719 |   }

===== M0269 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.checkEquivalenceHelper(JSType,EquivalenceMethod)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/JSType.java
Original range: 563-631
Documentation:
/**
   * An equivalence visitor.
   */
Method code:
563 |   boolean checkEquivalenceHelper(JSType that, EquivalenceMethod eqMethod) {
564 |     if (this == that) {
565 |       return true;
566 |     }
567 | 
568 |     boolean thisUnknown = isUnknownType();
569 |     boolean thatUnknown = that.isUnknownType();
570 |     if (thisUnknown || thatUnknown) {
571 |       if (eqMethod == EquivalenceMethod.INVARIANT) {
572 |         // If we're checking for invariance, the unknown type is invariant
573 |         // with everyone.
574 |         return true;
575 |       } else if (eqMethod == EquivalenceMethod.DATA_FLOW) {
576 |         // If we're checking data flow, then two types are the same if they're
577 |         // both unknown.
578 |         return thisUnknown && thatUnknown;
579 |       } else if (thisUnknown && thatUnknown &&
580 |           (isNominalType() ^ that.isNominalType())) {
581 |         // If they're both unknown, but one is a nominal type and the other
582 |         // is not, then we should fail out immediately. This ensures that
583 |         // we won't unbox the unknowns further down.
584 |         return false;
585 |       }
586 |     }
587 | 
588 |     if (isUnionType() && that.isUnionType()) {
589 |       return toMaybeUnionType().checkUnionEquivalenceHelper(
590 |           that.toMaybeUnionType(), eqMethod);
591 |     }
592 | 
593 |     if (isFunctionType() && that.isFunctionType()) {
594 |       return toMaybeFunctionType().checkFunctionEquivalenceHelper(
595 |           that.toMaybeFunctionType(), eqMethod);
596 |     }
597 | 
598 |     if (isRecordType() && that.isRecordType()) {
599 |       return toMaybeRecordType().checkRecordEquivalenceHelper(
600 |           that.toMaybeRecordType(), eqMethod);
601 |     }
602 | 
603 |     if (!getTemplateTypeMap().checkEquivalenceHelper(
604 |         that.getTemplateTypeMap(), eqMethod)) {
605 |       return false;
606 |     }
607 | 
608 |     if (isNominalType() && that.isNominalType()) {
609 |       return toObjectType().getReferenceName().equals(
610 |           that.toObjectType().getReferenceName());
611 |     }
612 | 
613 |     // Unbox other proxies.
614 |     if (this instanceof ProxyObjectType) {
615 |       return ((ProxyObjectType) this)
616 |           .getReferencedTypeInternal().checkEquivalenceHelper(
617 |               that, eqMethod);
618 |     }
619 | 
620 |     if (that instanceof ProxyObjectType) {
621 |       return checkEquivalenceHelper(
622 |           ((ProxyObjectType) that).getReferencedTypeInternal(),
623 |           eqMethod);
624 |     }
625 | 
626 |     // Relies on the fact that for the base {@link JSType}, only one
627 |     // instance of each sub-type will ever be created in a given registry, so
628 |     // there is no need to verify members. If the object pointers are not
629 |     // identical, then the type member must be different.
630 |     return this == that;
631 |   }

Method code:
136 |     @Override
137 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
138 |       if (n.isVar()) {
139 |         blacklistStubVars(t, n);
140 |       }
141 | 
142 |       // Only care about var nodes
143 |       if (!n.isVar() && !canBeRedeclared(n, t.getScope())) return;
144 | 
145 |       // If we've already looked at this node, skip it
146 |       if (nodesToCollapse.contains(n)) return;
147 | 
148 |       // Adjacent VAR children of an IF node are the if and else parts and can't
149 |       // be collapsed
150 |       if (parent.isIf()) return;
151 | 
152 |       Node varNode = n;
153 | 
154 |       boolean hasVar = n.isVar();
155 | 
156 |       // Find variable declarations that follow this one (if any)
157 |       n = n.getNext();
158 | 
159 |       boolean hasNodesToCollapse = false;
160 | 
161 |       while (n != null &&
162 |           (n.isVar() || canBeRedeclared(n, t.getScope()))) {
163 | 
164 |         if (n.isVar()) {
165 |           blacklistStubVars(t, n);
166 |           hasVar = true;
167 |         }
168 | 
169 |         nodesToCollapse.add(n);
170 |         hasNodesToCollapse = true;
171 | 
172 |         n = n.getNext();
173 |       }
174 | 
175 |       if (hasNodesToCollapse && hasVar) {
176 |         nodesToCollapse.add(varNode);
177 |         collapses.add(new Collapse(varNode, n, parent));
178 |       }
179 |     }

511 |   private void traverseBranch(Node n, Node parent) {
512 |     int type = n.getType();

515 |       sourceName = getSourceName(n);

520 |       return;
521 |     }

525 |     } else {
