/**
   * Performs the line-by-line parsing of the given fileContents. This method
   * strips out JavaScript comments and then uses the abstract parseLine()
   * method to do the line parsing.
   *
   * @param filePath The path to the file being parsed. Used for reporting parse
   *     exceptions.
   * @param fileContents A reader for the contents of the file.
   */
Method code:
119 |   void doParse(String filePath, Reader fileContents) {
120 |     this.filePath = filePath;
121 |     parseSucceeded = true;
122 | 
123 |     BufferedReader lineBuffer = new BufferedReader(fileContents);
124 | 
125 |     // Parse all lines.
126 |     String line = null;
127 |     lineNum = 0;
128 |     boolean inMultilineComment = false;
129 | 
130 |     try {
131 |       while (null != (line = lineBuffer.readLine())) {
132 |         ++lineNum;
133 |         try {
134 |           String revisedLine = line;
135 |           if (inMultilineComment) {
136 |             int endOfComment = revisedLine.indexOf("*/");
137 |             if (endOfComment != -1) {
138 |               revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(endOfComment + 2);
139 |               inMultilineComment = false;
140 |             } else {
141 |               revisedLine = "";
142 |             }
143 |           }
144 | 
145 |           if (!inMultilineComment) {
146 |             while (true) {
147 |               int startOfLineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("//");
148 |               int startOfMultilineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("/*");
149 |               if (startOfLineComment != -1 &&
150 |                   (startOfMultilineComment == -1 ||
151 |                    startOfLineComment < startOfMultilineComment)) {
152 |                 revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(0, startOfLineComment);
153 |                 break;
154 |               } else if (startOfMultilineComment != -1) {
155 |                 int endOfMultilineComment = revisedLine.indexOf("*/",
156 |                     startOfMultilineComment + 2);
157 |                 if (endOfMultilineComment == -1) {
158 |                   revisedLine = revisedLine.substring(
159 |                       0, startOfMultilineComment);
160 |                   inMultilineComment = true;
161 |                   break;
162 |                 } else {
163 |                   revisedLine =
164 |                       revisedLine.substring(0, startOfMultilineComment) +
165 |                       revisedLine.substring(endOfMultilineComment + 2);
166 |                 }
167 |               } else {
168 |                 break;
169 |               }
170 |             }
171 |           }
172 | 
173 |           if (!revisedLine.isEmpty()) {
174 |             // This check for shortcut mode should be redundant, but
175 |             // it's done for safety reasons.
176 |             if (!parseLine(revisedLine) && shortcutMode) {
177 |               break;
178 |             }
179 |           }
180 |         } catch (ParseException e) {
181 |           // Inform the error handler of the exception.
182 |           errorManager.report(
183 |               e.isFatal() ? CheckLevel.ERROR : CheckLevel.WARNING,
184 |               JSError.make(filePath, lineNum, 0 /* char offset */,
185 |                   e.isFatal() ? PARSE_ERROR : PARSE_WARNING,
186 |                   e.getMessage(), line));
187 |           parseSucceeded = parseSucceeded && !e.isFatal();
188 |         }
189 |       }
190 |     } catch (IOException e) {
191 |       errorManager.report(CheckLevel.ERROR,
192 |           JSError.make(filePath, 0, 0 /* char offset */,
193 |               PARSE_ERROR, "Error reading file: " + filePath));
194 |       parseSucceeded = false;
195 |     }
196 |   }

/**
   * Tells the type system that {@code owner} may have a property named
   * {@code propertyName}. This allows the registry to keep track of what
   * types a property is defined upon.
   *
   * This is NOT the same as saying that {@code owner} must have a property
   * named type. ObjectType#hasProperty attempts to minimize false positives
   * ("if we're not sure, then don't type check this property"). The type
   * registry, on the other hand, should attempt to minimize false negatives
   * ("if this property is assigned anywhere in the program, it must
   * show up in the type registry").
   */
Method code:

676 |       typesIndexedByProperty.put(propertyName, typeSet);
677 |     }
678 | 
679 |     typeSet.addAlternate(type);
680 |     addReferenceTypeIndexedByProperty(propertyName, type);
681 | 
682 |     // Clear cached values that depend on typesIndexedByProperty.
683 |     greatestSubtypeByProperty.remove(propertyName);
684 |   }

===== M0299 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PhaseOptimizer.consume(List<PassFactory>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PhaseOptimizer.java
Original range: 156-176
Documentation:
/**
   * Add the passes generated by the given factories to the compile sequence.
   *
   * Automatically pulls multi-run passes into fixed point loops. If there
   * are 1 or more multi-run passes in a row, they will run together in
   * the same fixed point loop. The passes will run until they are finished
   * making changes.
   *
   * The PhaseOptimizer is free to tweak the order and frequency of multi-run
   * passes in a fixed-point loop.
   */
Method code:
156 |   void consume(List<PassFactory> factories) {
157 |     Loop currentLoop = new Loop();
158 |     boolean isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
159 |     for (PassFactory factory : factories) {
160 |       if (factory.isOneTimePass()) {
161 |         if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
162 |           passes.add(currentLoop);
163 |           currentLoop = new Loop();
164 |           isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
165 |         }
166 |         addOneTimePass(factory);
167 |       } else {
168 |         currentLoop.addLoopedPass(factory);
169 |         isCurrentLoopPopulated = true;
170 |       }
171 |     }
172 | 
173 |     if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
174 |       passes.add(currentLoop);
175 |     }
176 |   }

Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CompilerOptions.java
Original range: 1030-1048
Documentation:
/**
   * Creates a map of String->Node from a map of String->Number/String/Boolean.
   */
Method code:
1030 |   private static Map<String, Node> getReplacementsHelper(
1031 |       Map<String, Object> source) {
1032 |     Map<String, Node> map = Maps.newHashMap();
1033 |     for (Map.Entry<String, Object> entry : source.entrySet()) {
1034 |       String name = entry.getKey();
1035 |       Object value = entry.getValue();
1036 |       if (value instanceof Boolean) {
1037 |         map.put(name, NodeUtil.booleanNode(((Boolean) value).booleanValue()));
1038 |       } else if (value instanceof Integer) {
1039 |         map.put(name, IR.number(((Integer) value).intValue()));
1040 |       } else if (value instanceof Double) {
1041 |         map.put(name, IR.number(((Double) value).doubleValue()));
1042 |       } else {
1043 |         Preconditions.checkState(value instanceof String);
1044 |         map.put(name, IR.string((String) value));
1045 |       }
1046 |     }
1047 |     return map;
1048 |   }

===== M0354 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.FixedPointGraphTraversal.computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E>,Set<N>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/graph/FixedPointGraphTraversal.java
Original range: 93-128
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute a fixed point for the given graph, entering from the given nodes.
   * @param graph The graph to traverse.
   * @param entrySet The nodes to begin traversing from.
   */
Method code:
93 |   public void computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E> graph, Set<N> entrySet) {
94 |     int cycleCount = 0;
95 |     long nodeCount = graph.getNodes().size();
96 | 
97 |     // Choose a bail-out heuristically in case the computation
98 |     // doesn't converge.
99 |     long maxIterations = Math.max(nodeCount * nodeCount * nodeCount, 100);
100 | 
101 |     // Use a LinkedHashSet, so that the traversal is deterministic.
102 |     LinkedHashSet<DiGraphNode<N, E>> workSet =
103 |         Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
104 |     for (N n : entrySet) {
105 |       workSet.add(graph.getDirectedGraphNode(n));
106 |     }
107 |     for (; !workSet.isEmpty() && cycleCount < maxIterations; cycleCount++) {
108 |       // For every out edge in the workSet, traverse that edge. If that
109 |       // edge updates the state of the graph, then add the destination
110 |       // node to the resultSet, so that we can update all of its out edges
111 |       // on the next iteration.
112 |       DiGraphNode<N, E> source = workSet.iterator().next();
113 |       N sourceValue = source.getValue();
114 | 
115 |       workSet.remove(source);
116 | 
117 |       List<DiGraphEdge<N, E>> outEdges = source.getOutEdges();
118 |       for (DiGraphEdge<N, E> edge : outEdges) {
119 |         N destNode = edge.getDestination().getValue();
120 |         if (callback.traverseEdge(sourceValue, edge.getValue(), destNode)) {
121 |           workSet.add(edge.getDestination());
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     Preconditions.checkState(cycleCount != maxIterations,
127 |         NON_HALTING_ERROR_MSG);
128 |   }

===== M0363 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 201-229
Documentation:
/**
   * Finds a fixed-point solution. The function has the side effect of replacing
   * the existing node annotations with the computed solutions using {@link
   * com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphNode#setAnnotation(Annotation)}.
   *
   * <p>Initially, each node's input and output flow state contains the value
   * given by {@link #createInitialEstimateLattice()} (with the exception of the
   * entry node of the graph which takes on the {@link #createEntryLattice()}
   * value. Each node will use the output state of its predecessor and compute a
   * output state according to the instruction. At that time, any nodes that
   * depends on the node's newly modified output value will need to recompute
   * their output state again. Each step will perform a computation at one node
   * until no extra computation will modify any existing output state anymore.
   *
   * @param maxSteps Max number of iterations before the method stops and throw
   *        a {@link MaxIterationsExceededException}. This will prevent the
   *        analysis from going into a infinite loop.
   */
Method code:
201 |   final void analyze(int maxSteps) {
202 |     initialize();
203 |     int step = 0;
204 |     while (!orderedWorkSet.isEmpty()) {
205 |       if (step > maxSteps) {
206 |         throw new MaxIterationsExceededException(
207 |           "Analysis did not terminate after " + maxSteps + " iterations");
208 |       }
209 |       DiGraphNode<N, Branch> curNode = orderedWorkSet.iterator().next();
210 |       orderedWorkSet.remove(curNode);
211 |       joinInputs(curNode);
212 |       if (flow(curNode)) {
213 |         // If there is a change in the current node, we want to grab the list
214 |         // of nodes that this node affects.
215 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> nextNodes = isForward() ?
216 |             cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(curNode) :
217 |             cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(curNode);
218 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> nextNode : nextNodes) {
219 |           if (nextNode != cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
220 |             orderedWorkSet.add(nextNode);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |       step++;
225 |     }
226 |     if (isForward()) {
227 |       joinInputs(getCfg().getImplicitReturn());
228 |     }
229 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GoogleCodingConvention.isConstant(String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GoogleCodingConvention.java
Original range: 70-87
Documentation:
/**
   * {@inheritDoc}
   *
   * <p>This enforces the Google const name convention, that the first character
   * after the last $ must be an upper-case letter and all subsequent letters
   * must be upper case. The name must be at least 2 characters long.
   *
   * <p>Examples:
   * <pre>
   *      aaa          Not constant - lower-case letters in the name
   *      A            Not constant - too short
   *      goog$A       Constant - letters after the $ are upper-case.
   *      AA17         Constant - digits can appear after the first letter
   *      goog$7A      Not constant - first character after the $ must be
   *                   upper case.
   *      $A           Constant - doesn't have to be anything in front of the $
   * </pre>
   */
Method code:
70 |   @Override
71 |   public boolean isConstant(String name) {
72 |     if (name.length() <= 1) {
73 |       return false;
74 |     }
75 | 
76 |     // In compiled code, '$' is often a namespace delimiter. To allow inlining
77 |     // of namespaced constants, we strip off any namespaces here.
78 |     int pos = name.lastIndexOf('$');
79 |     if (pos >= 0) {
80 |       name = name.substring(pos + 1);
81 |       if (name.length() == 0) {
82 |         return false;
83 |       }
84 |     }
85 | 
86 |     return isConstantKey(name);
87 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isExpressionResultUsed(Node)

/**
   * @returns false iff the result of the expression is not consumed.
   */
Method code:
3157 |   static boolean isExpressionResultUsed(Node expr) {
3158 |     // TODO(johnlenz): consider sharing some code with trySimpleUnusedResult.
3159 |     Node parent = expr.getParent();
3160 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
3161 |       case Token.BLOCK:
3162 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
3163 |         return false;
3164 |       case Token.CAST:
3165 |         return isExpressionResultUsed(parent);
3166 |       case Token.HOOK:
3167 |       case Token.AND:
3168 |       case Token.OR:
3169 |         return (expr == parent.getFirstChild())
3170 |             ? true : isExpressionResultUsed(parent);
3171 |       case Token.COMMA:
3172 |         Node gramps = parent.getParent();
3173 |         if (gramps.isCall() &&
3174 |             parent == gramps.getFirstChild()) {
3175 |           // Semantically, a direct call to eval is different from an indirect
3176 |           // call to an eval. See ECMA-262 S15.1.2.1. So it's OK for the first
3177 |           // expression to a comma to be a no-op if it's used to indirect
3178 |           // an eval. This we pretend that this is "used".
3179 |           if (expr == parent.getFirstChild() &&
3180 |               parent.getChildCount() == 2 &&
3181 |               expr.getNext().isName() &&
3182 |               "eval".equals(expr.getNext().getString())) {
3183 |             return true;
3184 |           }
3185 |         }
3186 | 
3187 |         return (expr == parent.getFirstChild())
3188 |             ? false : isExpressionResultUsed(parent);
3189 |       case Token.FOR:
3190 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
3191 |           // Only an expression whose result is in the condition part of the
3192 |           // expression is used.
3193 |           return (parent.getChildAtIndex(1) == expr);
3194 |         }
3195 |         break;
3196 |     }
3197 |     return true;
3198 |   }

/**
   * Is a FUNCTION node an function expression? An function expression is one
   * that has either no name or a name that is not added to the current scope.
   *
   * <p>Some examples of function expressions:
   * <pre>
   * (function () {})
   * (function f() {})()
   * [ function f() {} ]
   * var f = function f() {};
   * for (function f() {};;) {}
   * </pre>
   *
   * <p>Some examples of functions that are <em>not</em> expressions:
   * <pre>
   * function f() {}
   * if (x); else function f() {}
   * for (;;) { function f() {} }
   * </pre>
   *
   * @param n A node
   * @return Whether n is an function used within an expression.
   */
Method code:
1944 |   static boolean isFunctionExpression(Node n) {
1945 |     return n.isFunction() && !isStatement(n);
1946 |   }

148 |   @Override
149 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
150 |     this.root = root;
151 |     astPositionCounter = 0;
152 |     astPosition = Maps.newHashMap();
153 |     nodePriorities = Maps.newHashMap();
154 |     cfg = new AstControlFlowGraph(computeFallThrough(root), nodePriorities,
155 |                                   edgeAnnotations);
156 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, this);
157 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
158 | 
159 |     // Now, generate the priority of nodes by doing a depth-first
160 |     // search on the CFG.
161 |     priorityCounter = 0;
162 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry = cfg.getEntry();
163 |     prioritizeFromEntryNode(entry);
164 | 
165 |     if (shouldTraverseFunctions) {
166 |       // If we're traversing inner functions, we need to rank the
167 |       // priority of them too.
168 |       for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
169 |         Node value = candidate.getValue();
170 |         if (value != null && value.isFunction()) {
171 |           Preconditions.checkState(
172 |               !nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate) || candidate == entry);
173 |           prioritizeFromEntryNode(candidate);
174 |         }
175 |       }
176 |     }
177 | 
178 |     // At this point, all reachable nodes have been given a priority, but
179 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.
180 |     // Presumably, it doesn't really matter what priority they get, since
181 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
182 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
183 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
184 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
185 |       }
186 |     }
187 | 
188 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
189 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);
190 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MaybeReachingVariableUse.computeMayUse(Node,Node,ReachingUses,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MaybeReachingVariableUse.java
Original range: 169-254
Documentation:

Method code:
169 |   private void computeMayUse(
170 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, ReachingUses output, boolean conditional) {
171 |     switch (n.getType()) {
172 | 
173 |       case Token.BLOCK:
174 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
175 |         return;
176 | 
177 |       case Token.NAME:
178 |         addToUseIfLocal(n.getString(), cfgNode, output);
179 |         return;
180 | 
181 |       case Token.WHILE:
182 |       case Token.DO:
183 |       case Token.IF:
184 |         computeMayUse(
185 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
186 |         return;
187 | 
188 |       case Token.FOR:
189 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
190 |           computeMayUse(
191 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
192 |         } else {
193 |           // for(x in y) {...}
194 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
195 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
196 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
197 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
198 |           }
199 |           if (lhs.isName() && !conditional) {
200 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(lhs.getString(), output);
201 |           }
202 |           computeMayUse(rhs, cfgNode, output, conditional);
203 |         }
204 |         return;
205 | 
206 |       case Token.AND:
207 |       case Token.OR:
208 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
209 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
210 |         return;
211 | 
212 |       case Token.HOOK:
213 |         computeMayUse(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
214 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
215 |         computeMayUse(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
216 |         return;
217 | 
218 |       case Token.VAR:
219 |         Node varName = n.getFirstChild();
220 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasChildren(), "AST should be normalized");
221 | 
222 |         if (varName.hasChildren()) {
223 |           computeMayUse(varName.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
224 |           if (!conditional) {
225 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(varName.getString(), output);
226 |           }
227 |         }
228 |         return;
229 | 
230 |       default:
231 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
232 |           Node name = n.getFirstChild();
233 |           if (!conditional) {
234 |             removeFromUseIfLocal(name.getString(), output);
235 |           }
236 | 
237 |           // In case of a += "Hello". There is a read of a.
238 |           if (!n.isAssign()) {
239 |             addToUseIfLocal(name.getString(), cfgNode, output);
240 |           }
241 | 
242 |           computeMayUse(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
243 |         } else {
244 |           /*
245 |            * We want to traverse in reverse order because we want the LAST
246 |            * definition in the sub-tree....
247 |            * But we have no better way to traverse in reverse other :'(
248 |            */
249 |           for (Node c = n.getLastChild(); c != null; c = n.getChildBefore(c)) {
250 |             computeMayUse(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
251 |           }
252 |         }
253 |     }
254 |   }

1049 |       Node n = newStringNode(value);

1051 |         // NOTE(nicksantos): In JavaScript, there are 3 ways to
1052 |         // represent a vertical tab: \v, \x0B, \u000B.
1053 |         // The \v notation was added later, and is not understood

1062 |         // will be encoded with a \v.

1064 |         int end = start + literalNode.getLength();

===== M0408 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryMinimizeCondition(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 1131-1311
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to minimize conditions expressions, as there are additional
   * assumptions that can be made when it is known that the final result
   * is a boolean.
   *
   * The following transformations are done recursively:
   *   !(x||y) --> !x&&!y
   *   !(x&&y) --> !x||!y
   *   !!x     --> x
   * Thus:
   *   !(x&&!y) --> !x||!!y --> !x||y
   *
   *   Returns the replacement for n, or the original if no change was made
   */
Method code:
1131 |   private Node tryMinimizeCondition(Node n) {
1132 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
1133 | 
1134 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1135 |       case Token.NOT:
1136 |         Node first = n.getFirstChild();
1137 |         switch (first.getType()) {
1138 |           case Token.NOT: {
1139 |               Node newRoot = first.removeFirstChild();
1140 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1141 |               reportCodeChange();
1142 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1143 |               // NOT children are handled below.
1144 |               return newRoot;
1145 |             }
1146 |           case Token.AND:
1147 |           case Token.OR: {
1148 |               // !(!x && !y) --> x || y
1149 |               // !(!x || !y) --> x && y
1150 |               // !(!x && y) --> x || !y
1151 |               // !(!x || y) --> x && !y
1152 |               // !(x && !y) --> !x || y
1153 |               // !(x || !y) --> !x && y
1154 |               // !(x && y) --> !x || !y
1155 |               // !(x || y) --> !x && !y
1156 |               Node leftParent = first.getFirstChild();
1157 |               Node rightParent = first.getLastChild();
1158 |               Node left, right;
1159 | 
1160 |               // Check special case when such transformation cannot reduce
1161 |               // due to the added ()
1162 |               // It only occurs when both of expressions are not NOT expressions
1163 |               if (!leftParent.isNot()
1164 |                   && !rightParent.isNot()) {
1165 |                 // If an expression has higher precedence than && or ||,
1166 |                 // but lower precedence than NOT, an additional () is needed
1167 |                 // Thus we do not preceed
1168 |                 int op_precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType());
1169 |                 if ((isLowerPrecedence(leftParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1170 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(leftParent, op_precedence))
1171 |                     || (isLowerPrecedence(rightParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1172 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(rightParent, op_precedence))) {
1173 |                   return n;
1174 |                 }
1175 |               }
1176 | 
1177 |               if (leftParent.isNot()) {
1178 |                 left = leftParent.removeFirstChild();
1179 |               } else {
1180 |                 leftParent.detachFromParent();
1181 |                 left = IR.not(leftParent).srcref(leftParent);
1182 |               }
1183 |               if (rightParent.isNot()) {
1184 |                 right = rightParent.removeFirstChild();
1185 |               } else {
1186 |                 rightParent.detachFromParent();
1187 |                 right = IR.not(rightParent).srcref(rightParent);
1188 |               }
1189 | 
1190 |               int newOp = (first.isAnd()) ? Token.OR : Token.AND;
1191 |               Node newRoot = new Node(newOp, left, right);
1192 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1193 |               reportCodeChange();
1194 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1195 |               // AND and OR children below.
1196 |               return newRoot;
1197 |             }
1198 | 
1199 |            default:
1200 |              TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(first);
1201 |              if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1202 |                boolean result = nVal.not().toBoolean(true);
1203 |                int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1204 |                return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1205 |              }
1206 |         }
1207 |         // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the NOT
1208 |         // children in the general case in the main post-order traversal.
1209 |         return n;
1210 | 
1211 |       case Token.OR:
1212 |       case Token.AND: {
1213 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
1214 |         Node right = n.getLastChild();
1215 | 
1216 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1217 |         // the children, this can't be done in the general case.
1218 |         left = tryMinimizeCondition(left);
1219 |         right = tryMinimizeCondition(right);
1220 | 
1221 |         // Remove useless conditionals
1222 |         // Handle four cases:
1223 |         //   x || false --> x
1224 |         //   x || true  --> true
1225 |         //   x && true --> x
1226 |         //   x && false  --> false
1227 |         TernaryValue rightVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right);
1228 |         if (NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right) != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1229 |           int type = n.getType();
1230 |           Node replacement = null;
1231 |           boolean rval = rightVal.toBoolean(true);
1232 | 
1233 |           // (x || FALSE) => x
1234 |           // (x && TRUE) => x
1235 |           if (type == Token.OR && !rval ||
1236 |               type == Token.AND && rval) {
1237 |             replacement = left;
1238 |           } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
1239 |             replacement = right;
1240 |           }
1241 | 
1242 |           if (replacement != null) {
1243 |             n.detachChildren();
1244 |             parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1245 |             reportCodeChange();
1246 |             return replacement;
1247 |           }
1248 |         }
1249 |         return n;
1250 |       }
1251 | 
1252 |       case Token.HOOK: {
1253 |         Node condition = n.getFirstChild();
1254 |         Node trueNode = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
1255 |         Node falseNode = n.getLastChild();
1256 | 
1257 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1258 |         // the result children, this can't be done in the general case.
1259 |         // The condition is handled in the general case in #optimizeSubtree
1260 |         trueNode = tryMinimizeCondition(trueNode);
1261 |         falseNode = tryMinimizeCondition(falseNode);
1262 | 
1263 |         // Handle four cases:
1264 |         //   x ? true : false --> x
1265 |         //   x ? false : true --> !x
1266 |         //   x ? true : y     --> x || y
1267 |         //   x ? y : false    --> x && y
1268 |         Node replacement = null;
1269 |         TernaryValue trueNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(trueNode);
1270 |         TernaryValue falseNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(falseNode);
1271 |         if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE
1272 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1273 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1274 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1275 |           replacement = condition;
1276 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE
1277 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1278 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1279 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1280 |           replacement = IR.not(condition);
1281 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1282 |           // Remove useless true case.
1283 |           n.detachChildren();
1284 |           replacement = IR.or(condition, falseNode);
1285 |         } else if (falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1286 |           // Remove useless false case
1287 |           n.detachChildren();
1288 |           replacement = IR.and(condition, trueNode);
1289 |         }
1290 | 
1291 |         if (replacement != null) {
1292 |           parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1293 |           n = replacement;
1294 |           reportCodeChange();
1295 |         }
1296 | 
1297 |         return n;
1298 |       }
1299 | 
1300 |       default:
1301 |         // while(true) --> while(1)
1302 |         TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(n);
1303 |         if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1304 |           boolean result = nVal.toBoolean(true);
1305 |           int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1306 |           return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1307 |         }
1308 |         // We can't do anything else currently.
1309 |         return n;
1310 |     }
1311 |   }

Original range: 393-507
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to fold an array join: ['a', 'b', 'c'].join('') -> 'abc';
   */
Method code:
393 |   private Node tryFoldArrayJoin(Node n) {
394 |     Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
395 | 
396 |     if (callTarget == null || !callTarget.isGetProp()) {
397 |       return n;
398 |     }
399 | 
400 |     Node right = callTarget.getNext();
401 |     if (right != null) {
402 |       if (right.getNext() != null || !NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(right)) {
403 |         return n;
404 |       }
405 |     }
406 | 
407 |     Node arrayNode = callTarget.getFirstChild();
408 |     Node functionName = arrayNode.getNext();
409 | 
410 |     if (!arrayNode.isArrayLit() ||
411 |         !functionName.getString().equals("join")) {
412 |       return n;
413 |     }
414 | 
415 |     if (right != null && right.isString()
416 |         && ",".equals(right.getString())) {
417 |       // "," is the default, it doesn't need to be explicit
418 |       n.removeChild(right);
419 |       reportCodeChange();
420 |     }
421 | 
422 |     String joinString = (right == null) ? "," : NodeUtil.getStringValue(right);
423 |     List<Node> arrayFoldedChildren = Lists.newLinkedList();
424 |     StringBuilder sb = null;
425 |     int foldedSize = 0;
426 |     Node prev = null;
427 |     Node elem = arrayNode.getFirstChild();
428 |     // Merges adjacent String nodes.
429 |     while (elem != null) {
430 |       if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(elem) || elem.isEmpty()) {
431 |         if (sb == null) {
432 |           sb = new StringBuilder();
433 |         } else {
434 |           sb.append(joinString);
435 |         }
436 |         sb.append(NodeUtil.getArrayElementStringValue(elem));
437 |       } else {
438 |         if (sb != null) {
439 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
440 |           // + 2 for the quotes.
441 |           foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
442 |           arrayFoldedChildren.add(
443 |               IR.string(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
444 |           sb = null;
445 |         }
446 |         foldedSize += InlineCostEstimator.getCost(elem);
447 |         arrayFoldedChildren.add(elem);
448 |       }
449 |       prev = elem;
450 |       elem = elem.getNext();
451 |     }
452 | 
453 |     if (sb != null) {
454 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
455 |       // + 2 for the quotes.
456 |       foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
457 |       arrayFoldedChildren.add(
458 |           IR.string(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
459 |     }
460 |     // one for each comma.
461 |     foldedSize += arrayFoldedChildren.size() - 1;
462 | 
463 |     int originalSize = InlineCostEstimator.getCost(n);
464 |     switch (arrayFoldedChildren.size()) {
465 |       case 0:
466 |         Node emptyStringNode = IR.string("");
467 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, emptyStringNode);
468 |         reportCodeChange();
469 |         return emptyStringNode;
470 |       case 1:
471 |         Node foldedStringNode = arrayFoldedChildren.remove(0);
472 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
473 |           return n;
474 |         }
475 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
476 |         if (!foldedStringNode.isString()) {
477 |           // If the Node is not a string literal, ensure that
478 |           // it is coerced to a string.
479 |           Node replacement = IR.add(
480 |               IR.string("").srcref(n),
481 |               foldedStringNode);
482 |           foldedStringNode = replacement;
483 |         }
484 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, foldedStringNode);
485 |         reportCodeChange();
486 |         return foldedStringNode;
487 |       default:
488 |         // No folding could actually be performed.
489 |         if (arrayFoldedChildren.size() == arrayNode.getChildCount()) {
490 |           return n;
491 |         }
492 |         int kJoinOverhead = "[].join()".length();
493 |         foldedSize += kJoinOverhead;
494 |         foldedSize += (right != null) ? InlineCostEstimator.getCost(right) : 0;
495 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
496 |           return n;
497 |         }
498 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
499 |         for (Node node : arrayFoldedChildren) {
500 |           arrayNode.addChildToBack(node);
501 |         }
502 |         reportCodeChange();
503 |         break;
504 |     }
505 | 
506 |     return n;
507 |   }

   * TypeName := NameExpression | NameExpression TypeApplication
   * TypeApplication := '.<' TypeExpressionList '>'
   */

1843 |   private Node parseTypeName(JsDocToken token) {
1844 |     if (token != JsDocToken.STRING) {
1845 |       return reportGenericTypeSyntaxWarning();
1846 |     }

1848 |     String typeName = stream.getString();
1849 |     int lineno = stream.getLineno();

1853 |       skipEOLs();
1854 |       if (match(JsDocToken.STRING)) {
1855 |         next();
1856 |         typeName += stream.getString();
1857 |       }
1858 |     }
1859 |

1866 |       if (memberType != null) {

1871 |           return reportTypeSyntaxWarning("msg.jsdoc.missing.gt");
1872 |         }
1873 |

1875 |       }
1876 |     }

===== M0457 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.java
Original range: 158-192

Method code:
158 |   @Override
159 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
160 |     switch (n.getType()) {
161 |       case Token.NAME:
162 |         String newName = getReplacementName(n.getString());
163 |         if (newName != null) {
164 |           Renamer renamer = nameStack.peek();
165 |           if (renamer.stripConstIfReplaced()) {
166 |             // TODO(johnlenz): Do we need to do anything about the Javadoc?
167 |             n.removeProp(Node.IS_CONSTANT_NAME);
168 |           }
169 |           n.setString(newName);
170 |           t.getCompiler().reportCodeChange();
171 |         }
172 |         break;
173 | 
174 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
175 |         // Remove the function body scope
176 |         nameStack.pop();
177 |         // Remove function recursive name (if any).
178 |         nameStack.pop();
179 |         break;
180 | 
181 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
182 |         // Note: The parameters and function body variables live in the
183 |         // same scope, we introduce the scope when in the "shouldTraverse"
184 |         // visit of LP, but remove it when when we exit the function above.
185 |         break;
186 | 
187 |       case Token.CATCH:
188 |         // Remove catch except name from the stack of names.
189 |         nameStack.pop();
190 |         break;
191 |     }
192 |   }

===== M0466 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.functionCallHasSideEffects(Node,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 994-1051
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if calls to this function have side effects.
   *
   * @param callNode The call node to inspected.
   * @param compiler A compiler object to provide program state changing
   *     context information. Can be null.
   */
Method code:
994 |   static boolean functionCallHasSideEffects(
995 |       Node callNode, @Nullable AbstractCompiler compiler) {
996 |     if (!callNode.isCall()) {
997 |       throw new IllegalStateException(
998 |           "Expected CALL node, got " + Token.name(callNode.getType()));
999 |     }
1000 | 
1001 |     if (callNode.isNoSideEffectsCall()) {
1002 |       return false;
1003 |     }
1004 | 
1005 |     Node nameNode = callNode.getFirstChild();
1006 | 
1007 |     // Built-in functions with no side effects.
1008 |     if (nameNode.isName()) {
1009 |       String name = nameNode.getString();
1010 |       if (BUILTIN_FUNCTIONS_WITHOUT_SIDEEFFECTS.contains(name)) {
1011 |         return false;
1012 |       }
1013 |     } else if (nameNode.isGetProp()) {
1014 |       if (callNode.hasOneChild()
1015 |           && OBJECT_METHODS_WITHOUT_SIDEEFFECTS.contains(
1016 |                 nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
1017 |         return false;
1018 |       }
1019 | 
1020 |       if (callNode.isOnlyModifiesThisCall()
1021 |           && evaluatesToLocalValue(nameNode.getFirstChild())) {
1022 |         return false;
1023 |       }
1024 | 
1025 |       // Math.floor has no side-effects.
1026 |       // TODO(nicksantos): This is a terrible terrible hack, until
1027 |       // I create a definitionProvider that understands namespacing.
1028 |       if (nameNode.getFirstChild().isName()) {
1029 |         if ("Math.floor".equals(nameNode.getQualifiedName())) {
1030 |           return false;
1031 |         }
1032 |       }
1033 | 
1034 |       if (compiler != null && !compiler.hasRegExpGlobalReferences()) {
1035 |         if (nameNode.getFirstChild().isRegExp()
1036 |             && REGEXP_METHODS.contains(nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
1037 |           return false;
1038 |         } else if (nameNode.getFirstChild().isString()
1039 |             && STRING_REGEXP_METHODS.contains(
1040 |                 nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
1041 |           Node param = nameNode.getNext();
1042 |           if (param != null &&
1043 |               (param.isString() || param.isRegExp())) {
1044 |             return false;
1045 |           }
1046 |         }
1047 |       }
1048 |     }
1049 | 
1050 |     return true;
1051 |   }

   * Try removing unneeded block nodes and their useless children

Method code:
509 |   Node tryOptimizeBlock(Node n) {
510 |     // Remove any useless children
511 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; ) {
512 |       Node next = c.getNext();  // save c.next, since 'c' may be removed
513 |       if (!isUnremovableNode(c) && !mayHaveSideEffects(c)) {

74 |     // -Xmx1024 in closure. We might have to look at coding conventions for

78 |     }

83 |     }
84 | 
85 |     // We are not going to do any dead assignment elimination in when there is
86 |     // at least one inner function because in most browsers, when there is a
87 |     // closure, ALL the variables are saved (escaped).
88 |     Node fnBlock = t.getScopeRoot().getLastChild();
89 |     if (NodeUtil.containsFunction(fnBlock)) {

744 |         return;
745 |       }

755 |       }

760 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.removeUnreferencedVars()

/**
   * Removes any vars in the scope that were not referenced. Removes any
   * assignments to those variables as well.
   */
Method code:
803 |   private void removeUnreferencedVars() {
804 |     for (Iterator<Var> it = maybeUnreferenced.iterator(); it.hasNext(); ) {
805 |       Var var = it.next();
806 | 
807 |       // Remove calls to inheritance-defining functions where the unreferenced
808 |       // class is the subclass.
809 |       for (Node exprCallNode : classDefiningCalls.get(var)) {
810 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(exprCallNode.getParent(), exprCallNode);
811 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
812 |       }
813 | 
814 |       // Regardless of what happens to the original declaration,
815 |       // we need to remove all assigns, because they may contain references
816 |       // to other unreferenced variables.
817 |       removeAllAssigns(var);
818 | 
819 |       compiler.addToDebugLog("Unreferenced var: " + var.name);
820 |       Node nameNode = var.nameNode;
821 |       Node toRemove = nameNode.getParent();
822 |       Node parent = toRemove.getParent();
823 | 
824 |       Preconditions.checkState(
825 |           toRemove.isVar() ||
826 |           toRemove.isFunction() ||
827 |           toRemove.isParamList() &&
828 |           parent.isFunction(),
829 |           "We should only declare vars and functions and function args");
830 | 
831 |       if (toRemove.isParamList() &&
832 |           parent.isFunction()) {
833 |         // Don't remove function arguments here. That's a special case
834 |         // that's taken care of in removeUnreferencedFunctionArgs.
835 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(toRemove)) {
836 |         if (!preserveFunctionExpressionNames) {
837 |           toRemove.getFirstChild().setString("");
838 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
839 |         }
840 |         // Don't remove bleeding functions.
841 |       } else if (parent != null &&
842 |           parent.isFor() &&
843 |           parent.getChildCount() < 4) {
844 |         // foreach iterations have 3 children. Leave them alone.
845 |       } else if (toRemove.isVar() &&
846 |           nameNode.hasChildren() &&
847 |           NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(nameNode.getFirstChild(), compiler)) {
848 |         // If this is a single var declaration, we can at least remove the
849 |         // declaration itself and just leave the value, e.g.,
850 |         // var a = foo(); => foo();
851 |         if (toRemove.getChildCount() == 1) {
852 |           parent.replaceChild(toRemove,
853 |               IR.exprResult(nameNode.removeFirstChild()));
854 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
855 |         }
856 |       } else if (toRemove.isVar() &&
857 |           toRemove.getChildCount() > 1) {
858 |         // For var declarations with multiple names (i.e. var a, b, c),
859 |         // only remove the unreferenced name
860 |         toRemove.removeChild(nameNode);
861 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
862 |       } else if (parent != null) {
863 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(parent, toRemove);
864 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
865 |       }
866 |     }
867 |   }

/**
   * @param compareJsType Whether to compare the JSTypes of the nodes.
   * @param recur Whether to compare the children of the current node, if

   * @param shallow If true, the method doesn't recur into inner functions.
   * @return Whether this node is equivalent semantically to the provided node.
   */
Method code:
1512 |   boolean isEquivalentTo(
1513 |       Node node, boolean compareJsType, boolean recur, boolean shallow) {
1514 |     if (type != node.getType()
1515 |         || getChildCount() != node.getChildCount()
1516 |         || this.getClass() != node.getClass()) {
1517 |       return false;
1518 |     }

1521 |       return false;

===== M0550 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.interpretAssigns()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 723-772
Documentation:
/**
   * Look at all the property assigns to all variables.
   * These may or may not count as references. For example,
   *
   * <code>
   * var x = {};
   * x.foo = 3; // not a reference.
   * var y = foo();
   * y.foo = 3; // is a reference.
   * </code>
   *
   * Interpreting assignments could mark a variable as referenced that
   * wasn't referenced before, in order to keep it alive. Because we find
   * references by lazily traversing subtrees, marking a variable as
   * referenced could trigger new traversals of new subtrees, which could
   * find new references.
   *
   * Therefore, this interpretation needs to be run to a fixed point.
   */
Method code:
723 |   private void interpretAssigns() {
724 |     boolean changes = false;
725 |     do {
726 |       changes = false;
727 | 
728 |       // We can't use traditional iterators and iterables for this list,
729 |       // because our lazily-evaluated continuations will modify it while
730 |       // we traverse it.
731 |       for (int current = 0; current < maybeUnreferenced.size(); current++) {
732 |         Var var = maybeUnreferenced.get(current);
733 |         if (referenced.contains(var)) {
734 |           maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
735 |           current--;
736 |         } else {
737 |           boolean assignedToUnknownValue = false;
738 |           boolean hasPropertyAssign = false;
739 | 
740 |           if (var.getParentNode().isVar() &&
741 |               !NodeUtil.isForIn(var.getParentNode().getParent())) {
742 |             Node value = var.getInitialValue();
743 |             assignedToUnknownValue = value != null &&
744 |                 !NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(value, true);
745 |           } else {
746 |             // This was initialized to a function arg or a catch param
747 |             // or a for...in variable.
748 |             assignedToUnknownValue = true;
749 |           }
750 | 
751 |           boolean maybeEscaped = false;
752 |           for (Assign assign : assignsByVar.get(var)) {
753 |             if (assign.isPropertyAssign) {
754 |               hasPropertyAssign = true;
755 |             } else if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(
756 |                 assign.assignNode.getLastChild(), true)) {
757 |               assignedToUnknownValue = true;
758 |             }
759 |             if (assign.maybeAliased) {
760 |               maybeEscaped = true;
761 |             }
762 |           }
763 | 
764 |           if ((assignedToUnknownValue || maybeEscaped) && hasPropertyAssign) {
765 |             changes = markReferencedVar(var) || changes;
766 |             maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
767 |             current--;
768 |           }
769 |         }
770 |       }
771 |     } while (changes);
772 |   }

1332 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1333 |         if (hasErrors()) {
1334 |           return null;

1341 |         processAMDAndCommonJSModules();

1343 |

1349 |         for (CompilerInput input : inputs) {
1350 |           // Forward-declare all the provided types, so that they
1351 |           // are not flagged even if they are dropped from the process.
1352 |           for (String provide : input.getProvides()) {
1353 |             getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(provide);
1354 |           }
1355 |         }
1356 | 
1357 |         try {

1359 |               (moduleGraph == null ? new JSModuleGraph(modules) : moduleGraph)
1360 |               .manageDependencies(options.dependencyOptions, inputs);
1361 |           staleInputs = true;

211 |   private Node tryFoldSimpleFunctionCall(Node n) {
212 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isCall());
213 |     Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
214 |     if (callTarget != null && callTarget.isName() &&
215 |           callTarget.getString().equals("String")) {
216 |       // Fold String(a) to '' + (a) on immutable literals,
217 |       // which allows further optimizations
218 |       //
219 |       // We can't do this in the general case, because String(a) has
220 |       // slightly different semantics than '' + (a). See
221 |       // http://code.google.com/p/closure-compiler/issues/detail?id=759
222 |       Node value = callTarget.getNext();
223 |       if (value != null && value.getNext() == null &&
224 |           NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value)) {
225 |         Node addition = IR.add(
226 |             IR.string("").srcref(callTarget),
227 |             value.detachFromParent());
228 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, addition);
229 |         reportCodeChange();
230 |         return addition;
231 |       }
232 |     }
233 |     return n;
234 |   }

===== M0612 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeReplaceKnownMethods.tryFoldKnownStringMethods(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeReplaceKnownMethods.java
Original range: 81-131
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to evaluate known String methods
   *    .indexOf(), .substr(), .substring()
   */
Method code:
81 |   private Node tryFoldKnownStringMethods(Node subtree) {
82 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(subtree.isCall());
83 | 
84 |     // check if this is a call on a string method
85 |     // then dispatch to specific folding method.
86 |     Node callTarget = subtree.getFirstChild();
87 |     if (callTarget == null) {
88 |       return subtree;
89 |     }
90 | 
91 |     if (!NodeUtil.isGet(callTarget)) {
92 |       return subtree;
93 |     }
94 | 
95 |     Node stringNode = callTarget.getFirstChild();
96 |     Node functionName = stringNode.getNext();
97 | 
98 |     if ((!stringNode.isString()) ||
99 |         (!functionName.isString())) {
100 |       return subtree;
101 |     }
102 | 
103 |     String functionNameString = functionName.getString();
104 |     Node firstArg = callTarget.getNext();
105 |     if (functionNameString.equals("split")) {
106 |       subtree = tryFoldStringSplit(subtree, stringNode, firstArg);
107 |     } else if (firstArg == null) {
108 |       if (functionNameString.equals("toLowerCase")) {
109 |         subtree = tryFoldStringToLowerCase(subtree, stringNode);
110 |       } else if (functionNameString.equals("toUpperCase")) {
111 |         subtree = tryFoldStringToUpperCase(subtree, stringNode);
112 |       }
113 |       return subtree;
114 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(firstArg)) {
115 |       if (functionNameString.equals("indexOf") ||
116 |           functionNameString.equals("lastIndexOf")) {
117 |         subtree = tryFoldStringIndexOf(subtree, functionNameString,
118 |             stringNode, firstArg);
119 |       } else if (functionNameString.equals("substr")) {
120 |         subtree = tryFoldStringSubstr(subtree, stringNode, firstArg);
121 |       } else if (functionNameString.equals("substring")) {
122 |         subtree = tryFoldStringSubstring(subtree, stringNode, firstArg);
123 |       } else if (functionNameString.equals("charAt")) {
124 |         subtree = tryFoldStringCharAt(subtree, stringNode, firstArg);
125 |       } else if (functionNameString.equals("charCodeAt")) {
126 |         subtree = tryFoldStringCharCodeAt(subtree, stringNode, firstArg);
127 |       }
128 |     }
129 | 
130 |     return subtree;
131 |   }

/**
   * Traverses everything in the current scope and marks variables that
   * are referenced.
   *
   * During traversal, we identify subtrees that will only be
   * referenced if their enclosing variables are referenced. Instead of
   * traversing those subtrees, we create a continuation for them,
   * and traverse them lazily.
   */
Method code:
192 |   private void traverseNode(Node n, Node parent, Scope scope) {
193 |     int type = n.getType();
194 |     Var var = null;
195 |     switch (type) {
196 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
197 |         // If this function is a removable var, then create a continuation
198 |         // for it instead of traversing immediately.
199 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
200 |           var = scope.getVar(n.getFirstChild().getString());
201 |         }
202 | 
203 |         if (var != null && isRemovableVar(var)) {
204 |           continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
205 |         } else {
206 |           traverseFunction(n, scope);
207 |         }
208 |         return;
209 | 
210 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
211 |         Assign maybeAssign = Assign.maybeCreateAssign(n);
212 |         if (maybeAssign != null) {
213 |           // Put this in the assign map. It might count as a reference,
214 |           // but we won't know that until we have an index of all assigns.
215 |           var = scope.getVar(maybeAssign.nameNode.getString());
216 |           if (var != null) {
217 |             assignsByVar.put(var, maybeAssign);
218 |             assignsByNode.put(maybeAssign.nameNode, maybeAssign);
219 | 
220 |             if (isRemovableVar(var) &&
221 |                 !maybeAssign.mayHaveSecondarySideEffects) {
222 |               // If the var is unreferenced and performing this assign has
223 |               // no secondary side effects, then we can create a continuation
224 |               // for it instead of traversing immediately.
225 |               continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
226 |               return;
227 |             }
228 |           }
229 |         }
230 |         break;
231 | 
232 |       case Token.CALL:
233 |         Var modifiedVar = null;
234 | 
235 |         // Look for calls to inheritance-defining calls (such as goog.inherits).
236 |         SubclassRelationship subclassRelationship =
237 |             codingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(n);
238 |         if (subclassRelationship != null) {
239 |           modifiedVar = scope.getVar(subclassRelationship.subclassName);
240 |         } else {
241 |           // Look for calls to addSingletonGetter calls.
242 |           String className = codingConvention.getSingletonGetterClassName(n);
243 |           if (className != null) {
244 |             modifiedVar = scope.getVar(className);
245 |           }
246 |         }
247 | 
248 |         // Don't try to track the inheritance calls for non-globals. It would
249 |         // be more correct to only not track when the subclass does not
250 |         // reference a constructor, but checking that it is a global is
251 |         // easier and mostly the same.
252 |         if (modifiedVar != null && modifiedVar.isGlobal()
253 |             && !referenced.contains(modifiedVar)) {
254 |           // Save a reference to the EXPR node.
255 |           classDefiningCalls.put(modifiedVar, parent);
256 |           continuations.put(modifiedVar, new Continuation(n, scope));
257 |           return;
258 |         }
259 |         break;
260 | 
261 |       case Token.NAME:
262 |         var = scope.getVar(n.getString());
263 |         if (parent.isVar()) {
264 |           Node value = n.getFirstChild();
265 |           if (value != null && var != null && isRemovableVar(var) &&
266 |               !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(value, compiler)) {
267 |             // If the var is unreferenced and creating its value has no side
268 |             // effects, then we can create a continuation for it instead
269 |             // of traversing immediately.
270 |             continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
271 |             return;
272 |           }
273 |         } else {
274 | 
275 |           // If arguments is escaped, we just assume the worst and continue
276 |           // on all the parameters.
277 |           if ("arguments".equals(n.getString()) && scope.isLocal()) {
278 |             Node lp = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
279 |             for (Node a = lp.getFirstChild(); a != null; a = a.getNext()) {
280 |               markReferencedVar(scope.getVar(a.getString()));
281 |             }
282 |           }
283 | 
284 |           // All name references that aren't declarations or assigns
285 |           // are references to other vars.
286 |           if (var != null) {
287 |             // If that var hasn't already been marked referenced, then
288 |             // start tracking it.  If this is an assign, do nothing
289 |             // for now.
290 |             if (isRemovableVar(var)) {
291 |               if (!assignsByNode.containsKey(n)) {
292 |                 markReferencedVar(var);
293 |               }
294 |             } else {
295 |               markReferencedVar(var);
296 |             }
297 |           }
298 |         }
299 |         break;
300 |     }
301 | 
302 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
303 |       traverseNode(c, n, scope);
304 |     }
305 |   }

     * Move all the functions that are valid at the execution of the first
     * statement of the function to the beginning of the function definition.

46 |   private boolean canFuseIntoOneStatement(Node block) {
47 |     // Fold only statement block. NOT scripts block.
48 |     if (!block.isBlock()) {
49 |       return false;
50 |     }
51 | 
52 |     // Nothing to do here.
53 |     if (!block.hasChildren() || block.hasOneChild()) {
54 |       return false;
55 |     }
56 | 
57 |     Node last = block.getLastChild();
58 | 
59 |     for (Node c = block.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
60 |       if (!c.isExprResult() && c != last) {
61 |         return false;
62 |       }
63 |     }
64 | 
65 |     // TODO(user): Support more control statement for fusion.
66 |     // FOR
67 |     switch(last.getType()) {
68 |       case Token.IF:
69 |       case Token.THROW:
70 |       case Token.SWITCH:
71 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
72 |         return true;
73 |       case Token.RETURN:
74 |         // We don't want to add a new return value.
75 |         return last.hasChildren();
76 |       case Token.FOR:
77 |         return NodeUtil.isForIn(last) &&
78 |             // Avoid cases where we have for(var x = foo() in a) { ....
79 |             !mayHaveSideEffects(last.getFirstChild());
80 |     }
81 | 
82 |     return false;
83 |   }

   * Try to fold array-length. e.g [1, 2, 3].length ==> 3, [x, y].length ==> 2
   */
Method code:
1338 |   private Node tryFoldGetProp(Node n, Node left, Node right) {
1339 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(n.isGetProp());
1340 | 
1341 |     if (left.isObjectLit()) {
1342 |       return tryFoldObjectPropAccess(n, left, right);
1343 |     }

1346 |         right.getString().equals("length")) {

===== M0699 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.java
Original range: 170-279
Documentation:
/**
   * General cascading unused operation node removal.
   * @param n The root of the expression to simplify.
   * @param removeUnused If true, the node is removed from the AST if
   *     it is not useful, otherwise it replaced with an EMPTY node.
   * @return The replacement node, or null if the node was is not useful.
   */
Method code:
170 |   private Node trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node n, boolean removeUnused) {
171 |     Node result = n;
172 | 
173 |     // Simplify the results of conditional expressions
174 |     switch (n.getType()) {
175 |       case Token.HOOK:
176 |         Node trueNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild().getNext());
177 |         Node falseNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
178 |         // If one or more of the conditional children were removed,
179 |         // transform the HOOK to an equivalent operation:
180 |         //    x() ? foo() : 1 --> x() && foo()
181 |         //    x() ? 1 : foo() --> x() || foo()
182 |         //    x() ? 1 : 1 --> x()
183 |         //    x ? 1 : 1 --> null
184 |         if (trueNode == null && falseNode != null) {
185 |           n.setType(Token.OR);
186 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
187 |         } else if (trueNode != null && falseNode == null) {
188 |           n.setType(Token.AND);
189 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
190 |         } else if (trueNode == null && falseNode == null) {
191 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
192 |         } else {
193 |           // The structure didn't change.
194 |           result = n;
195 |         }
196 |         break;
197 |       case Token.AND:
198 |       case Token.OR:
199 |         // Try to remove the second operand from a AND or OR operations:
200 |         //    x() || f --> x()
201 |         //    x() && f --> x()
202 |         Node conditionalResultNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(
203 |             n.getLastChild());
204 |         if (conditionalResultNode == null) {
205 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
206 |           // The conditionally executed code was removed, so
207 |           // replace the AND/OR with its LHS or remove it if it isn't useful.
208 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
209 |         }
210 |         break;
211 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
212 |         // A function expression isn't useful if it isn't used, remove it and
213 |         // don't bother to look at its children.
214 |         result = null;
215 |         break;
216 |       case Token.COMMA:
217 |         // We rewrite other operations as COMMA expressions (which will later
218 |         // get split into individual EXPR_RESULT statement, if possible), so
219 |         // we special case COMMA (we don't want to rewrite COMMAs as new COMMAs
220 |         // nodes.
221 |         Node left = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
222 |         Node right = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
223 |         if (left == null && right == null) {
224 |           result = null;
225 |         } else if (left == null) {
226 |           result = right;
227 |         } else if (right == null){
228 |           result = left;
229 |         } else {
230 |           // The structure didn't change.
231 |           result = n;
232 |         }
233 |         break;
234 |       default:
235 |         if (!nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
236 |           // This is the meat of this function. The node itself doesn't generate
237 |           // any side-effects but preserve any side-effects in the children.
238 |           Node resultList = null;
239 |           for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
240 |             next = c.getNext();
241 |             c = trySimplifyUnusedResult(c);
242 |             if (c != null) {
243 |               c.detachFromParent();
244 |               if (resultList == null)  {
245 |                 // The first side-effect can be used stand-alone.
246 |                 resultList = c;
247 |               } else {
248 |                 // Leave the side-effects in-place, simplifying it to a COMMA
249 |                 // expression.
250 |                 resultList = IR.comma(resultList, c).srcref(c);
251 |               }
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 |           result = resultList;
255 |         }
256 |     }
257 | 
258 |     // Fix up the AST, replace or remove the an unused node (if requested).
259 |     if (n != result) {
260 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
261 |       if (result == null) {
262 |         if (removeUnused) {
263 |           parent.removeChild(n);
264 |         } else {
265 |           result = IR.empty().srcref(n);
266 |           parent.replaceChild(n, result);
267 |         }
268 |       } else {
269 |         // A new COMMA expression may not have an existing parent.
270 |         if (result.getParent() != null) {
271 |           result.detachFromParent();
272 |         }
273 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, result);
274 |       }
275 |       reportCodeChange();
276 |     }
277 | 
278 |     return result;
279 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.PrototypeObjectType.isSubtype(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/PrototypeObjectType.java

Method code:
316 |   @Override
317 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
318 |     if (JSType.isSubtypeHelper(this, that)) {
319 |       return true;
320 |     }
321 | 
322 |     // Union types
323 |     if (that.isUnionType()) {
324 |       // The static {@code JSType.isSubtype} check already decomposed
325 |       // union types, so we don't need to check those again.
326 |       return false;
327 |     }
328 | 
329 |     // record types
330 |     if (that.isRecordType()) {
331 |       return RecordType.isSubtype(this, that.toMaybeRecordType());
332 |     }
333 | 
334 |     // Interfaces
335 |     // Find all the interfaces implemented by this class and compare each one
336 |     // to the interface instance.
337 |     ObjectType thatObj = that.toObjectType();
338 |     FunctionType thatCtor = thatObj == null ? null : thatObj.getConstructor();
339 | 
340 |     if (getConstructor() != null && getConstructor().isInterface()) {
341 |       for (ObjectType thisInterface : getCtorExtendedInterfaces()) {
342 |         if (thisInterface.isSubtype(that)) {
343 |           return true;
344 |         }
345 |       }
346 |     } else if (thatCtor != null && thatCtor.isInterface()) {
347 |       Iterable<ObjectType> thisInterfaces = getCtorImplementedInterfaces();
348 |       for (ObjectType thisInterface : thisInterfaces) {
349 |         if (thisInterface.isSubtype(that)) {
350 |           return true;
351 |         }
352 |       }
353 |     }
354 | 
355 |     // other prototype based objects
356 |     if (isUnknownType() || implicitPrototypeChainIsUnknown()) {
357 |       // If unsure, say 'yes', to avoid spurious warnings.
358 |       // TODO(user): resolve the prototype chain completely in all cases,
359 |       // to avoid guessing.
360 |       return true;
361 |     }
362 |     return thatObj != null && isImplicitPrototype(thatObj);
363 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 123-169

/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a literal. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function
   * except it return UNKNOWN for known values with side-effects, use
   * getImpureBooleanValue if you don't care about side-effects.
   */
Method code:
123 |   static TernaryValue getPureBooleanValue(Node n) {
124 |     switch (n.getType()) {
125 |       case Token.STRING:
126 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getString().length() > 0);
127 | 
128 |       case Token.NUMBER:
129 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getDouble() != 0);
130 | 
131 |       case Token.NOT:
132 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild()).not();
133 | 
134 |       case Token.NULL:
135 |       case Token.FALSE:
136 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
137 | 
138 |       case Token.VOID:
139 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n.getFirstChild())) {
140 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
141 |         }
142 |         break;
143 | 
144 |       case Token.NAME:
145 |         String name = n.getString();
146 |         if ("undefined".equals(name)
147 |             || "NaN".equals(name)) {
148 |           // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the keyword
149 |           // undefined to something other than the value undefined.
150 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
151 |         } else if ("Infinity".equals(name)) {
152 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
153 |         }
154 |         break;
155 | 
156 |       case Token.TRUE:
157 |       case Token.REGEXP:
158 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
159 | 
160 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
161 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
162 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
163 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
164 |         }
165 |         break;
166 |     }
167 | 
168 |     return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
169 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ShadowVariables.DoShadowVariables.enterScope(NodeTraversal)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ShadowVariables.java
Original range: 174-225

Method code:
174 |     @Override
175 |     public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
176 |       Scope s = t.getScope();
177 |       if (!s.isLocal()) {
178 |         return;
179 |       }
180 | 
181 |       // Since we don't shadow global, there is nothing to be done in the
182 |       // first immediate local scope as well.
183 |       if (s.getParent().isGlobal()) {
184 |         return;
185 |       }
186 | 
187 |       for (Iterator<Var> vars = s.getVars(); vars.hasNext();) {
188 |         Var var = vars.next();
189 | 
190 |         // Don't shadow variables that is bleed-out to fix an IE bug.
191 |         if (var.isBleedingFunction()) {
192 |           continue;
193 |         }
194 | 
195 |         // Don't shadow an exported local.
196 |         if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.name, s.isLocal())) {
197 |           continue;
198 |         }
199 | 
200 |         // Try to look for the best shadow for the current candidate.
201 |         Assignment bestShadow = findBestShadow(s);
202 |         if (bestShadow == null) {
203 |           continue;
204 |         }
205 | 
206 |         // The name assignment being shadowed.
207 |         Assignment localAssignment = assignments.get(var.getName());
208 | 
209 |         // Only shadow if this increases the number of occurrences of the
210 |         // shadowed variable.
211 |         if (bestShadow.count < localAssignment.count) {
212 |           continue; // Hope the next local variable would have a smaller count.
213 |         }
214 | 
215 |         doShadow(localAssignment, bestShadow, var);
216 | 
217 |         if (oldPseudoNameMap != null) {
218 |           String targetPseudoName =
219 |             oldPseudoNameMap.get(s.getVar(bestShadow.oldName).nameNode);
220 |           for (Node use : varToNameUsage.get(var)) {
221 |             deltaPseudoNameMap.put(use, targetPseudoName);
222 |           }
223 |         }
224 |       }
225 |     }

350 |           break;
351 |         case Token.NAME:
352 |           // This may be a variable get or set.
353 |           if (parent != null) {
354 |             switch (parent.getType()) {
355 |               case Token.VAR:
356 |                 isSet = true;
357 |                 Node rvalue = n.getFirstChild();
358 |                 type = rvalue == null ? Name.Type.OTHER : getValueType(rvalue);
359 |                 break;
360 |               case Token.ASSIGN:
361 |                 if (parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
362 |                   isSet = true;
363 |                   type = getValueType(n.getNext());
364 |                 }
365 |                 break;
366 |               case Token.GETPROP:
367 |                 return;
368 |               case Token.FUNCTION:
369 |                 Node gramps = parent.getParent();
370 |                 if (gramps == null ||
371 |                     NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) return;
372 |                 isSet = true;
373 |                 type = Name.Type.FUNCTION;
374 |                 break;
375 |               case Token.INC:
376 |               case Token.DEC:
377 |                 isSet = true;
378 |                 type = Name.Type.OTHER;
379 |                 break;
380 |               default:
381 |                 if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent) &&
382 |                     parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
383 |                   isSet = true;
384 |                   type = Name.Type.OTHER;
385 |                 }
386 |             }
387 |           }
388 |           name = n.getString();
389 |           break;
390 |         case Token.GETPROP:
391 |           // This may be a namespaced name get or set.
392 |           if (parent != null) {
393 |             switch (parent.getType()) {
394 |               case Token.ASSIGN:
395 |                 if (parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
396 |                   isSet = true;
397 |                   type = getValueType(n.getNext());
398 |                   isPropAssign = true;
399 |                 }
400 |                 break;
401 |               case Token.INC:
402 |               case Token.DEC:
403 |                 isSet = true;
404 |                 type = Name.Type.OTHER;
405 |                 break;
406 |               case Token.GETPROP:
407 |                 return;
408 |               default:
409 |                 if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(parent) &&
410 |                     parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
411 |                   isSet = true;
412 |                   type = Name.Type.OTHER;
413 |                 }
414 |             }
415 |           }
416 |           name = n.getQualifiedName();
417 |           if (name == null) return;
418 |           break;
419 |         default:
420 |           return;
421 |       }
422 | 
423 |       // We are only interested in global names.
424 |       Scope scope = t.getScope();
425 |       if (!isGlobalNameReference(name, scope)) {
426 |         return;
427 |       }
428 | 
429 |       if (isSet) {
430 |         if (isGlobalScope(scope)) {
431 |           handleSetFromGlobal(t, n, parent, name, isPropAssign, type);
432 |         } else {
433 |           handleSetFromLocal(t, n, parent, name);
434 |         }
435 |       } else {
436 |         handleGet(t, n, parent, name);
437 |       }
438 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PhaseOptimizer.Loop.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PhaseOptimizer.java
Original range: 380-450
Documentation:

Method code:
380 |     @Override
381 |     public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
382 |       Preconditions.checkState(!inLoop, "Nested loops are forbidden");
383 |       inLoop = true;
384 |       if (randomizeLoops) {
385 |         randomizePasses();
386 |       } else {
387 |         optimizePasses();
388 |       }
389 | 
390 |       // Set up function-change tracking
391 |       scopeHandler = new ScopedChangeHandler();
392 |       compiler.addChangeHandler(scopeHandler);
393 |       currentScope = root;
394 |       // lastRuns is initialized before each loop. This way, when a pass is run
395 |       // in the 2nd loop for the 1st time, it looks at all scopes.
396 |       lastRuns = new HashMap<NamedPass, Integer>();
397 |       for (NamedPass pass : myPasses) {
398 |         lastRuns.put(pass, START_TIME);
399 |       }
400 |       // Contains a pass iff it made changes the last time it was run.
401 |       Set<NamedPass> madeChanges = new HashSet<NamedPass>();
402 |       // Contains a pass iff it was run during the last inner loop.
403 |       Set<NamedPass> runInPrevIter = new HashSet<NamedPass>();
404 |       State s = State.RUN_PASSES_NOT_RUN_IN_PREV_ITER;
405 |       boolean lastIterMadeChanges;
406 |       int count = 0;
407 | 
408 |       try {
409 |         while (true) {
410 |           if (count++ > MAX_LOOPS) {
411 |             compiler.throwInternalError(OPTIMIZE_LOOP_ERROR, null);
412 |           }
413 |           lastIterMadeChanges = false;
414 |           for (NamedPass pass : myPasses) {
415 |             if ((s == State.RUN_PASSES_NOT_RUN_IN_PREV_ITER &&
416 |                 !runInPrevIter.contains(pass)) ||
417 |                 (s == State.RUN_PASSES_THAT_CHANGED_STH_IN_PREV_ITER &&
418 |                     madeChanges.contains(pass))) {
419 |               timestamp++;
420 |               currentPass = pass;
421 |               pass.process(externs, root);
422 |               runInPrevIter.add(pass);
423 |               lastRuns.put(pass, timestamp);
424 |               if (hasHaltingErrors()) {
425 |                 return;
426 |               } else if (scopeHandler.hasCodeChangedSinceLastCall()) {
427 |                 madeChanges.add(pass);
428 |                 lastIterMadeChanges = true;
429 |               } else {
430 |                 madeChanges.remove(pass);
431 |               }
432 |             } else {
433 |               runInPrevIter.remove(pass);
434 |             }
435 |           }
436 |           if (s == State.RUN_PASSES_NOT_RUN_IN_PREV_ITER) {
437 |             if (lastIterMadeChanges) {
438 |               s = State.RUN_PASSES_THAT_CHANGED_STH_IN_PREV_ITER;
439 |             } else {
440 |               return;
441 |             }
442 |           } else if (!lastIterMadeChanges) {
443 |             s = State.RUN_PASSES_NOT_RUN_IN_PREV_ITER;
444 |           }
445 |         }
446 |       } finally {
447 |         inLoop = false;
448 |         compiler.removeChangeHandler(scopeHandler);
449 |       }
450 |     }
