===== M0815 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowGraph.java
Original range: 159-205
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if n should be represented by a new CFG node in the control
   * flow graph.
   */
Method code:
159 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
160 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
161 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
162 |       case Token.BLOCK:
163 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
164 |       case Token.TRY:
165 |         return true;
166 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
167 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
168 |         // bleeds into the local scope and parameters are assigned
169 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
170 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
171 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
172 |         // control is going into the function's body, represented by the second
173 |         // child.
174 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
175 |       case Token.WHILE:
176 |       case Token.DO:
177 |       case Token.IF:
178 |         // These control structures are represented by a node that holds the
179 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
180 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
181 | 
182 |       case Token.FOR:
183 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structures in that
184 |         // it has an initialization and an increment statement. Those
185 |         // two statements have corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
186 |         // The FOR node only represents the condition check for each iteration.
187 |         // That way the following:
188 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
189 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
190 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
191 |           // TODO(user): Investigate how we should handle the case where
192 |           // we have a very complex expression inside the FOR-IN header.
193 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
194 |         } else {
195 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
196 |         }
197 |       case Token.SWITCH:
198 |       case Token.CASE:
199 |       case Token.CATCH:
200 |       case Token.WITH:
201 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
202 |       default:
203 |         return false;
204 |     }
205 |   }

169 |     @Override
170 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
171 |       if (!n.isCall() || !n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
172 |         return;
173 |       }
174 | 
175 |       Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
176 |       String callName = callTarget.getString();
177 | 
178 |       if (startMarkerName.equals(callName)) {
179 |         if (!parent.isExprResult()) {
180 |           compiler.report(
181 |               t.makeError(n, INVALID_MARKER_USAGE, startMarkerName));
182 |           return;
183 |         }
184 |         markerStack.push(parent);
185 |         return;
186 |       }
187 | 
188 |       if (!endMarkerName.equals(callName)) {
189 |         return;
190 |       }
191 | 
192 |       Node endMarkerNode = parent;
193 |       if (!endMarkerNode.isExprResult()) {
194 |         compiler.report(
195 |             t.makeError(n, INVALID_MARKER_USAGE, endMarkerName));
196 |         return;
197 |       }
198 | 
199 |       if (markerStack.isEmpty()) {
200 |         compiler.report(t.makeError(n, UNMATCHED_END_MARKER,
201 |             startMarkerName, endMarkerName));
202 |         return;
203 |       }
204 | 
205 |       Node startMarkerNode = markerStack.pop();
206 |       if (endMarkerNode.getParent() != startMarkerNode.getParent()) {
207 |         // The end marker isn't in the same block as the start marker.
208 |         compiler.report(t.makeError(n, UNMATCHED_END_MARKER,
209 |             startMarkerName, endMarkerName));
210 |         return;
211 |       }
212 | 
213 |       // This is a valid marker set add it to the list of markers to process.
214 |       validMarkers.add(new Marker(startMarkerNode, endMarkerNode));
215 |     }

/** Re-arrange the passes in an optimal order. */
Method code:
458 |     private void optimizePasses() {
459 |       // It's important that this ordering is deterministic, so that
460 |       // multiple compiles with the same input produce exactly the same
461 |       // results.
462 |       //
463 |       // To do this, grab any passes we recognize, and move them to the end
464 |       // in an "optimal" order.
465 |       List<NamedPass> optimalPasses = Lists.newArrayList();
466 |       for (String passName : OPTIMAL_ORDER) {
467 |         for (NamedPass pass : myPasses) {
468 |           if (pass.name.equals(passName)) {
469 |             optimalPasses.add(pass);
470 |             break;
471 |           }
472 |         }
473 |       }
474 | 
475 |       myPasses.removeAll(optimalPasses);
476 |       myPasses.addAll(optimalPasses);
477 |     }

/**
     * Replace the provide statement.
     *
     * If we're providing a name with no definition, then create one.
     * If we're providing a name with a duplicate definition, then make sure
     * that definition becomes a declaration.
     */
Method code:
963 |     void replace() {
964 |       if (firstNode == null) {
965 |         // Don't touch the base case ('goog').
966 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
967 |         return;
968 |       }
969 | 
970 |       // Handle the case where there is a duplicate definition for an explicitly
971 |       // provided symbol.
972 |       if (candidateDefinition != null && explicitNode != null) {
973 |         explicitNode.detachFromParent();
974 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
975 | 
976 |         // Does this need a VAR keyword?
977 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
978 |         if (candidateDefinition.isExprResult() &&
979 |             !candidateDefinition.getFirstChild().isQualifiedName()) {
980 |           candidateDefinition.putBooleanProp(Node.IS_NAMESPACE, true);
981 |           Node assignNode = candidateDefinition.getFirstChild();
982 |           Node nameNode = assignNode.getFirstChild();
983 |           if (nameNode.isName()) {
984 |             // Need to convert this assign to a var declaration.
985 |             Node valueNode = nameNode.getNext();
986 |             assignNode.removeChild(nameNode);
987 |             assignNode.removeChild(valueNode);
988 |             nameNode.addChildToFront(valueNode);
989 |             Node varNode = IR.var(nameNode);
990 |             varNode.copyInformationFrom(candidateDefinition);
991 |             candidateDefinition.getParent().replaceChild(
992 |                 candidateDefinition, varNode);
993 |             nameNode.setJSDocInfo(assignNode.getJSDocInfo());
994 |             compiler.reportCodeChange();
995 |             replacementNode = varNode;
996 |           }
997 |         }
998 |       } else {
999 |         // Handle the case where there's not a duplicate definition.
1000 |         replacementNode = createDeclarationNode();
1001 |         if (firstModule == minimumModule) {
1002 |           firstNode.getParent().addChildBefore(replacementNode, firstNode);
1003 |         } else {
1004 |           // In this case, the name was implicitly provided by two independent
1005 |           // modules. We need to move this code up to a common module.
1006 |           int indexOfDot = namespace.lastIndexOf('.');
1007 |           if (indexOfDot == -1) {
1008 |             // Any old place is fine.
1009 |             compiler.getNodeForCodeInsertion(minimumModule)
1010 |                 .addChildToBack(replacementNode);
1011 |           } else {
1012 |             // Add it after the parent namespace.
1013 |             ProvidedName parentName =
1014 |                 providedNames.get(namespace.substring(0, indexOfDot));
1015 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(parentName);
1016 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(parentName.replacementNode);
1017 |             parentName.replacementNode.getParent().addChildAfter(
1018 |                 replacementNode, parentName.replacementNode);
1019 |           }
1020 |         }
1021 |         if (explicitNode != null) {
1022 |           explicitNode.detachFromParent();
1023 |         }
1024 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
1025 |       }
1026 |     }

Method code:
399 |   void setPrototypeBasedOn(ObjectType baseType, Node propertyNode) {
400 |     // This is a bit weird. We need to successfully handle these
401 |     // two cases:
402 |     // Foo.prototype = new Bar();
403 |     // and
404 |     // Foo.prototype = {baz: 3};
405 |     // In the first case, we do not want new properties to get
406 |     // added to Bar. In the second case, we do want new properties
407 |     // to get added to the type of the anonymous object.
408 |     //
409 |     // We handle this by breaking it into two cases:
410 |     //
411 |     // In the first case, we create a new PrototypeObjectType and set
412 |     // its implicit prototype to the type being assigned. This ensures
413 |     // that Bar will not get any properties of Foo.prototype, but properties
414 |     // later assigned to Bar will get inherited properly.
415 |     //
416 |     // In the second case, we just use the anonymous object as the prototype.
417 |     if (baseType.hasReferenceName() ||
418 |         isNativeObjectType() ||
419 |         baseType.isFunctionPrototypeType()) {
420 |       baseType = new PrototypeObjectType(
421 |           registry, getReferenceName() + ".prototype", baseType);
422 |     }
423 |     setPrototype(baseType, propertyNode);
424 |   }

/**
   * Gets all the dependencies of the given roots. The inputs must be returned
   * in a stable order. In other words, if A comes before B, and A does not
   * transitively depend on B, then A must also come before B in the returned
   * list.
   *
   * @param sorted If true, get them in topologically sorted order. If false,
   *     get them in the original order they were passed to the compiler.
   */
Method code:
210 |   public List<INPUT> getDependenciesOf(List<INPUT> roots, boolean sorted) {
211 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(inputs.containsAll(roots));
212 |     Set<INPUT> included = Sets.newHashSet();
213 |     Deque<INPUT> worklist = new ArrayDeque<INPUT>(roots);
214 |     while (!worklist.isEmpty()) {
215 |       INPUT current = worklist.pop();
216 |       if (included.add(current)) {
217 |         for (String req : current.getRequires()) {
218 |           INPUT dep = provideMap.get(req);
219 |           if (dep != null) {
220 |             worklist.add(dep);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |     }
225 | 
226 |     ImmutableList.Builder<INPUT> builder = ImmutableList.builder();
227 |     for (INPUT current : (sorted ? sortedList : inputs)) {
228 |       if (included.contains(current)) {
229 |         builder.add(current);
230 |       }
231 |     }
232 |     return builder.build();

   * FunctionType := 'function' FunctionSignatureType
   * FunctionSignatureType :=
   *    TypeParameters '(' 'this' ':' TypeName, ParametersType ')' ResultType
   */

1885 |   private Node parseFunctionType(JsDocToken token) {
1886 |     // NOTE(nicksantos): We're not implementing generics at the moment, so
1887 |     // just throw out TypeParameters.
1888 |     if (token != JsDocToken.LP) {
1889 |       restoreLookAhead(token);
1890 |       return reportTypeSyntaxWarning("msg.jsdoc.missing.lp");
1891 |     }
1892 | 
1893 |     Node functionType = newNode(Token.FUNCTION);
1894 |     Node parameters = null;
1895 |     skipEOLs();
1896 |     if (!match(JsDocToken.RP)) {
1897 |       token = next();
1898 | 
1899 |       boolean hasParams = true;
1900 |       if (token == JsDocToken.STRING) {
1901 |         String tokenStr = stream.getString();
1902 |         boolean isThis = "this".equals(tokenStr);
1903 |         boolean isNew = "new".equals(tokenStr);
1904 |         if (isThis || isNew) {
1905 |           if (match(JsDocToken.COLON)) {
1906 |             next();
1907 |             skipEOLs();
1908 |             Node contextType = wrapNode(
1909 |                 isThis ? Token.THIS : Token.NEW,
1910 |                 parseTypeName(next()));
1911 |             if (contextType == null) {
1912 |               return null;
1913 |             }
1914 | 
1915 |             functionType.addChildToFront(contextType);
1916 |           } else {
1917 |             return reportTypeSyntaxWarning("msg.jsdoc.missing.colon");
1918 |           }
1919 | 
1920 |           if (match(JsDocToken.COMMA)) {
1921 |             next();
1922 |             skipEOLs();
1923 |             token = next();
1924 |           } else {
1925 |             hasParams = false;
1926 |           }
1927 |         }
1928 |       }
1929 | 
1930 |       if (hasParams) {
1931 |         parameters = parseParametersType(token);
1932 |         if (parameters == null) {
1933 |           return null;
1934 |         }
1935 |       }
1936 |     }
1937 | 
1938 |     if (parameters != null) {
1939 |       functionType.addChildToBack(parameters);
1940 |     }
1941 | 
1942 |     skipEOLs();

1945 |     }

===== M0900 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SuppressDocWarningsGuard.level(JSError)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SuppressDocWarningsGuard.java
Original range: 51-101
Documentation:

Method code:
51 |   @Override
52 |   public CheckLevel level(JSError error) {
53 |     Node node = error.node;
54 |     if (node != null) {
55 |       boolean visitedFunction = false;
56 |       for (Node current = node;
57 |            current != null;
58 |            current = current.getParent()) {
59 |         int type = current.getType();
60 |         JSDocInfo info = null;
61 | 
62 |         if (type == Token.FUNCTION) {
63 |           info = NodeUtil.getBestJSDocInfo(current);
64 |           visitedFunction = true;
65 |         } else if (type == Token.SCRIPT) {
66 |           info = current.getJSDocInfo();
67 |         } else if (current.isVar() || current.isAssign()) {
68 |           // There's one edge case we're worried about:
69 |           // if the warning points to an assigment to a function, we
70 |           // want the suppressions on that function to apply.
71 |           // It's OK if we double-count some cases.
72 |           Node rhs = NodeUtil.getRValueOfLValue(current.getFirstChild());
73 |           if (rhs != null) {
74 |             if (rhs.isCast()) {
75 |               rhs = rhs.getFirstChild();
76 |             }
77 | 
78 |             if (rhs.isFunction() && !visitedFunction) {
79 |               info = NodeUtil.getBestJSDocInfo(current);
80 |             }
81 |           }
82 |         }
83 | 
84 |         if (info != null) {
85 |           for (String suppressor : info.getSuppressions()) {
86 |             WarningsGuard guard = suppressors.get(suppressor);
87 | 
88 |             // Some @suppress tags are for other tools, and
89 |             // may not have a warnings guard.
90 |             if (guard != null) {
91 |               CheckLevel newLevel = guard.level(error);
92 |               if (newLevel != null) {
93 |                 return newLevel;
94 |               }
95 |             }
96 |           }
97 |         }
98 |       }
99 |     }
100 |     return null;
101 |   }

===== M0917 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 217-292
Documentation:

Method code:
217 |   @Override
218 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
219 |       NodeTraversal nodeTraversal, Node n, Node parent) {
220 |     astPosition.put(n, astPositionCounter++);
221 | 
222 |     switch (n.getType()) {
223 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
224 |         if (shouldTraverseFunctions || n == cfg.getEntry().getValue()) {
225 |           exceptionHandler.push(n);
226 |           return true;
227 |         }
228 |         return false;
229 |       case Token.TRY:
230 |         exceptionHandler.push(n);
231 |         return true;
232 |     }
233 | 
234 |     /*
235 |      * We are going to stop the traversal depending on what the node's parent
236 |      * is.
237 |      *
238 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
239 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
240 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
241 |      *
242 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
243 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
244 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
245 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
246 |      *
247 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
248 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
249 |      */
250 |     if (parent != null) {
251 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
252 |         case Token.FOR:
253 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
254 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
255 | 
256 |         // Skip the conditions.
257 |         case Token.IF:
258 |         case Token.WHILE:
259 |         case Token.WITH:
260 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
261 |         case Token.DO:
262 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
263 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
264 |         case Token.SWITCH:
265 |         case Token.CASE:
266 |         case Token.CATCH:
267 |         case Token.LABEL:
268 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
269 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
270 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
271 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
272 |         case Token.BREAK:
273 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
274 |         case Token.VAR:
275 |         case Token.RETURN:
276 |         case Token.THROW:
277 |           return false;
278 |         case Token.TRY:
279 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
280 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
281 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
282 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
283 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
284 |            */
285 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
286 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
287 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
288 |           }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return true;
292 |   }

     * Parse the directives, encode them in the AST, and remove their nodes.

===== M0943 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.UnreachableCodeElimination.EliminationPass.tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/UnreachableCodeElimination.java
Original range: 128-175
Documentation:
/**
     * Tries to remove n if it is an unconditional branch node (break, continue,
     * or return) and the target of n is the same as the the follow of n.
     * That is, if removing n preserves the control flow. Also if n targets
     * another unconditional branch, this function will recursively try to
     * remove the target branch as well. The reason why we want to cascade this
     * removal is because we only run this pass once. If we have code such as
     *
     * break -> break -> break
     *
     * where all 3 breaks are useless, then the order of removal matters. When
     * we first look at the first break, we see that it branches to the 2nd
     * break. However, if we remove the last break, the 2nd break becomes
     * useless and finally the first break becomes useless as well.
     *
     * @returns The target of this jump. If the target is also useless jump,
     *     the target of that useless jump recursively.
     */
Method code:
128 |     @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
129 |     private void tryRemoveUnconditionalBranching(Node n) {
130 |       /*
131 |        * For each unconditional branching control flow node, check to see
132 |        * if the ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode of that node is same as
133 |        * the branching target. If it is, the branch node is safe to be removed.
134 |        *
135 |        * This is not as clever as MinimizeExitPoints because it doesn't do any
136 |        * if-else conversion but it handles more complicated switch statements
137 |        * much more nicely.
138 |        */
139 | 
140 |       // If n is null the target is the end of the function, nothing to do.
141 |       if (n == null) {
142 |          return;
143 |       }
144 | 
145 |       DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = cfg.getDirectedGraphNode(n);
146 | 
147 |       if (gNode == null) {
148 |         return;
149 |       }
150 | 
151 |       switch (n.getType()) {
152 |         case Token.RETURN:
153 |           if (n.hasChildren()) {
154 |             break;
155 |           }
156 |         case Token.BREAK:
157 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
158 |           // We are looking for a control flow changing statement that always
159 |           // branches to the same node. If after removing it control still
160 |           // branches to the same node, it is safe to remove.
161 |           List<DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch>> outEdges = gNode.getOutEdges();
162 |           if (outEdges.size() == 1 &&
163 |               // If there is a next node, this jump is not useless.
164 |               (n.getNext() == null || n.getNext().isFunction())) {
165 | 
166 |             Preconditions.checkState(
167 |                 outEdges.get(0).getValue() == Branch.UNCOND);
168 |             Node fallThrough = computeFollowing(n);
169 |             Node nextCfgNode = outEdges.get(0).getDestination().getValue();
170 |             if (nextCfgNode == fallThrough) {
171 |               removeNode(n);
172 |             }
173 |           }
174 |       }
175 |     }

83 |   @Override
84 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
85 |     // VOID nodes appear when there are extra semicolons at the BLOCK level.

87 |     // and apparently some people like keeping these semicolons around,
88 |     // so we'll allow it.

99 |     // these cases when we visit the child, and the peephole passes will
100 |     // fix up the tree in more clever ways when these are removed.
101 |     if (n.isExprResult() || n.isBlock()) {

115 |       String msg = "This code lacks side-effects. Is there a bug?";

121 |       }

===== M0962 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.ContextualRenameInverter.exitScope(NodeTraversal)

Original range: 313-334
Documentation:
/**
     * Rename vars for the current scope, and merge any referenced
     * names into the parent scope reference set.
     */
Method code:
313 |     @Override
314 |     public void exitScope(NodeTraversal t) {
315 |       if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
316 |         return;
317 |       }
318 | 
319 |       for (Iterator<Var> it = t.getScope().getVars(); it.hasNext();) {
320 |         Var v = it.next();
321 |         handleScopeVar(v);
322 |       }
323 | 
324 |       // Merge any names that were referenced but not declared in the current

148 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
149 |     if (colorings.isEmpty() || !n.isName() ||
150 |         parent.isFunction()) {
151 |       // Don't rename named functions.
152 |       return;
153 |     }
154 |     Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
155 |     GraphNode<Var, ?> vNode = colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(var);
156 |     if (vNode == null) {

158 |       return;
159 |     }
160 |     Var coalescedVar = colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(var);
161 |

163 |       if (vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar)) {
164 |         // The coalesced name is itself, nothing to do.
165 |         return;
166 |       }
167 | 
168 |       // Rename.
169 |       n.setString(coalescedVar.name);
170 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();

174 |       }
175 |     } else {
176 |       // This code block is slow but since usePseudoName is for debugging,
177 |       // we should not sacrifice performance for non-debugging compilation to
178 |       // make this fast.
179 |       String pseudoName = null;
180 |       Set<String> allMergedNames = Sets.newTreeSet();
181 |       for (Iterator<Var> i = t.getScope().getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
182 |         Var iVar = i.next();
183 | 
184 |         // Look for all the variables that can be merged (in the graph by now)
185 |         // and it is merged with the current coalescedVar.
186 |         if (colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(iVar) != null &&
187 |             coalescedVar.equals(colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(iVar))) {
188 |           allMergedNames.add(iVar.name);
189 |         }
190 |       }
191 | 
192 |       // Keep its original name.
193 |       if (allMergedNames.size() == 1) {
194 |         return;
195 |       }
196 | 
197 |       pseudoName = Joiner.on("_").join(allMergedNames);
198 | 
199 |       while (t.getScope().isDeclared(pseudoName, true)) {
200 |         pseudoName += "$";
201 |       }
202 | 
203 |       n.setString(pseudoName);
204 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
205 | 
206 |       if (!vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar) && parent.isVar()) {
207 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
208 |       }
209 |     }

434 |   private Collection<CompilerInput> createEntryPointInputs(
435 |       DependencyOptions depOptions,
436 |       List<CompilerInput> inputs,
437 |       SortedDependencies<CompilerInput> sorter)
438 |       throws MissingModuleException, MissingProvideException {
439 |     Set<CompilerInput> entryPointInputs = Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
440 |     Map<String, JSModule> modulesByName = getModulesByName();
441 | 
442 |     if (depOptions.shouldPruneDependencies()) {
443 |       if (!depOptions.shouldDropMoochers()) {
444 |         entryPointInputs.addAll(sorter.getInputsWithoutProvides());
445 |       }
446 | 
447 |       for (String entryPoint : depOptions.getEntryPoints()) {
448 |         // An entry point is either formatted as:
449 |         // 'foo.bar' - peg foo.bar to its current module
450 |         // 'modC:foo.bar' - peg foo.bar to modC
451 |         String inputName = entryPoint;
452 |         int splitPoint = entryPoint.indexOf(':');
453 |         CompilerInput entryPointInput = null;
454 |         if (splitPoint != -1) {
455 |           String moduleName = entryPoint.substring(0, splitPoint);
456 |           inputName = entryPoint.substring(
457 |               Math.min(splitPoint + 1, entryPoint.length() - 1));
458 |           JSModule module = modulesByName.get(moduleName);
459 |           if (module == null) {
460 |             throw new MissingModuleException(moduleName);
461 |           } else {
462 |             entryPointInput = sorter.getInputProviding(inputName);
463 |             entryPointInput.overrideModule(module);
464 |           }
465 |         } else {
466 |           entryPointInput = sorter.getInputProviding(inputName);
467 |         }
468 | 
469 |         entryPointInputs.add(entryPointInput);
470 |       }
471 | 
472 |       CompilerInput baseJs = sorter.maybeGetInputProviding("goog");
473 |       if (baseJs != null) {
474 |         entryPointInputs.add(baseJs);
475 |       }
476 |     } else {
477 |       entryPointInputs.addAll(inputs);
478 |     }
479 |     return entryPointInputs;
480 |   }

/**
   * Parses a line of JavaScript, extracting goog.provide and goog.require
   * information.

Method code:
137 |   @Override
138 |   protected boolean parseLine(String line) throws ParseException {
139 |     boolean lineHasProvidesOrRequires = false;
140 | 
141 |     // Quick sanity check that will catch most cases. This is a performance
142 |     // win for people with a lot of JS.
143 |     if (line.indexOf("provide") != -1 ||
144 |         line.indexOf("require") != -1 ||
145 |         line.indexOf("addDependency") != -1) {
146 |       // Iterate over the provides/requires.
147 |       googMatcher.reset(line);
148 |       while (googMatcher.find()) {
149 |         lineHasProvidesOrRequires = true;
150 | 
151 |         if (includeGoogBase && !fileHasProvidesOrRequires) {
152 |           fileHasProvidesOrRequires = true;
153 |           requires.add("goog");
154 |         }
155 | 
156 |         // See if it's a require or provide.
157 |         char firstChar = googMatcher.group(1).charAt(0);
158 |         boolean isProvide = firstChar == 'p';
159 |         boolean isRequire = firstChar == 'r';
160 | 
161 |         if (isProvide || isRequire) {
162 |           // Parse the param.
163 |           String arg = parseJsString(googMatcher.group(2));
164 | 
165 |           // Add the dependency.
166 |           if (isRequire) {
167 |             // goog is always implicit.
168 |             // TODO(nicksantos): I'm pretty sure we don't need this anymore.
169 |             // Remove this later.
170 |             if (!"goog".equals(arg)) {
171 |               requires.add(arg);
172 |             }
173 |           } else {
174 |             provides.add(arg);
175 |           }
176 |         }
177 |       }
178 |     } else if (includeGoogBase && line.startsWith(BASE_JS_START) &&
179 |                provides.isEmpty() && requires.isEmpty()) {
180 |       provides.add("goog");
181 | 
182 |       // base.js can't provide or require anything else.
183 |       return false;
184 |     }
185 | 
186 |     return !shortcutMode || lineHasProvidesOrRequires ||
187 |         CharMatcher.WHITESPACE.matchesAllOf(line);
188 |   }

/**
   * @param n The node in question.
   * @param cfgNode The node to add
   * @param conditional true if the definition is not always executed.
   */
Method code:
223 |   private void computeMustDef(
224 |       Node n, Node cfgNode, MustDef output, boolean conditional) {
225 |     switch (n.getType()) {
226 | 
227 |       case Token.BLOCK:
228 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
229 |         return;
230 | 
231 |       case Token.WHILE:
232 |       case Token.DO:
233 |       case Token.IF:
234 |         computeMustDef(
235 |             NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
236 |         return;
237 | 
238 |       case Token.FOR:
239 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
240 |           computeMustDef(
241 |               NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(n), cfgNode, output, conditional);
242 |         } else {
243 |           // for(x in y) {...}
244 |           Node lhs = n.getFirstChild();
245 |           Node rhs = lhs.getNext();
246 |           if (lhs.isVar()) {
247 |             lhs = lhs.getLastChild(); // for(var x in y) {...}
248 |           }
249 |           if (lhs.isName()) {
250 |             addToDefIfLocal(lhs.getString(), cfgNode, rhs, output);
251 |           }
252 |         }
253 |         return;
254 | 
255 |       case Token.AND:
256 |       case Token.OR:
257 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
258 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
259 |         return;
260 | 
261 |       case Token.HOOK:
262 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
263 |         computeMustDef(n.getFirstChild().getNext(), cfgNode, output, true);
264 |         computeMustDef(n.getLastChild(), cfgNode, output, true);
265 |         return;
266 | 
267 |       case Token.VAR:
268 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
269 |           if (c.hasChildren()) {
270 |             computeMustDef(c.getFirstChild(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
271 |             addToDefIfLocal(c.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
272 |                 c.getFirstChild(), output);
273 |           }
274 |         }
275 |         return;
276 | 
277 |       default:
278 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n)) {
279 |           if (n.getFirstChild().isName()) {
280 |             Node name = n.getFirstChild();
281 |             computeMustDef(name.getNext(), cfgNode, output, conditional);
282 |             addToDefIfLocal(name.getString(), conditional ? null : cfgNode,
283 |               n.getLastChild(), output);
284 |             return;
285 |           } else if (NodeUtil.isGet(n.getFirstChild())) {
286 |             // Treat all assignments to arguments as redefining the
287 |             // parameters itself.
288 |             Node obj = n.getFirstChild().getFirstChild();
289 |             if (obj.isName() && "arguments".equals(obj.getString())) {
290 |               // TODO(user): More accuracy can be introduced
291 |               // i.e. We know exactly what arguments[x] is if x is a constant
292 |               // number.
293 |               escapeParameters(output);
294 |             }
295 |           }
296 |         }
297 | 
298 |         if (n.isName() && "arguments".equals(n.getString())) {
299 |           escapeParameters(output);
300 |         }
301 | 
302 |         // DEC and INC actually defines the variable.
303 |         if (n.isDec() || n.isInc()) {
304 |           Node target = n.getFirstChild();
305 |           if (target.isName()) {
306 |             addToDefIfLocal(target.getString(),
307 |                 conditional ? null : cfgNode, null, output);
308 |             return;
309 |           }
310 |         }
311 | 
312 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
313 |           computeMustDef(c, cfgNode, output, conditional);
314 |         }
315 |     }
316 |   }

   * BasicTypeExpression := '*' | 'null' | 'undefined' | TypeName

Method code:
1811 |   private Node parseBasicTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1812 |     if (token == JsDocToken.STAR) {

1816 |       return parseArrayType(next());
1817 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.LC) {

1819 |       return parseRecordType(next());
1820 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.LP) {
1821 |       skipEOLs();
1822 |       return parseUnionType(next());

1826 |         skipEOLs();

1828 |       } else if ("null".equals(string) || "undefined".equals(string)) {
1829 |         return newStringNode(string);
1830 |       } else {
1831 |         return parseTypeName(token);
1832 |       }

===== M1004 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.deps.SortedDependencies.topologicalStableSort(List<T>,Multimap<T, T>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/deps/SortedDependencies.java
Original range: 239-288
Documentation:

Method code:
239 |   private static <T> List<T> topologicalStableSort(
240 |       List<T> items, Multimap<T, T> deps) {
241 |     if (items.size() == 0) {
242 |       // Priority queue blows up if we give it a size of 0. Since we need
243 |       // to special case this either way, just bail out.
244 |       return Lists.newArrayList();
245 |     }
246 | 
247 |     final Map<T, Integer> originalIndex = Maps.newHashMap();
248 |     for (int i = 0; i < items.size(); i++) {
249 |       originalIndex.put(items.get(i), i);
250 |     }
251 | 
252 |     PriorityQueue<T> inDegreeZero = new PriorityQueue<T>(items.size(),
253 |         new Comparator<T>() {
254 |       @Override
255 |       public int compare(T a, T b) {
256 |         return originalIndex.get(a).intValue() -
257 |             originalIndex.get(b).intValue();
258 |       }
259 |     });
260 |     List<T> result = Lists.newArrayList();
261 | 
262 |     Multiset<T> inDegree = HashMultiset.create();
263 |     Multimap<T, T> reverseDeps = ArrayListMultimap.create();
264 |     Multimaps.invertFrom(deps, reverseDeps);
265 | 
266 |     // First, add all the inputs with in-degree 0.
267 |     for (T item : items) {
268 |       Collection<T> itemDeps = deps.get(item);
269 |       inDegree.add(item, itemDeps.size());
270 |       if (itemDeps.isEmpty()) {
271 |         inDegreeZero.add(item);
272 |       }
273 |     }
274 | 
275 |     // Then, iterate to a fixed point over the reverse dependency graph.
276 |     while (!inDegreeZero.isEmpty()) {
277 |       T item = inDegreeZero.remove();
278 |       result.add(item);
279 |       for (T inWaiting : reverseDeps.get(item)) {
280 |         inDegree.remove(inWaiting, 1);
281 |         if (inDegree.count(inWaiting) == 0) {
282 |           inDegreeZero.add(inWaiting);
283 |         }
284 |       }
285 |     }
286 | 
287 |     return result;
288 |   }

===== M1014 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.optimizeSubtree(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 78-169
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries apply our various peephole minimizations on the passed in node.
   */
Method code:
78 |   @Override
79 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
80 |   public Node optimizeSubtree(Node node) {
81 |     switch(node.getType()) {
82 |       case Token.RETURN: {
83 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
84 |         if (result != node) {
85 |           return result;
86 |         }
87 |         result = tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
88 |         if (result != node) {
89 |           return result;
90 |         }
91 |         return tryReduceReturn(node);
92 |       }
93 | 
94 |       case Token.THROW: {
95 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
96 |         if (result != node) {
97 |           return result;
98 |         }
99 |         return tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
100 |       }
101 | 
102 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Maybe remove redundant BREAK and CONTINUE. Overlaps
103 |       // with MinimizeExitPoints.
104 | 
105 |       case Token.NOT:
106 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
107 |         return tryMinimizeNot(node);
108 | 
109 |       case Token.IF:
110 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
111 |         return tryMinimizeIf(node);
112 | 
113 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
114 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
115 |         return node;
116 | 
117 |       case Token.HOOK:
118 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
119 |         return node;
120 | 
121 |       case Token.WHILE:
122 |       case Token.DO:
123 |         tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
124 |         return node;
125 | 
126 |       case Token.FOR:
127 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(node)) {
128 |           tryJoinForCondition(node);
129 |           tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
130 |         }
131 |         return node;
132 | 
133 |       case Token.TRUE:
134 |       case Token.FALSE:
135 |         return reduceTrueFalse(node);
136 | 
137 |       case Token.NEW:
138 |         node = tryFoldStandardConstructors(node);
139 |         if (!node.isCall()) {
140 |           return node;
141 |         }
142 |         // Fall through on purpose because tryFoldStandardConstructors() may
143 |         // convert a NEW node into a CALL node
144 |       case Token.CALL:
145 |         Node result =  tryFoldLiteralConstructor(node);
146 |         if (result == node) {
147 |           result = tryFoldSimpleFunctionCall(node);
148 |           if (result == node) {
149 |             result = tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(node);
150 |           }
151 |         }
152 |         return result;
153 | 
154 |       case Token.COMMA:
155 |         return trySplitComma(node);
156 | 
157 |       case Token.NAME:
158 |         return tryReplaceUndefined(node);
159 | 
160 |       case Token.BLOCK:
161 |         return tryReplaceIf(node);
162 | 
163 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
164 |         return tryMinimizeArrayLiteral(node);
165 | 
166 |       default:
167 |         return node; //Nothing changed
168 |     }
169 |   }

===== M1017 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MinimizeExitPoints.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

47 |   @Override
48 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
49 |     switch (n.getType()) {
50 |       case Token.LABEL:
51 |         tryMinimizeExits(
52 |             n.getLastChild(), Token.BREAK, n.getFirstChild().getString());
53 |         break;
54 |

===== M1043 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 1762-1805
Documentation:
/**
   * TypeExpression := BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '?' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '!' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '?'
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '!'
   *     | '?'
   */
Method code:
1762 |   private Node parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1763 |     if (token == JsDocToken.QMARK) {
1764 |       // A QMARK could mean that a type is nullable, or that it's unknown.
1765 |       // We use look-ahead 1 to determine whether it's unknown. Otherwise,
1766 |       // we assume it means nullable. There are 5 cases:
1767 |       // {?} - right curly
1768 |       // {?=} - equals
1769 |       // {function(?, number)} - comma
1770 |       // {function(number, ?)} - right paren
1771 |       // {function(number, ...[?])} - right bracket
1772 |       // {function(): ?|number} - pipe
1773 |       // {Array.<?>} - greater than
1774 |       // I'm not a big fan of using look-ahead for this, but it makes
1775 |       // the type language a lot nicer.
1776 |       token = next();
1777 |       if (token == JsDocToken.COMMA ||
1778 |           token == JsDocToken.EQUALS ||
1779 |           token == JsDocToken.RB ||
1780 |           token == JsDocToken.RC ||
1781 |           token == JsDocToken.RP ||
1782 |           token == JsDocToken.PIPE ||
1783 |           token == JsDocToken.GT) {
1784 |         restoreLookAhead(token);
1785 |         return newNode(Token.QMARK);
1786 |       }
1787 | 
1788 |       return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, parseBasicTypeExpression(token));
1789 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.BANG) {
1790 |       return wrapNode(Token.BANG, parseBasicTypeExpression(next()));
1791 |     } else {
1792 |       Node basicTypeExpr = parseBasicTypeExpression(token);
1793 |       if (basicTypeExpr != null) {
1794 |         if (match(JsDocToken.QMARK)) {
1795 |           next();
1796 |           return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, basicTypeExpr);
1797 |         } else if (match(JsDocToken.BANG)) {
1798 |           next();
1799 |           return wrapNode(Token.BANG, basicTypeExpr);
1800 |         }
1801 |       }
1802 | 
1803 |       return basicTypeExpr;
1804 |     }
1805 |   }

Documentation:
/**
   * Use "return x?1:2;" in place of "if(x)return 1;return 2;"
   */
Method code:
306 |   private Node tryReplaceIf(Node n) {
307 | 
308 |     for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
309 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()){
310 |       if (child.isIf()){
311 |         Node cond = child.getFirstChild();
312 |         Node thenBranch = cond.getNext();
313 |         Node elseBranch = thenBranch.getNext();
314 |         Node nextNode = child.getNext();
315 | 
316 |         if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null
317 |             && isReturnBlock(thenBranch)
318 |             && nextNode.isIf()) {
319 |           Node nextCond = nextNode.getFirstChild();
320 |           Node nextThen = nextCond.getNext();
321 |           Node nextElse = nextThen.getNext();
322 |           if (thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextThen)) {
323 |             // Transform
324 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) return 1;
325 |             // to
326 |             //   if (x||y) return 1;
327 |             child.detachFromParent();
328 |             child.detachChildren();
329 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.OR, cond);
330 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
331 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
332 |             reportCodeChange();
333 |           } else if (nextElse != null
334 |               && thenBranch.isEquivalentToTyped(nextElse)) {
335 |             // Transform
336 |             //   if (x) return 1; if (y) foo() else return 1;
337 |             // to
338 |             //   if (!x&&y) foo() else return 1;
339 |             child.detachFromParent();
340 |             child.detachChildren();
341 |             Node newCond = new Node(Token.AND,
342 |                 IR.not(cond).srcref(cond));
343 |             nextNode.replaceChild(nextCond, newCond);
344 |             newCond.addChildToBack(nextCond);
345 |             reportCodeChange();
346 |           }
347 |         } else if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null &&
348 |             isReturnBlock(thenBranch) && isReturnExpression(nextNode)) {
349 |           Node thenExpr = null;
350 |           // if(x)return; return 1 -> return x?void 0:1
351 |           if (isReturnExpressBlock(thenBranch)) {
352 |             thenExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(thenBranch);
353 |             thenExpr.detachFromParent();
354 |           } else {
355 |             thenExpr = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(child);
356 |           }
357 | 
358 |           Node elseExpr = nextNode.getFirstChild();
359 | 
360 |           cond.detachFromParent();
361 |           elseExpr.detachFromParent();
362 | 
363 |           Node returnNode = IR.returnNode(
364 |                                 IR.hook(cond, thenExpr, elseExpr)
365 |                                     .srcref(child));
366 |           n.replaceChild(child, returnNode);
367 |           n.removeChild(nextNode);
368 |           reportCodeChange();
369 |         } else if (elseBranch != null && statementMustExitParent(thenBranch)) {
370 |           child.removeChild(elseBranch);
371 |           n.addChildAfter(elseBranch, child);
372 |           reportCodeChange();
373 |         }
374 |       }

377 |   }

===== M1062 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 830-857
Documentation:
/**
   * Connects cfgNode to the proper CATCH block if target subtree might throw
   * an exception. If there are FINALLY blocks reached before a CATCH, it will
   * make the corresponding entry in finallyMap.
   */
Method code:
830 |   private void connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node cfgNode, Node target) {
831 |     if (mayThrowException(target) && !exceptionHandler.isEmpty()) {
832 |       Node lastJump = cfgNode;
833 |       for (Node handler : exceptionHandler) {
834 |         if (handler.isFunction()) {
835 |           return;
836 |         }
837 |         Preconditions.checkState(handler.isTry());
838 |         Node catchBlock = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(handler);
839 | 
840 |         if (!NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(catchBlock)) { // No catch but a FINALLY.
841 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
842 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, handler.getLastChild());
843 |           } else {
844 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, handler.getLastChild());
845 |           }
846 |         } else { // Has a catch.
847 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
848 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, catchBlock);
849 |             return;
850 |           } else {
851 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, catchBlock);
852 |           }
853 |         }
854 |         lastJump = handler;
855 |       }
856 |     }
857 |   }

Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 1165-1185

Method code:
1165 |   static String identifierEscape(String s) {
1166 |     // First check if escaping is needed at all -- in most cases it isn't.
1167 |     if (NodeUtil.isLatin(s)) {
1168 |       return s;
1169 |     }
1170 | 
1171 |     // Now going through the string to escape non-Latin characters if needed.
1172 |     StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
1173 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
1174 |       char c = s.charAt(i);
1175 |       // Identifiers should always go to Latin1/ ASCII characters because
1176 |       // different browser's rules for valid identifier characters are
1177 |       // crazy.
1178 |       if (c > 0x1F && c < 0x7F) {
1179 |         sb.append(c);
1180 |       } else {
1181 |         appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1182 |       }
1183 |     }
1184 |     return sb.toString();
1185 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryFoldLiteralConstructor(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 1369-1417
Documentation:
/**
   * Replaces a new Array or Object node with an object literal, unless the
   * call to Array or Object is to a local function with the same name.
   */
Method code:
1369 |   private Node tryFoldLiteralConstructor(Node n) {
1370 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(n.isCall()
1371 |         || n.isNew());
1372 | 
1373 |     Node constructorNameNode = n.getFirstChild();
1374 | 
1375 |     Node newLiteralNode = null;
1376 | 
1377 |     // We require the AST to be normalized to ensure that, say,
1378 |     // Object() really refers to the built-in Object constructor
1379 |     // and not a user-defined constructor with the same name.
1380 | 
1381 |     if (isASTNormalized() && Token.NAME == constructorNameNode.getType()) {
1382 | 
1383 |       String className = constructorNameNode.getString();
1384 | 
1385 |       if ("RegExp".equals(className)) {
1386 |         // "RegExp("boo", "g")" --> /boo/g
1387 |         return tryFoldRegularExpressionConstructor(n);
1388 |       } else {
1389 |         boolean constructorHasArgs = constructorNameNode.getNext() != null;
1390 | 
1391 |         if ("Object".equals(className) && !constructorHasArgs) {
1392 |           // "Object()" --> "{}"
1393 |           newLiteralNode = IR.objectlit();
1394 |         } else if ("Array".equals(className)) {
1395 |           // "Array(arg0, arg1, ...)" --> "[arg0, arg1, ...]"
1396 |           Node arg0 = constructorNameNode.getNext();
1397 |           FoldArrayAction action = isSafeToFoldArrayConstructor(arg0);
1398 | 
1399 |           if (action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITH_ARGS ||
1400 |               action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITHOUT_ARGS) {
1401 |             newLiteralNode = IR.arraylit();
1402 |             n.removeChildren();
1403 |             if (action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITH_ARGS) {
1404 |               newLiteralNode.addChildrenToFront(arg0);
1405 |             }
1406 |           }
1407 |         }
1408 | 
1409 |         if (newLiteralNode != null) {
1410 |           n.getParent().replaceChild(n, newLiteralNode);
1411 |           reportCodeChange();
1412 |           return newLiteralNode;
1413 |         }
1414 |       }
1415 |     }
1416 |     return n;
1417 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.handleStmtList(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 484-523

Method code:
484 |   private void handleStmtList(Node node) {
485 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
486 |     // Special case, don't add a block of empty CATCH block to the graph.
487 |     if (node.isBlock() && parent != null &&
488 |         parent.isTry() &&
489 |         NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node &&
490 |         !NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(node)) {
491 |       return;
492 |     }
493 | 
494 |     // A block transfer control to its first child if it is not empty.
495 |     Node child = node.getFirstChild();
496 | 
497 |     // Function declarations are skipped since control doesn't go into that
498 |     // function (unless it is called)
499 |     while (child != null && child.isFunction()) {
500 |       child = child.getNext();
501 |     }
502 | 
503 |     if (child != null) {
504 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFallThrough(child));
505 |     } else {
506 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFollowNode(node, this));
507 |     }
508 | 
509 |     // Synthetic blocks
510 |     if (parent != null) {
511 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
512 |         case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
513 |         case Token.CASE:
514 |         case Token.TRY:
515 |           break;
516 |         default:
517 |           if (node.isBlock() && node.isSyntheticBlock()) {
518 |             createEdge(node, Branch.SYN_BLOCK, computeFollowNode(node, this));
519 |           }
520 |           break;
521 |       }
522 |     }
523 |   }

===== M1117 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.UnionTypeBuilder.addAlternate(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/UnionTypeBuilder.java
Original range: 120-281
Documentation:
/**
   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
120 |   UnionTypeBuilder addAlternate(JSType alternate) {
121 |     // build() returns the bottom type by default, so we can
122 |     // just bail out early here.
123 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
124 |       return this;
125 |     }
126 | 
127 |     isAllType = isAllType || alternate.isAllType();
128 | 
129 |     boolean isAlternateUnknown = alternate instanceof UnknownType;
130 |     isNativeUnknownType = isNativeUnknownType || isAlternateUnknown;
131 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
132 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
133 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
134 |     }
135 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
136 |       if (alternate.isUnionType()) {
137 |         UnionType union = alternate.toMaybeUnionType();
138 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
139 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
140 |         }
141 |       } else {
142 |         if (alternates.size() > maxUnionSize) {
143 |           return this;
144 |         }
145 | 
146 |         // Function types are special, because they have their
147 |         // own bizarre sub-lattice. See the comments on
148 |         // FunctionType#supAndInf helper and above at functionTypePosition.
149 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType() && functionTypePosition != -1) {
150 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
151 |           FunctionType other =
152 |               alternates.get(functionTypePosition).toMaybeFunctionType();
153 |           FunctionType supremum =
154 |               alternate.toMaybeFunctionType().supAndInfHelper(other, true);
155 |           alternates.set(functionTypePosition, supremum);
156 |           result = null;
157 |           return this;
158 |         }
159 | 
160 |         // Look through the alternates we've got so far,
161 |         // and check if any of them are duplicates of
162 |         // one another.
163 |         int currentIndex = 0;
164 |         Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
165 |         while (it.hasNext()) {
166 |           boolean removeCurrent = false;
167 |           JSType current = it.next();
168 | 
169 |           // Unknown and NoResolved types may just be names that haven't
170 |           // been resolved yet. So keep these in the union, and just use
171 |           // equality checking for simple de-duping.
172 |           if (alternate.isUnknownType() ||
173 |               current.isUnknownType() ||
174 |               alternate.isNoResolvedType() ||
175 |               current.isNoResolvedType() ||
176 |               alternate.hasAnyTemplateTypes() ||
177 |               current.hasAnyTemplateTypes()) {
178 |             if (alternate.isEquivalentTo(current)) {
179 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
180 |               return this;
181 |             }
182 |           } else {
183 | 
184 |             // Because "Foo" and "Foo.<?>" are roughly equivalent
185 |             // templatized types, special care is needed when building the
186 |             // union. For example:
187 |             //   Object is consider a subtype of Object.<string>
188 |             // but we want to leave "Object" not "Object.<string>" when
189 |             // building the subtype.
190 |             //
191 | 
192 |             if (alternate.isTemplatizedType() || current.isTemplatizedType()) {
193 |               // Cases:
194 |               // 1) alternate:Array.<string> and current:Object ==> Object
195 |               // 2) alternate:Array.<string> and current:Array ==> Array
196 |               // 3) alternate:Object.<string> and
197 |               //    current:Array ==> Array|Object.<string>
198 |               // 4) alternate:Object and current:Array.<string> ==> Object
199 |               // 5) alternate:Array and current:Array.<string> ==> Array
200 |               // 6) alternate:Array and
201 |               //    current:Object.<string> ==> Array|Object.<string>
202 |               // 7) alternate:Array.<string> and
203 |               //    current:Array.<number> ==> Array.<?>
204 |               // 8) alternate:Array.<string> and
205 |               //    current:Array.<string> ==> Array.<string>
206 |               // 9) alternate:Array.<string> and
207 |               //    current:Object.<string> ==> Object.<string>|Array.<string>
208 | 
209 |               if (!current.isTemplatizedType()) {
210 |                 if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
211 |                   // case 1, 2
212 |                   return this;
213 |                 }
214 |                 // case 3: leave current, add alternate
215 |               } else if (!alternate.isTemplatizedType()) {
216 |                 if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
217 |                   // case 4, 5
218 |                   removeCurrent = true;
219 |                 }
220 |                 // case 6: leave current, add alternate
221 |               } else {
222 |                 Preconditions.checkState(current.isTemplatizedType()
223 |                     && alternate.isTemplatizedType());
224 |                 TemplatizedType templatizedAlternate = alternate.toMaybeTemplatizedType();
225 |                 TemplatizedType templatizedCurrent = current.toMaybeTemplatizedType();
226 | 
227 |                 if (templatizedCurrent.wrapsSameRawType(templatizedAlternate)) {
228 |                   if (alternate.getTemplateTypeMap().checkEquivalenceHelper(
229 |                       current.getTemplateTypeMap(),
230 |                       EquivalenceMethod.IDENTITY)) {
231 |                     // case 8
232 |                     return this;
233 |                   } else {
234 |                     // TODO(johnlenz): should we leave both types?
235 |                     // case 7: add a merged alternate
236 |                     // We currently merge to the templatized types to "unknown"
237 |                     // which is equivalent to the raw type.
238 |                     JSType merged = templatizedCurrent
239 |                         .getReferencedObjTypeInternal();
240 |                     return addAlternate(merged);
241 |                   }
242 |                 }
243 |                 // case 9: leave current, add alternate
244 |               }
245 |               // Otherwise leave both templatized types.
246 |             } else if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
247 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
248 |               return this;
249 |             } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
250 |               // Alternate makes current obsolete
251 |               removeCurrent = true;
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 | 
255 |           if (removeCurrent) {
256 |             it.remove();
257 | 
258 |             if (currentIndex == functionTypePosition) {
259 |               functionTypePosition = -1;
260 |             } else if (currentIndex < functionTypePosition) {
261 |               functionTypePosition--;
262 |               currentIndex--;
263 |             }
264 |           }
265 |           currentIndex++;
266 |         }
267 | 
268 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType()) {
269 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
270 |           Preconditions.checkState(functionTypePosition == -1);
271 |           functionTypePosition = alternates.size();
272 |         }
273 | 
274 |         alternates.add(alternate);
275 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
276 |       }
277 |     } else {
278 |       result = null;
279 |     }
280 |     return this;
281 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ShadowVariables.GatherReferenceInfo.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ShadowVariables.java
Original range: 128-168
Documentation:

Method code:
128 |     @Override
129 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
130 |       // Skipping over non-name nodes and empty function names.
131 |       if (!NodeUtil.isReferenceName(n)) {
132 |         return;
133 |       }
134 | 
135 |       // We focus on shadowing local variables as their name occurs much more
136 |       // than global names.
137 |       // TODO(user): Alternatively, we could experiment with using a local
138 |       // name to shadow a global variable.
139 |       if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
140 |         return;
141 |       }
142 | 
143 |       Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
144 |       if (var == null) {
145 |         // extern name or undefined name.
146 |         return;
147 |       }
148 | 
149 |       if (var.getScope().isGlobal()) {
150 |         // We will not shadow a global variable name.
151 |         return;
152 |       }
153 | 
154 |       // Using the definition of upward referencing, fill in the map.
155 |       if (var.getScope() != t.getScope()) {
156 |         for (Scope s = t.getScope();
157 |             s != var.getScope() && s.isLocal(); s = s.getParent()) {
158 |           scopeUpRefMap.put(s.getRootNode(), var.name);
159 |         }
160 |       }
161 | 
162 |       if (var.getScope() == t.getScope()) {
163 |         scopeUpRefMap.put(t.getScopeRoot(), var.name);
164 |       }
165 | 
166 |       // Find in the usage map that tracks a var and all of its usage.
167 |       varToNameUsage.put(var, n);
168 |     }

===== M1160 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SyntacticScopeCreator.java
Original range: 124-178
Documentation:
/**
   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node
   */
Method code:
124 |   private void scanVars(Node n) {
125 |     switch (n.getType()) {
126 |       case Token.VAR:
127 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
128 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
129 |              child != null;) {
130 |           Node next = child.getNext();
131 |           declareVar(child);
132 |           child = next;
133 |         }
134 |         return;
135 | 
136 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
137 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
138 |           return;
139 |         }
140 | 
141 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
142 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
143 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
144 |           return;
145 |         }
146 |         declareVar(n.getFirstChild());
147 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
148 | 
149 |       case Token.CATCH:
150 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
151 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().isName());
152 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
153 |         // is the code block
154 | 
155 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();
156 |         final Node block = var.getNext();
157 | 
158 |         declareVar(var);
159 |         scanVars(block);
160 |         return;  // only one child to scan
161 | 
162 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
163 |         inputId = n.getInputId();
164 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(inputId);
165 |         break;
166 |     }
167 | 
168 |     // Variables can only occur in statement-level nodes, so
169 |     // we only need to traverse children in a couple special cases.
170 |     if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(n) || NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(n)) {
171 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
172 |            child != null;) {
173 |         Node next = child.getNext();
174 |         scanVars(child);
175 |         child = next;
176 |       }
177 |     }
178 |   }

238 |     startTimeMs = clock.currentTimeMillis();

246 |         i++;
247 |       }
248 |     }
249 |

251 | 
252 |     // Do nothing if the current thread trace wasn't initialized.
253 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {
254 |       return;
255 |     }
256 | 
257 |     // Check if we are creating too many Tracers.
258 |     if (trace.events.size() >= MAX_TRACE_SIZE) {
259 |       logger.log(Level.WARNING,

261 |                     + "Clearing to avoid memory leak.",

264 |     }
265 | 
266 |     // Check if we forgot to close the Tracers.
267 |     if (trace.outstandingEvents.size() >= MAX_TRACE_SIZE) {

270 |                     + "or Tracer.stop() is not wrapped in a "
271 |                     + "try/finally block. "
272 |                     + "Clearing to avoid memory leak.",
273 |                   new Throwable(trace.toString()));

275 |     }
276 | 
277 |     trace.startEvent(this);
278 |   }

103 |   private Node tryFoldBinaryOperator(Node subtree) {
104 |     Node left = subtree.getFirstChild();
105 | 
106 |     if (left == null) {
107 |       return subtree;
108 |     }
109 | 
110 |     Node right = left.getNext();

114 |     }

116 |     // If we've reached here, node is truly a binary operator.
117 |     switch(subtree.getType()) {
118 |       case Token.GETPROP:
119 |         return tryFoldGetProp(subtree, left, right);
120 | 
121 |       case Token.GETELEM:
122 |         return tryFoldGetElem(subtree, left, right);
123 | 
124 |       case Token.INSTANCEOF:
125 |         return tryFoldInstanceof(subtree, left, right);
126 | 
127 |       case Token.AND:
128 |       case Token.OR:
129 |         return tryFoldAndOr(subtree, left, right);
130 | 
131 |       case Token.LSH:
132 |       case Token.RSH:
133 |       case Token.URSH:
134 |         return tryFoldShift(subtree, left, right);
135 | 
136 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
137 |         return tryFoldAssign(subtree, left, right);
138 | 
139 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITOR:
140 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITXOR:
141 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITAND:
142 |       case Token.ASSIGN_LSH:
143 |       case Token.ASSIGN_RSH:
144 |       case Token.ASSIGN_URSH:
145 |       case Token.ASSIGN_ADD:
146 |       case Token.ASSIGN_SUB:
147 |       case Token.ASSIGN_MUL:
148 |       case Token.ASSIGN_DIV:
149 |       case Token.ASSIGN_MOD:
150 |         return tryUnfoldAssignOp(subtree, left, right);
151 | 
152 |       case Token.ADD:

154 | 
155 |       case Token.SUB:

159 |

164 |         Node result = tryFoldArithmeticOp(subtree, left, right);
165 |         if (result != subtree) {

169 |

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.JSModuleGraph.manageDependencies(DependencyOptions,List<CompilerInput>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/JSModuleGraph.java
Original range: 367-432
Documentation:
/**
   * Apply the dependency options to the list of sources, returning a new
   * source list re-ordering and dropping files as necessary.
   * This module graph will be updated to reflect the new list.
   *
   * @param inputs The original list of sources. Used to ensure that the sort
   *     is stable.
   * @throws CircularDependencyException if there is a circular dependency
   *     between the provides and requires.
   * @throws MissingProvideException if an entry point was not provided
   *     by any of the inputs.
   * @see DependencyOptions for more info on how this works.
   */
Method code:
367 |   public List<CompilerInput> manageDependencies(
368 |       DependencyOptions depOptions,
369 |       List<CompilerInput> inputs)
370 |       throws CircularDependencyException, MissingProvideException,
371 |           MissingModuleException {
372 | 
373 |     SortedDependencies<CompilerInput> sorter =
374 |         new SortedDependencies<CompilerInput>(inputs);
375 |     Iterable<CompilerInput> entryPointInputs = createEntryPointInputs(
376 |         depOptions, inputs, sorter);
377 | 
378 |     // The order of inputs, sorted independently of modules.
379 |     List<CompilerInput> absoluteOrder =
380 |         sorter.getDependenciesOf(inputs, depOptions.shouldSortDependencies());
381 | 
382 |     // Figure out which sources *must* be in each module.
383 |     ListMultimap<JSModule, CompilerInput> entryPointInputsPerModule =
384 |         LinkedListMultimap.create();
385 |     for (CompilerInput input : entryPointInputs) {
386 |       JSModule module = input.getModule();
387 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(module);
388 |       entryPointInputsPerModule.put(module, input);
389 |     }
390 | 
391 |     // Clear the modules of their inputs. This also nulls out
392 |     // the input's reference to its module.
393 |     for (JSModule module : getAllModules()) {
394 |       module.removeAll();
395 |     }
396 | 
397 |     // Figure out which sources *must* be in each module, or in one
398 |     // of that module's dependencies.
399 |     for (JSModule module : entryPointInputsPerModule.keySet()) {
400 |       List<CompilerInput> transitiveClosure =
401 |           sorter.getDependenciesOf(
402 |               entryPointInputsPerModule.get(module),
403 |               depOptions.shouldSortDependencies());
404 |       for (CompilerInput input : transitiveClosure) {
405 |         JSModule oldModule = input.getModule();
406 |         if (oldModule == null) {
407 |           input.setModule(module);
408 |         } else {
409 |           input.setModule(null);
410 |           input.setModule(
411 |               getDeepestCommonDependencyInclusive(oldModule, module));
412 |         }
413 |       }
414 |     }
415 | 
416 |     // All the inputs are pointing to the modules that own them. Yeah!
417 |     // Update the modules to reflect this.
418 |     for (CompilerInput input : absoluteOrder) {
419 |       JSModule module = input.getModule();
420 |       if (module != null) {
421 |         module.add(input);
422 |       }
423 |     }
424 | 
425 |     // Now, generate the sorted result.
426 |     List<CompilerInput> result = Lists.newArrayList();
427 |     for (JSModule module : getAllModules()) {
428 |       result.addAll(module.getInputs());
429 |     }
430 | 
431 |     return result;
432 |   }

Method code:
89 |   public JSModuleGraph(List<JSModule> modulesInDepOrder) {
90 |     Preconditions.checkState(
91 |         modulesInDepOrder.size() == Sets.newHashSet(modulesInDepOrder).size(),
92 |         "Found duplicate modules");

104 |               module, dep);
105 |         }

107 |       }
108 |

110 |       if (depth == modulesByDepth.size()) {
111 |         modulesByDepth.add(new ArrayList<JSModule>());
112 |       }
113 |       modulesByDepth.get(depth).add(module);
114 |     }

106 |   @Override
107 |   public void hotSwapScript(Node root, Node originalRoot) {
108 |     Traversal traversal = new Traversal();
109 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, traversal);
110 | 
111 |     if (!traversal.hasErrors()) {
112 | 
113 |       // Apply the aliases.
114 |       for (AliasUsage aliasUsage : traversal.getAliasUsages()) {
115 |         aliasUsage.applyAlias();
116 |       }
117 | 
118 |       // Remove the alias definitions.
119 |       for (Node aliasDefinition : traversal.getAliasDefinitionsInOrder()) {
120 |         if (aliasDefinition.getParent().isVar() &&
121 |             aliasDefinition.getParent().hasOneChild()) {
122 |           aliasDefinition.getParent().detachFromParent();
123 |         } else {
124 |           aliasDefinition.detachFromParent();
125 |         }
126 |       }
127 | 
128 |       // Collapse the scopes.
129 |       for (Node scopeCall : traversal.getScopeCalls()) {
130 |         Node expressionWithScopeCall = scopeCall.getParent();
131 |         Node scopeClosureBlock = scopeCall.getLastChild().getLastChild();
132 |         scopeClosureBlock.detachFromParent();
133 |         expressionWithScopeCall.getParent().replaceChild(
134 |             expressionWithScopeCall,
135 |             scopeClosureBlock);
136 |         NodeUtil.tryMergeBlock(scopeClosureBlock);
137 |       }
138 | 
139 |       if (traversal.getAliasUsages().size() > 0 ||
140 |           traversal.getAliasDefinitionsInOrder().size() > 0 ||
141 |           traversal.getScopeCalls().size() > 0) {
142 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
143 |       }
144 |     }
145 |   }

205 |   private void regenerateDependencyInfoIfNecessary() throws IOException {
206 |     // If the code is NOT a JsAst, then it was not originally JS code.

/**
   * Traverses the current scope and collects declared names.  Does not
   * decent into functions or add CATCH exceptions.
   */
Method code:
212 |   private void findDeclaredNames(Node n, Node parent, Renamer renamer) {
213 |     // Do a shallow traversal, so don't traverse into function declarations,
214 |     // except for the name of the function itself.
215 |     if (parent == null
216 |         || !parent.isFunction()
217 |         || n == parent.getFirstChild()) {
218 |       if (NodeUtil.isVarDeclaration(n)) {
219 |         renamer.addDeclaredName(n.getString());
220 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
221 |         Node nameNode = n.getFirstChild();
222 |         renamer.addDeclaredName(nameNode.getString());
223 |       }
224 | 
225 |       for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
226 |         findDeclaredNames(c, n, renamer);
227 |       }
228 |     }
229 |   }

/**
   * Finds all defines, and creates a {@link DefineInfo} data structure for
   * each one.
   * @return A map of {@link DefineInfo} structures, keyed by name.
   */
Method code:
172 |   private Map<String, DefineInfo> collectDefines(Node root,
173 |       GlobalNamespace namespace) {
174 |     // Find all the global names with a @define annotation
175 |     List<Name> allDefines = Lists.newArrayList();
176 |     for (Name name : namespace.getNameIndex().values()) {
177 |       Ref decl = name.getDeclaration();
178 |       if (name.docInfo != null && name.docInfo.isDefine()) {
179 |         // Process defines should not depend on check types being enabled,
180 |         // so we look for the JSDoc instead of the inferred type.
181 |         if (isValidDefineType(name.docInfo.getType())) {
182 |           allDefines.add(name);
183 |         } else {
184 |           JSError error = JSError.make(
185 |               decl.getSourceName(),
186 |               decl.node, INVALID_DEFINE_TYPE_ERROR);
187 |           compiler.report(error);
188 |         }
189 |       } else {
190 |         for (Ref ref : name.getRefs()) {
191 |           if (ref == decl) {
192 |             // Declarations were handled above.
193 |             continue;
194 |           }
195 | 
196 |           Node n = ref.node;
197 |           Node parent = ref.node.getParent();
198 |           JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
199 |           if (info == null &&
200 |               parent.isVar() && parent.hasOneChild()) {
201 |             info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
202 |           }
203 | 
204 |           if (info != null && info.isDefine()) {
205 |             allDefines.add(name);
206 |             break;
207 |           }
208 |         }
209 |       }
210 |     }
211 | 
212 |     CollectDefines pass = new CollectDefines(compiler, allDefines);
213 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, pass);
214 |     return pass.getAllDefines();

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ClosureCodingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ClosureCodingConvention.java
Original range: 94-153
Documentation:
/**
   * {@inheritDoc}
   *
   * <p>Understands several different inheritance patterns that occur in
   * Google code (various uses of {@code inherits} and {@code mixin}).
   */
Method code:
94 |   @Override
95 |   public SubclassRelationship getClassesDefinedByCall(Node callNode) {
96 |     SubclassRelationship relationship =
97 |         super.getClassesDefinedByCall(callNode);
98 |     if (relationship != null) return relationship;
99 | 
100 |     Node callName = callNode.getFirstChild();
101 |     SubclassType type = typeofClassDefiningName(callName);
102 |     if (type != null) {
103 |       Node subclass = null;
104 |       Node superclass = callNode.getLastChild();
105 | 
106 |       // There are six possible syntaxes for a class-defining method:
107 |       // SubClass.inherits(SuperClass)
108 |       // goog.inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
109 |       // goog$inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
110 |       // SubClass.mixin(SuperClass.prototype)
111 |       // goog.mixin(SubClass.prototype, SuperClass.prototype)
112 |       // goog$mixin(SubClass.prototype, SuperClass.prototype)
113 |       boolean isDeprecatedCall = callNode.getChildCount() == 2 &&
114 |           callName.isGetProp();
115 |       if (isDeprecatedCall) {
116 |         // SubClass.inherits(SuperClass)
117 |         subclass = callName.getFirstChild();
118 |       } else if (callNode.getChildCount() == 3) {
119 |         // goog.inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)
120 |         subclass = callName.getNext();
121 |       } else {
122 |         return null;
123 |       }
124 | 
125 |       if (type == SubclassType.MIXIN) {
126 |         // Only consider mixins that mix two prototypes as related to
127 |         // inheritance.
128 |         if (!endsWithPrototype(superclass)) {
129 |           return null;
130 |         }
131 |         if (!isDeprecatedCall) {
132 |           if (!endsWithPrototype(subclass)) {
133 |             return null;
134 |           }
135 |           // Strip off the prototype from the name.
136 |           subclass = subclass.getFirstChild();
137 |         }
138 |         superclass = superclass.getFirstChild();
139 |       }
140 | 
141 |       // bail out if either of the side of the "inherits"
142 |       // isn't a real class name. This prevents us from
143 |       // doing something weird in cases like:
144 |       // goog.inherits(MySubClass, cond ? SuperClass1 : BaseClass2)
145 |       if (subclass != null &&
146 |           subclass.isUnscopedQualifiedName() &&
147 |           superclass.isUnscopedQualifiedName()) {
148 |         return new SubclassRelationship(type, subclass, superclass);
149 |       }
150 |     }
151 | 
152 |     return null;
153 |   }

/**
     * Transforms the given node and then sets its type to Token.STRING if it
     * was Token.NAME. If its type was already Token.STRING, then quotes it.
     * Used for properties, as the old AST uses String tokens, while the new one
     * uses Name tokens for unquoted strings. For example, in
     * var o = {'a' : 1, b: 2};
     * the string 'a' is quoted, while the name b is turned into a string, but
     * unquoted.
     */
Method code:
537 |     private Node transformAsString(AstNode n) {
538 |       Node ret;
539 |       if (n instanceof Name) {
540 |         ret = transformNameAsString((Name)n);
541 |       } else if (n instanceof NumberLiteral) {
542 |         ret = transformNumberAsString((NumberLiteral)n);
543 |         ret.putBooleanProp(Node.QUOTED_PROP, true);
544 |       } else {
545 |         ret = transform(n);
546 |         ret.putBooleanProp(Node.QUOTED_PROP, true);
547 |       }
548 |       Preconditions.checkState(ret.isString());
549 |       return ret;
550 |     }
