/**
   * Traversal for passes that work only on changed functions.
   * Suppose a loopable pass P1 uses this traversal.
   * Then, if a function doesn't change between two runs of P1, it won't look at
   * the function the second time.
   * (We're assuming that P1 runs to a fixpoint, o/w we may miss optimizations.)
   */
Method code:
464 |   public static void traverseChangedFunctions(
465 |       AbstractCompiler compiler, FunctionCallback callback) {
466 |     final AbstractCompiler comp = compiler;
467 |     final FunctionCallback cb = callback;
468 |     final Node jsRoot = comp.getJsRoot();
469 |     if (comp.hasScopeChanged(jsRoot)) {
470 |       cb.visit(comp, jsRoot);
471 |     }
472 |     traverse(comp, jsRoot,
473 |         new AbstractPreOrderCallback() {
474 |           @Override
475 |           public final boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node p) {
476 |             if (n.isFunction() && comp.hasScopeChanged(n)) {
477 |               cb.visit(comp, n);
478 |             }
479 |             return true;
480 |           }
481 |         });
482 |   }

120 |   @Override
121 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
122 |     if (!n.isName()) {
123 |       return;
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     String varName = n.getString();
127 | 
128 |     // Only a function can have an empty name.
129 |     if (varName.isEmpty()) {
130 |       Preconditions.checkState(parent.isFunction());
131 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent));
132 |       return;
133 |     }
134 | 
135 |     // Check if this is a declaration for a var that has been declared
136 |     // elsewhere. If so, mark it as a duplicate.
137 |     if ((parent.isVar() ||
138 |          NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent)) &&
139 |         varsToDeclareInExterns.contains(varName)) {
140 |       createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
141 | 
142 |       n.addSuppression("duplicate");
143 |     }
144 | 
145 |     // Check that the var has been declared.
146 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
147 |     Scope.Var var = scope.getVar(varName);
148 |     if (var == null) {
149 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
150 |         // e.g. [ function foo() {} ], it's okay if "foo" isn't defined in the
151 |         // current scope.
152 |       } else {
153 |         // The extern checks are stricter, don't report a second error.
154 |         if (!strictExternCheck || !t.getInput().isExtern()) {
155 |           t.report(n, UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR, varName);
156 |         }
157 | 
158 |         if (sanityCheck) {
159 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected variable " + varName);
160 |         } else {
161 |           createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
162 |           scope.getGlobalScope().declare(varName, n,
163 |               null, getSynthesizedExternsInput());
164 |         }
165 |       }
166 |       return;
167 |     }
168 | 
169 |     CompilerInput currInput = t.getInput();
170 |     CompilerInput varInput = var.input;
171 |     if (currInput == varInput || currInput == null || varInput == null) {
172 |       // The variable was defined in the same file. This is fine.
173 |       return;
174 |     }
175 | 
176 |     // Check module dependencies.
177 |     JSModule currModule = currInput.getModule();
178 |     JSModule varModule = varInput.getModule();
179 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
180 |     if (!sanityCheck &&
181 |         varModule != currModule && varModule != null && currModule != null) {
182 |       if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(currModule, varModule)) {
183 |         // The module dependency was properly declared.
184 |       } else {
185 |         if (scope.isGlobal()) {
186 |           if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(varModule, currModule)) {
187 |             // The variable reference violates a declared module dependency.
188 |             t.report(n, VIOLATED_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
189 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
190 |           } else {
191 |             // The variable reference is between two modules that have no
192 |             // dependency relationship. This should probably be considered an
193 |             // error, but just issue a warning for now.
194 |             t.report(n, MISSING_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
195 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
196 |           }
197 |         } else {
198 |           t.report(n, STRICT_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
199 |                    currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
200 |         }
201 |       }
202 |     }
203 |   }

514 |     @Override

517 |       if (!preferLineBreakAtEndOfFile) {
518 |         return;
519 |       }
520 |       if (lineLength > lineLengthThreshold / 2) {

33 |   Node optimizeSubtree(Node subtree) {
34 |     // if the operator is symmetric
35 |     if (NodeUtil.isSymmetricOperation(subtree)
36 |         || NodeUtil.isRelationalOperation(subtree)) {

38 |       if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(subtree.getLastChild())

49 |         Node lastNode = subtree.getLastChild().detachFromParent();
50 |

54 |       }
55 |     }
56 |     return subtree;

===== M1398 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.ProcessVars.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 210-281
Documentation:

Method code:
210 |     @Override
211 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
212 |       if (!n.isName()) {
213 |         return;
214 |       }
215 | 
216 |       String name = n.getString();
217 | 
218 |       // Ignore anonymous functions
219 |       if (name.length() == 0) {
220 |         return;
221 |       }
222 | 
223 |       // Is this local or Global?
224 |       // Bleeding functions should be treated as part of their outer
225 |       // scope, because IE has bugs in how it handles bleeding
226 |       // functions.
227 |       Scope.Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
228 |       boolean local = (var != null) && var.isLocal() &&
229 |           (!var.scope.getParent().isGlobal() ||
230 |            !var.isBleedingFunction());
231 | 
232 |       // Are we renaming global variables?
233 |       if (!local && localRenamingOnly) {
234 |         reservedNames.add(name);
235 |         return;
236 |       }
237 | 
238 |       // Are we renaming function expression names?
239 |       if (preserveFunctionExpressionNames && var != null
240 |           && NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(var.getParentNode())) {
241 |         reservedNames.add(name);
242 |         return;
243 |       }
244 | 
245 |       // Check if we can rename this.
246 |       if (!okToRenameVar(name, local)) {
247 |         if (local) {
248 |           // Blindly de-uniquify for the Prototype library for issue 103.
249 |           String newName = MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.ContextualRenameInverter
250 |               .getOrginalName(name);
251 |           if (!newName.equals(name)) {
252 |             n.setString(newName);
253 |           }
254 |         }
255 |         return;
256 |       }
257 | 
258 |       if (isExternsPass_) {
259 |         // Keep track of extern globals.
260 |         if (!local) {
261 |           externNames.add(name);
262 |         }
263 |         return;
264 |       }
265 | 
266 |       if (pseudoNameMap != null) {
267 |         recordPseudoName(n);
268 |       }
269 | 
270 |       if (local) {
271 |         // Local var: assign a new name
272 |         String tempName = LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX + getLocalVarIndex(var);
273 |         incCount(tempName);
274 |         localNameNodes.add(n);
275 |         n.setString(tempName);
276 |       } else if (var != null) { // Not an extern
277 |         // If it's global, increment global count
278 |         incCount(name);
279 |         globalNameNodes.add(n);
280 |       }
281 |     }

196 |   private void prioritizeFromEntryNode(DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry) {

336 |   protected int getChar() {
337 |     if (ungetCursor != 0) {

342 |       }

348 |       if (sourceCursor == sourceEnd) {
349 |         hitEOF = true;
350 |         if (charno == -1) {
351 |           charno = getOffset();
352 |         }
353 |         return EOF_CHAR;
354 |       }

356 |       c = sourceString.charAt(sourceCursor++);
357 |

360 |         if (lineEndChar == '\r' && c == '\n') {

362 |           continue;
363 |         }

381 |         }
382 |       }

386 |       }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.doInlinesForScope(NodeTraversal,ReferenceMap)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 194-222
Documentation:
/**
     * For all variables in this scope, see if they are only used once.
     * If it looks safe to do so, inline them.
     */
Method code:
194 |     private void doInlinesForScope(NodeTraversal t, ReferenceMap referenceMap) {
195 | 
196 |       boolean maybeModifiedArguments =
197 |           maybeEscapedOrModifiedArguments(t.getScope(), referenceMap);
198 |       for (Iterator<Var> it = t.getScope().getVars(); it.hasNext();) {
199 |         Var v = it.next();
200 | 
201 |         ReferenceCollection referenceInfo = referenceMap.getReferences(v);
202 | 
203 |         // referenceInfo will be null if we're in constants-only mode
204 |         // and the variable is not a constant.
205 |         if (referenceInfo == null || isVarInlineForbidden(v)) {
206 |           // Never try to inline exported variables or variables that
207 |           // were not collected or variables that have already been inlined.
208 |           continue;
209 |         } else if (isInlineableDeclaredConstant(v, referenceInfo)) {
210 |           Reference init = referenceInfo.getInitializingReferenceForConstants();
211 |           Node value = init.getAssignedValue();
212 |           inlineDeclaredConstant(v, value, referenceInfo.references);
213 |           staleVars.add(v);
214 |         } else if (mode == Mode.CONSTANTS_ONLY) {
215 |           // If we're in constants-only mode, don't run more aggressive
216 |           // inlining heuristics. See InlineConstantsTest.
217 |           continue;
218 |         } else {
219 |           inlineNonConstants(v, referenceInfo, maybeModifiedArguments);
220 |         }
221 |       }
222 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.isSubtype(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/JSType.java
Original range: 1221-1223
Documentation:
/**
   * Checks whether {@code this} is a subtype of {@code that}.<p>
   *
   * Subtyping rules:
   * <ul>
   * <li>(unknown) &mdash; every type is a subtype of the Unknown type.</li>
   * <li>(no) &mdash; the No type is a subtype of every type.</li>
   * <li>(no-object) &mdash; the NoObject type is a subtype of every object
   * type (i.e. subtypes of the Object type).</li>
   * <li>(ref) &mdash; a type is a subtype of itself.</li>
   * <li>(union-l) &mdash; A union type is a subtype of a type U if all the
   * union type's constituents are a subtype of U. Formally<br>
   * {@code (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>) &lt;: U} if and only
   * {@code T<sub>k</sub> &lt;: U} for all {@code k &isin; 1..n}.</li>
   * <li>(union-r) &mdash; A type U is a subtype of a union type if it is a
   * subtype of one of the union type's constituents. Formally<br>
   * {@code U &lt;: (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>)} if and only
   * if {@code U &lt;: T<sub>k</sub>} for some index {@code k}.</li>
   * <li>(objects) &mdash; an Object {@code O<sub>1</sub>} is a subtype
   * of an object {@code O<sub>2</sub>} if it has more properties
   * than {@code O<sub>2</sub>} and all common properties are
   * pairwise subtypes.</li>
   * </ul>
   *
   * @return {@code this &lt;: that}
   */
Method code:
1221 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
1222 |     return isSubtypeHelper(this, that);
1223 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.FlowSensitiveInlineVariables.enterScope(NodeTraversal)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/FlowSensitiveInlineVariables.java

Method code:
122 |   @Override
123 |   public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
124 | 
125 |     if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
126 |       return; // Don't even brother. All global variables are likely escaped.
127 |     }
128 | 
129 |     if (LiveVariablesAnalysis.MAX_VARIABLES_TO_ANALYZE <
130 |         t.getScope().getVarCount()) {
131 |       return;
132 |     }
133 | 
134 |     // Compute the forward reaching definition.
135 |     ControlFlowAnalysis cfa = new ControlFlowAnalysis(compiler, false, true);
136 |     // Process the body of the function.
137 |     Preconditions.checkState(t.getScopeRoot().isFunction());
138 |     cfa.process(null, t.getScopeRoot().getLastChild());
139 |     cfg = cfa.getCfg();
140 |     reachingDef = new MustBeReachingVariableDef(cfg, t.getScope(), compiler);
141 |     reachingDef.analyze();
142 |     candidates = Lists.newLinkedList();
143 | 
144 |     // Using the forward reaching definition search to find all the inline
145 |     // candidates
146 |     new NodeTraversal(compiler, new GatherCandiates()).traverse(
147 |         t.getScopeRoot().getLastChild());
148 | 
149 |     // Compute the backward reaching use. The CFG can be reused.
150 |     reachingUses = new MaybeReachingVariableUse(cfg, t.getScope(), compiler);
151 |     reachingUses.analyze();
152 |     for (Candidate c : candidates) {
153 |       if (c.canInline(t.getScope())) {
154 |         c.inlineVariable();
155 | 
156 |         // If definition c has dependencies, then inlining it may have
157 |         // introduced new dependencies for our other inlining candidates.
158 |         //
159 |         // MustBeReachingVariableDef uses this dependency graph in its
160 |         // analysis, so some of these candidates may no longer be valid.
161 |         // We keep track of when the variable dependency graph changed
162 |         // so that we can back off appropriately.
163 |         if (!c.defMetadata.depends.isEmpty()) {
164 |           inlinedNewDependencies.add(t.getScope().getVar(c.varName));
165 |         }
166 |       }
167 |     }
